findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-buttons--square ()
  "Upstream SquareButtonSample."
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-button "Button" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Button") :variant "filled")
   :bg "primary" :corner 12 :clip t))

;; 12 = the M3 square container corner; the clip removes the pill, the bg
;; fills the corners the pill leaves bare. Same composition, same three
;; attributes, as jetpacs-m3-split-button--half.
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on the README fidelity rule plus a hard geometry error the triage agent did not check.

What the triage agent got RIGHT (so this is not a dead-member/`badge ""` case): Renderer.kt:273 `val m = modifier.universal(node)` and Renderer.kt:304 `"button" -> RenderButton(node, ctx, m)` do hand the universal modifier to InputNodes.kt:93 `else -> Button(onClick, m, enabled, contentPadding = pad)`; Attributes.kt:92-109/158-161 do turn `corner` into RoundedCornerShape and apply clip(shape) + background(color, shape); resolveColorIn("primary") = scheme.primary (ColorModel.kt:55); and jetpacs-widgets.el:60-61, 192-216, 427-442 accept `:bg "primary" :corner 12 :clip t` on any node. So the sketch would compile, validate, and draw something.

Why it still fails:

1. It decorates the WRONG BOX. `m` is the Button's modifier, which lands outside Surface's minimum-touch-target expansion. Disassembling the exact dependency (companion/gradle/libs.versions.toml compose-bom 2026.02.01 → material3-android 1.4.0 in the gradle cache), the clickable Surface overload that Button uses builds `modifier .minimumInteractiveComponentSize() .surface(shape, containerColor, border, shadow) .clickable(ripple)` (SurfaceKt$Surface$2 bytecode: InteractiveComponentSizeKt.minimumInteractiveComponentSize at pc 49, then access$surface-XO-JAsU at pc 155, then ClickableKt.clickable at pc 187), and `surface-XO-JAsU` is graphicsLayer(shadow) → border → background(color, shape) → clip(shape). MinimumInteractiveModifierNode measures the child and then lays out at max(placeable, LocalMinimumInteractiveComponentSize = 48dp) centered. ButtonDefaults.MinHeight = ButtonSmallTokens.ContainerHeight = 40.0dp. So the sketch's primary/12dp rectangle is painted at the 48dp touch target, with 4dp of primary bleeding above and below the actual 40dp button. A real `ButtonDefaults.squareShape` button is 40dp tall with 12dp corners (ButtonSmallTokens.ContainerShapeSquare = ShapeKeyTokens.CornerMedium = ShapeTokens.CornerMedium = RoundedCornerShape(12.dp) — the `12` constant is right, the box it lands on is not). The recreated "square button" is 20% taller than every sibling sample and than the thing it claims to be.

2. The claimed mechanism is false. "The clip removes the pill" cannot be true: `Modifier.clip(RoundedCornerShape(12.dp))` is applied outside the Surface and is a strict superset of the pill — clipping only removes pixels, it never fills corners. The pill is still painted (BackgroundKt.background inside surface-XO-JAsU) and is merely hidden by an identically-colored rectangle underneath it. The Button's real shape is completely unchanged: the ripple/state layer comes from ClickableKt.clickable applied INSIDE `.clip(ButtonDefaults.shape)`, so the pill outline is drawn on the first tap — and every catalog sample invites a tap, since `(jetpacs-m3-demo "Button")` pops a snackbar. On the one sample whose entire subject is the shape, pressing it reveals the pill.

3. Fidelity rule (README lines 35-52). SquareButtonSample exists to demonstrate one thing: passing `shape = ButtonDefaults.squareShape` to `Button`. contract.json:295-305 gives `button` required label/on_tap and optional icon/variant/enabled only — there is no shape member, so the wire cannot ask for it. The sketch does not reshape the button; it paints a rectangle behind an unmodified pill button and relies on a color coincidence. That is precisely the README's "something vaguely similar could be drawn" case, and the README's own worked example — ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample, unsupported "even though a plain button would render" — is the animated sibling of this exact missing member.

4. The cited precedents do not carry it. jetpacs-m3-lists.el:123-128 applies :corner/:bg/:clip to a `row` node (jetpacs-m3-lists--row at jetpacs-m3-lists.el:73-99 returns a row) — a plain container with no inner Surface, no 48dp expansion and no competing shape, so that one is exact. jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66 does put it on a `button`, but its subject is the fused seam of two halves, not a claim about a Button's own `shape` parameter, and it silently inherits the same 48dp artifact — precedent for a deliberate approximation, not proof of fidelity.

The existing reason string is accurate as written; if anything it could be sharpened to say what the universal attributes can and cannot do, e.g. "The button node has no shape member (label/on_tap/icon/variant/enabled): the universal corner/bg/clip attributes decorate the button's 48dp touch-target box, not the Button's own 40dp container, so ButtonDefaults.squareShape cannot be requested from Emacs."

findings.evidence: The shared size-note is wrong on its main clause: the container-height scale IS expressible (§16.5 height/min_height, consumed at Attributes.kt:139-148 and applied to the Button's own modifier — see the Medium/Large/XLarge findings, and jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:136-141 which already uses `:height` for "the container height the bar composable owns upstream"). The clause that is true is the content-padding one, and it is the whole of THIS sample: InputNodes.kt:80 fixes `PaddingValues(horizontal = 12.dp, vertical = 8.dp)` for every variant, and universal `padding`/`pad` (Attributes.kt:120-133) lands on the modifier OUTSIDE the Button, i.e. as margin, never as content padding.

findings.subject: The ElevatedButton variant — a tonal-looking button lifted off the surface by a shadow.

missing.name: button.variant=elevated
missing.detail: Add "elevated" to contract.json enums "button.variant" and one arm to InputNodes.kt:89-94 — `"elevated" -> ElevatedButton(onClick, m, enabled, contentPadding = pad) { content() }`. That is the whole change; ElevatedButton already ships in the material3 the Companion links.

findings.evidence: contract.json:626-631 enums "button.variant" = filled|tonal|outlined|text; InputNodes.kt:89-94's when-block has no ElevatedButton arm. No composition reaches it either: `surface.elevation` is TONAL elevation only (LayoutNodes.kt:219-223 passes it to `tonalElevation`, never shadowElevation), so a surface-wrapped text button gets a colour lift and no shadow; `card` is the only shadow-casting node (LayoutNodes.kt:334 ElevatedCard) but it is hard-wired to `fillMaxWidth()` with a 16.dp inner Box and its own card shape, and clipping it to a pill (`:corner N :clip t`) would clip the shadow away.

findings.subject: The elevated variant AND the press-time shape morph together.

missing.name: button.variant=elevated
missing.detail: As for ElevatedButtonSample: a fifth variant arm dispatching to ElevatedButton.

missing.name: button.animate_shape
missing.detail: Boolean; true makes RenderButton pass `shapes = ButtonDefaults.shapes()` to the chosen constructor so the container morphs while pressed.

findings.evidence: Both halves check out: contract.json:626-631 has no elevated variant and contract.json:295 has no shape/shapes member; InputNodes.kt:89-94 neither constructs an ElevatedButton nor passes a `shapes` argument. The universal `corner` (Attributes.kt:92-109) is static, so even the composed square-button trick cannot animate on press.

findings.subject: That the tonal button's container morphs shape on press (`shapes = ButtonDefaults.shapes()`); the tonal variant itself is incidental.

missing.name: button.animate_shape
missing.detail: Boolean, default false; when true RenderButton adds `shapes = ButtonDefaults.shapes()` to whichever variant constructor it picks. This one member covers all four *WithAnimatedShape samples.

findings.evidence: contract.json:295 button optional = [icon, variant, enabled]; InputNodes.kt:92 `"tonal" -> FilledTonalButton(onClick, m, enabled, contentPadding = pad)` passes no shapes. A press-state visual has no wire carrier at all: the only shape input is the static universal `corner` (Attributes.kt:92-109), and nothing in §14/§16.5 exposes a pressed state.

findings.subject: That the outlined button's container morphs shape on press.

missing.name: button.animate_shape
missing.detail: Boolean; true -> `shapes = ButtonDefaults.shapes()` on the OutlinedButton call.

findings.evidence: contract.json:295; InputNodes.kt:91 `"outlined" -> OutlinedButton(onClick, m, enabled, contentPadding = pad)` — no shapes argument, and the border the universal `:border` attribute could draw (Attributes.kt:162-167) is a static stroke on the outer modifier, not the button's animated container.

findings.subject: That the text button's (otherwise invisible) container morphs shape on press.

missing.name: button.animate_shape
missing.detail: Boolean; true -> `shapes = ButtonDefaults.shapes()` on the TextButton call.

findings.evidence: contract.json:295; InputNodes.kt:90 `"text" -> TextButton(onClick, m, enabled, contentPadding = pad)` — no shapes argument. Static `corner`/`bg` (Attributes.kt:153-167) can paint a container but cannot animate it.

findings.subject: The smallest step of the M3 container-height scale: `Modifier.heightIn(ButtonDefaults.ExtraSmallContainerHeight)` (32dp) with the matching contentPaddingFor / iconSizeFor.

missing.name: button.size
missing.detail: Optional string enum "xsmall"|"small"|"medium"|"large"|"xlarge". RenderButton derives contentPadding = ButtonDefaults.contentPaddingFor(h), icon size = ButtonDefaults.iconSizeFor(h), spacing = iconSpacingFor(h), text style = textStyleFor(h) and Modifier.heightIn(h) from it. Without it the DOWNWARD steps of the scale are unreachable; with it, all five samples in the family become exact.

findings.evidence: The size-note's claim that "the M3 container-height scale ... cannot be expressed on the wire" is false in general — `min_height` IS upstream's `Modifier.heightIn(size)` (Attributes.kt:145-148 -> m.heightIn(min = …), on the same modifier the Button receives, Renderer.kt:273 + InputNodes.kt:93). But it fails on THIS step specifically, and only this one: a MIN cannot shrink anything, and the Companion's fixed content padding (InputNodes.kt:80, 12/8dp), fixed 18.dp icon (InputNodes.kt:83) and default label style put a ~36dp intrinsic floor under the button, against a 40dp default — so `:min_height 32` moves it by at most a few dp and the XSmall step is not demonstrated. (`:height 32` would force 32dp but squeezes content the renderer sized itself.)

findings.subject: The Medium step of the M3 container-height scale (56dp) on a button with a leading Edit icon and the label "Label".
findings.evidence: The size-note asserts the container-height scale cannot be expressed on the wire; it can, and by the exact modifier upstream uses. Attributes.kt:145-148 turns `min_height` into `Modifier.heightIn(min = 56.dp)` and Renderer.kt:273 hands that modifier to RenderButton, which passes it as the Button's own modifier (InputNodes.kt:93) — i.e. literally upstream's `Modifier.heightIn(size)`. In-repo precedent: jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:136-141 uses the same universal attribute for "the container height the bar composable owns upstream". Residual (worth naming in a comment, not a blocker): the leading icon stays 18.dp (InputNodes.kt:83) where upstream uses iconSizeFor(56dp)=24dp, and the label keeps the default style where upstream applies textStyleFor(size).
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-buttons--medium ()
  "Upstream MediumButtonWithIconSample."
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-button "Label" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Label")
                   :icon "edit" :variant "filled")
   :min_height 56))

;; Higher-fidelity variant if the icon/text scale matters more than the
;; button node itself (same composition jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar--item
;; already ships): a tappable box painted with bg/corner.
;;   (jetpacs-with-attrs
;;    (jetpacs-box
;;     (jetpacs-row (jetpacs-icon "edit" :size 24 :color "on_primary"
;;                                :content-description "Localized description")
;;                  (jetpacs-text "Label" :style "title" :color "on_primary")
;;                  :spacing 8 :align "center")
;;     :alignment "center" :on-tap (jetpacs-m3-demo "Label"))
;;    :min_height 56 :corner 28 :bg "primary" :clip t
;;    :pad (list :horizontal 24))
findings.refuted_note:
The mechanical half of the claim is correct — and irrelevant. I verified it end to end: `min_height` is in contract.json `universal_node_attributes`; `jetpacs--check-attr` accepts `:min_height 56` (jetpacs-widgets.el:199, number >= 0); I built the node in batch Emacs and it serializes to `(:t "button" :label "Label" :on_tap … :icon "edit" :variant "filled" :min_height 56)`; Renderer.kt:273 computes `m = modifier.universal(node)` and hands it to RenderButton (InputNodes.kt:75), which passes `m` as the Button's own modifier (InputNodes.kt:93); Attributes.kt:145-148 turns min_height into `Modifier.heightIn(min = 56.dp)`. Nothing here is a `badge ""`-class dead member. The button will be 56dp tall.

It still fails the README fidelity rule, on criterion 4 ("renders something superficially similar but does NOT demonstrate the sample's actual subject").

1. The sample IS the token set, not the height. Read the body (ButtonSamples.kt:177-192): after `val size = ButtonDefaults.MediumContainerHeight`, there are FOUR `…For(size)` calls — `contentPaddingFor(size)`, `iconSizeFor(size)`, `iconSpacingFor(size)`, `textStyleFor(size)` — plus the one `heightIn(size)`. The sample exists to show that a step of the expressive scale is a coordinated proportion. The claim carries 1 of 5 and concedes the other 4 as a "residual worth a comment". They are not a residual; they are four fifths of the sample's source lines.

2. All four are hardcoded in RenderButton and unreachable from the wire. InputNodes.kt:80 `val pad = PaddingValues(horizontal = 12.dp, vertical = 8.dp)`; :83 `Icon(IconMap.get(iconName), null, Modifier.size(18.dp))`; :84 `Spacer(Modifier.size(6.dp))`; :86 `Text(node.stringOr("label"), …)` with no style. Crucially, `:pad`/`:padding` cannot substitute for contentPadding: `Modifier.universal` (Attributes.kt:119-133) applies padding to `m` BEFORE `m` is handed to Button, i.e. outside the container — it inflates the touch target, it does not pad the content inside the 56dp pill. So the second clause of the existing reason string, "and its matching content padding cannot be expressed on the wire", is exactly true and the claim never addresses it. Upstream Medium is 24dp horizontal / 16dp vertical; the wire is stuck at 12/8.

3. What a user would actually see is wrong, not merely imprecise. Upstream Medium: 56dp tall, 24dp icon, 8dp gap, titleMedium (16sp) label, 24dp side padding — a substantial button. The proposed build: 56dp tall, 18dp icon, 6dp gap, labelLarge (14sp) label, 12dp side padding — a tall narrow pill with default-40dp-button content floating in the middle of it. Presented on the Example screen under the caption "MediumButtonWithIconSample", that tells the user "this is M3's Medium button" and it is not. That is precisely the false product text this pass exists to prevent; a wrong picture is worse than an honest "Not supported".

4. `min_height` is a minimum constraint, not the container-height scale, and the family proves it. `jetpacs-m3-buttons--size-note` is one shared constant covering SmallButtonSample (40dp), XSmallButtonWithIconSample (32dp — ButtonSamples.kt:155-170), Medium (56dp), Large (96dp), XLarge (136dp). `heightIn(min=…)` cannot shrink a button below its intrinsic content: at 40dp it is already the Button default (no visible change at all), and at 32dp the hardcoded 8dp vertical content padding plus the 18dp icon floors the button around 34-36dp, so XSmall renders neither 32dp nor anything recognizably XSmall. An attribute that only ever grows, and only visibly for 3 of the 5 steps, is not "the container-height scale on the wire" — and flipping Medium alone would leave the catalog asserting, via the same shared constant, that the scale both can and cannot be expressed.

5. The commented "higher-fidelity variant" is worse, not better. Hand-painting a `box` with `:bg "primary" :corner 28` and a fake row is the "even when something vaguely similar could be drawn" case the README rules out by name. The navigation-bar precedent does not transfer: NavigationBar is not a node type at all (README's "Not node types" list), so composition is the only route; `button` IS a node type, and painting a fake one to route around its missing member is an admission the member is missing. It also drops the Button's state layer/ripple shape, its `enabled` semantics and its Material role — RenderBox gives only `m.clickable { … }` (LayoutNodes.kt:200), a bare indication-less click.

One correction to the size-note's wording is warranted, and it is the only thing the triage agent found: the first clause "the button node has no size member" should not be read as denying that height is expressible. A sharper reason would be: "The button node has no size member: the wire can set the 56dp container height (min_height) but not ButtonDefaults.contentPaddingFor/iconSizeFor/iconSpacingFor/textStyleFor, which are what a step of the M3 container-height scale consists of." Same verdict, better sentence.

findings.subject: The Large step of the M3 container-height scale (96dp) on a button with a leading Edit icon and the label "Label".
findings.evidence: Same as Medium: `min_height` is §16.5, is consumed (Attributes.kt:145-148), and reaches the Button's modifier unchanged (Renderer.kt:273 -> InputNodes.kt:93), which is exactly upstream's `Modifier.heightIn(size)`. 96dp against a 40dp default is unmistakable on device. Residual: the 18.dp icon (InputNodes.kt:83) vs iconSizeFor(96dp)=32dp and the fixed label style vs textStyleFor(size) — the wire's `text` node does carry a "headline" style (ContentNodes.kt:121-128 -> headlineSmall) if the box composition is preferred.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-buttons--large ()
  "Upstream LargeButtonWithIconSample."
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-button "Label" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Label")
                   :icon "edit" :variant "filled")
   :min_height 96))

;; Full-fidelity alternative (icon size + text style + corner all carried):
;;   (jetpacs-with-attrs
;;    (jetpacs-box
;;     (jetpacs-row (jetpacs-icon "edit" :size 32 :color "on_primary"
;;                                :content-description "Localized description")
;;                  (jetpacs-text "Label" :style "headline" :color "on_primary")
;;                  :spacing 12 :align "center")
;;     :alignment "center" :on-tap (jetpacs-m3-demo "Label"))
;;    :min_height 96 :corner 48 :bg "primary" :clip t
;;    :pad (list :horizontal 48))
findings.refuted_note:
The claim is mechanically half-right and fidelity-wrong, and it fails the README rule.

WHAT I CONCEDE. `min_height` is a real universal attribute (contract.json `universal_node_attributes`; jetpacs-widgets.el:60 in `jetpacs-universal-attributes`, validated at :199-200 as a >=0 number), it is consumed (Attributes.kt:145-148 -> `heightIn`), and Renderer.kt:273 builds `m = modifier.universal(node)` before Renderer.kt:304 dispatches `"button" -> RenderButton(node, ctx, m)`, where InputNodes.kt:93 passes `m` as Compose `Button`'s positional `modifier`. So `heightIn(min=96.dp)` really does land in the same place upstream's `Modifier.heightIn(size)` lands. No renderer trap on that member.

WHY IT STILL FAILS.

1. The sample's subject is a TOKEN SET, and 4 of its 5 tokens are hardcoded literals in the renderer. Upstream `LargeButtonWithIconSample` (ButtonSamples.kt:198-213) is `size = ButtonDefaults.LargeContainerHeight` fanned out into five coordinated calls: `heightIn(size)`, `contentPaddingFor(size)`, `Icon(Modifier.size(iconSizeFor(size)))`, `Spacer(Modifier.size(iconSpacingFor(size)))`, `Text("Label", style = textStyleFor(size))`. In RenderButton the last four are frozen constants with no wire member reaching them:
   - InputNodes.kt:80  `val pad = PaddingValues(horizontal = 12.dp, vertical = 8.dp)` (upstream Large: 48dp horizontal). Note the universal `padding`/`pad` cannot substitute — it rides `m`, which is the Button's OUTER modifier, so it becomes margin around the button, never contentPadding inside it.
   - InputNodes.kt:83  `Icon(IconMap.get(iconName), null, Modifier.size(18.dp))` (upstream Large: 32dp).
   - InputNodes.kt:84  `Spacer(Modifier.size(6.dp))` (upstream Large: 12dp).
   - InputNodes.kt:86  `Text(node.stringOr("label"), ...)` with no `style` argument, i.e. Button's labelLarge (upstream Large: headlineSmall).
   contract.json `node_schema.button` is exactly `{required: [label, on_tap], optional: [icon, variant, enabled]}` — there is no member that could reach any of them. The triage agent listed two of these as "residual"; they are not residual, they are four fifths of the subject.

2. The result is not merely less detailed, it is visually the OPPOSITE of the sample. With contentPadding stuck at 12dp horizontal and the label at labelLarge, the button's intrinsic width is roughly icon 18 + spacer 6 + "Label" (~40) + 24 padding ~= 88dp, against Material3's `defaultMinSize(MinWidth = 58.dp)`. The Companion theme installs no custom `Shapes` (no `Shapes(` / `shapes =` anywhere under companion/app/src/main/kotlin), so `ButtonDefaults.shape` stays the full 50% pill. An ~88dp x 96dp full-corner pill is a near-circular blob. Upstream's Large button is a wide lozenge (~230dp x 96dp, 48dp padding, headlineSmall label). Rendering the blob under the name "LargeButtonWithIconSample" teaches the user something false about M3. That is squarely the README's `ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample` precedent — "even when something vaguely similar could be drawn."

3. The "full-fidelity alternative" is worse, not better: it abandons the `button` node. Every constructor in it is legal (I checked: box `:on-tap` -> LayoutNodes.kt:200 `m.clickable`; icon `:size` -> ContentNodes.kt:247-256 `Modifier.size`; text `"headline"` -> ContentNodes.kt:121 `headlineSmall`; `:pad (list :horizontal 48)` passes jetpacs--pad-keys at widgets:190/206; `:corner 48` and `:clip t` are real per Attributes.kt:92-108/158; `:spacing 12` survives because no `:arrange` is present). But `Modifier.clickable` on a Box carries no `Role.Button` semantics, no `enabled`, and none of M3's button state layer/ripple coloring — it is a painted rectangle, not a Button. And it hardcodes 48dp corner and 48dp padding as literals, which is precisely the derivation the size token exists to perform. A sample whose subject is "Button supports the Large container height" cannot be demonstrated by a node tree containing no button.

4. House consistency confirms the reading. The identical M3 container-height scale is marked unsupported with the same reasoning in five sibling modules: jetpacs-m3-extended-fab.el:45, jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:88, jetpacs-m3-togglebuttons.el:50, jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons.el:52, jetpacs-m3-floating-action-buttons.el:45. `min_height` is equally available to all of them. If it settled the question here it would unmark ~20 examples across the catalog; the note plainly means the coordinated token set, not the raw dp.

The existing `jetpacs-m3-buttons--size-note` is accurate as written ("no size member ... and its matching content padding"). If anything it could be tightened to pre-empt this exact re-triage, e.g. naming that `min_height` can stretch the box but cannot reach `contentPaddingFor`/`iconSizeFor`/`textStyleFor`. The `:unsupported` marking itself is correct and should stand.

findings.subject: The XLarge step of the M3 container-height scale (136dp) on a button with a leading Edit icon and the label "Label".
findings.evidence: Same mechanism, largest delta: Attributes.kt:145-148 (`min_height` -> heightIn(min)) on the modifier RenderButton passes to Button (Renderer.kt:273, InputNodes.kt:93). The size-note's "cannot be expressed on the wire" is contradicted inside the catalog itself by jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:136-141 and jetpacs-m3-card.el:64-68, both of which carry an upstream container height on the universal height attribute. Residual: fixed 18.dp icon and default label style inside a 136dp container (use the box composition when that matters).
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-buttons--xlarge ()
  "Upstream XLargeButtonWithIconSample."
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-button "Label" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Label")
                   :icon "edit" :variant "filled")
   :min_height 136))

;; Full-fidelity alternative: icon :size 40, text :style "headline",
;; :corner 68 :bg "primary" :clip t :pad (list :horizontal 64) on a
;; box with :on-tap, exactly as jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar--item builds
;; its indicator.
findings.refuted_note: The mechanism half of the claim checks out — min_height is a universal attribute (contract.json), jetpacs-with-attrs validates it (jetpacs-widgets.el:199-200), Renderer.kt:272 builds `modifier.universal(node)` before RenderButton, and Attributes.kt:143-146 turns it into heightIn(min), the same modifier upstream uses. But the fidelity half fails. XLargeButtonWithIconSample (ButtonSamples.kt:219-234) is a bundle of four coordinated ButtonDefaults size tokens: heightIn(ExtraLargeContainerHeight), contentPaddingFor(size), iconSizeFor(size) on the Edit icon, and textStyleFor(size) on the label. Three of the four are hardcoded in the renderer and absent from the schema, so the sketch renders a 136dp-tall, ~110dp-wide filled oval holding an 18dp icon and a labelLarge "Label" — a stretched ordinary button, not the XLarge size step. That is precisely the README's ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample failure mode (renders something similar, does not demonstrate the subject). The "full-fidelity alternative" box composition is also refuted: it is not a Button, it carries no height as written, and `:pad (list :horizontal 64)` with `:bg "primary"` puts the 64dp OUTSIDE the fill because universal() applies padding first and bg later (Attributes.kt:118 padding, :157 background), yielding a content-hugging primary blob ringed by transparent margin; the icon/text would also render at on_surface over primary since Modifier.background does not set content color and RenderText passes Color.Unspecified (ContentNodes.kt:176-177). Painting a button out of a box also contradicts how the module already treats SquareButtonSample and the four WithAnimatedShape samples. The cited precedents (jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:133-141, jetpacs-m3-card.el:59-67) only set the height of a row/card the author draws entirely, which says nothing about a Button's internal size tokens; and the identical note covers XSmall/Small/Medium/Large, none of which XLarge differs from. The one legitimate residue is that the current reason's phrase "the M3 container-height scale ... cannot be expressed on the wire" is imprecise (the height alone can be); the note should be re-worded to name the missing member set rather than flipped to supported.

findings.subject: An M3 AlertDialog raised over the app from a button, filling four slots: title, text, confirmButton and dismissButton, dismissible by scrim/back.
findings.evidence: The reason treats a CATALOG-HARNESS limit as a wire limit. `dialog.show` is a first-class, implemented, advertised wire message: contract.json:1147 + SPEC.md:1226 and SPEC.md:2695-2715 ("The Companion MUST display the node tree modally" until dialog.submit/dialog.dismiss concludes it); the Companion implements it (MainActivity.kt:127-163 DialogHost renders the Emacs-sent spec inside Dialog { Surface(shape = shapes.large, tonalElevation = 6.dp) { Column(padding 24.dp) } }) and advertises the capability (DeviceBridge.kt:123 supportedCapabilities includes "surfaces.dialog"); NodeSupport.kt:55-57 puts text/row/column/box/spacer/button/icon in DIALOG_NODE_TYPES and NodeSupport.kt:70 puts dialog.submit/dialog.dismiss in DIALOG_BUILTINS; the Emacs side already ships ebp-client-dialog-show (ebp.el:1985) and the two builtin constructors (jetpacs-widgets.el:568-579). So title, text and BOTH buttons with their upstream labels are all carriable. Two secondary errors in the reason: `confirm` (SPEC.md:1598, a non-empty string) does not lose the two button slots either — ConfirmHost (MainActivity.kt:99-115) draws a real AlertDialog with text + OK + Cancel, so it is only the title and the two LABELS that `confirm` drops, not "three of four slots". What is genuinely missing is only inside the catalog: jetpacs-m3-core.el:94-101 `jetpacs-m3-slot-keys` has no :dialog key and a :build returns one node, so the example needs a core-side affordance (a :dialog slot, or a core verb like m3catalog.dialog dispatched through jetpacs-flow-continue exactly as jetpacs-m3--on-open does — the dialog must be raised OUTSIDE the dispatch extent, cf. jetpacs-dialog.el:93-96).
findings.build_sketch:
;; body of the Example screen
(defun jetpacs-m3-dialogs--open ()
  (jetpacs-button "Open dialog"
                  (jetpacs-action "m3catalog.dialog"
                                  :args (list :sample "AlertDialogSample"))))

;; the spec a core verb hands to `ebp-client-dialog-show' (style "dialog");
;; every node here is in NodeSupport.DIALOG_NODE_TYPES.
(defun jetpacs-m3-dialogs--alert-spec ()
  (jetpacs-column
   (jetpacs-text "Title" :style "title")
   (jetpacs-text "Turned on by default")
   ;; NOT :arrange "end" — horizontalArrange discards :spacing in every
   ;; explicit-arrange branch (LayoutNodes.kt:99-108); push with a
   ;; weighted spacer instead.  :align_self is NOT an option either: it
   ;; is validated in elisp but read NOWHERE in the Kotlin renderer.
   (jetpacs-row (jetpacs-with-attrs (jetpacs-spacer) :weight 1)
                (jetpacs-button "Dismiss" (jetpacs-dialog-dismiss)
                                :variant "text")
                (jetpacs-button "Confirm" (jetpacs-dialog-submit)
                                :variant "text")
                :spacing 8 :fill t)
   :spacing 16))
findings.refuted_note:
The sketch's NODE mechanics do check out — I verified each one rather than assuming: `weight` on the spacer is really applied (Renderer.kt:337-348 `RenderRowChildren` wraps a weighted child in `Modifier.weight`), `spacing` survives because the sketch correctly omits `arrange` (LayoutNodes.kt:99-108), `variant "text"` reaches `TextButton` (InputNodes.kt RenderButton), and `dialog.submit`/`dialog.dismiss` on a button's `on_tap` are resolved in `RenderCtx.action` (Renderer.kt:158-192), not dropped. `dialog.show` is genuinely implemented (MainActivity DialogHost, NodeSupport.kt:55-57/70). So the claim fails on the other two criteria, not on schema/renderer/constructor grounds.

(1) FIDELITY — the wire's dialog is a BasicAlertDialog, not an M3 AlertDialog. `dialog.show` params are exactly `{dialog_id, spec, style}` (SPEC.md:2697-2703); there is no title, text, confirmButton, dismissButton or icon slot anywhere, and `style` is only dialog/sheet/sheet_full. The Companion fixes the chrome: `Dialog { Surface(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.large, tonalElevation = 6.dp) { Column(padding 24.dp) } }` (MainActivity.kt DialogHost) — that is verbatim the anatomy of upstream **BasicAlertDialogSample** (AlertDialogSamples.kt:126-131: `Surface(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.large, tonalElevation = AlertDialogDefaults.TonalElevation) { Column(padding 16.dp) }`). So what the wire can raise is the unstyled dialog window whose content the caller supplies; the sketch then hand-draws an AlertDialog lookalike inside it — a `text :style "title"` (which is `titleLarge`, ContentNodes.kt:122, not AlertDialog's headlineSmall) and a weighted-spacer row standing in for AlertDialogFlowRow. AlertDialogSample exists to demonstrate the AlertDialog component's four-slot API and its Material-managed layout; the wire cannot ask for that, exactly as `button` cannot ask for shape morphing (README fidelity rule). It would also render AlertDialogSample by the same mechanism as its sibling BasicAlertDialogSample, against "never merge an example".

(2) SCREEN/EXAMPLE MODEL — the claim concedes the operative point of the reason it is refuting. A `:build` is a nullary function returning ONE root node (`jetpacs-m3--guard` errors unless `jetpacs--root-node-p`), and `jetpacs-m3-slot-keys` (jetpacs-m3-core.el:94-101) is `(:fab :bottom-bar :drawer :floating-toolbar :on-refresh :snackbar)` — no dialog. A builder cannot make a wire request. The sketch therefore is not a recreation with the existing app: it needs a NEW core verb `m3catalog.dialog` (jetpacs-m3-core.el registers only open/example/theme/pref/pin/demo/home) plus a `jetpacs-flow-continue` continuation, which the claim itself asks for. "The existing wire CAN in fact recreate it" is false as stated.

(3) The claim's two "secondary errors" are misreadings of the authored reason. The reason does NOT say `confirm` loses the button slots — it says "of the four slots this sample fills only text survives: the title \"Title\" and the \"Confirm\" and \"Dismiss\" button labels have no member to carry them", i.e. exactly the triage's own conclusion (labels + title dropped). And the reason does not treat a harness limit as a wire limit while ignoring `dialog.show`: the shared sentence names `ebp-client-dialog-show`, and the module commentary (jetpacs-m3-dialogs.el:12-34) spells out the SPEC 18.1 request, the dialog.submit/dismiss builtins, and why a builder cannot reach them.

(4) Extra risk the claim does not price in: `dialog.show` is capability-gated on `surfaces.dialog` (ebp.el:971; every jetpacs call site gates on `jetpacs-granted-p "surfaces.dialog"` — jetpacs-dialog.el:103, jetpacs-files.el:1141, jetpacs-sections.el:696). A `:build` on this path would be the only catalog example whose sample silently does nothing on a Companion that has not granted an optional capability.

Two claims in the sketch's comments I confirmed as true and note for the record: `align_self` is indeed read nowhere in the Kotlin (only the stale comment at Attributes.kt:5-6), and the `arrange`-discards-`spacing` trap is real.

findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on four independent grounds; any one is fatal.

(1) THE SKETCH IS NOT A DIALOG — it fails the README fidelity rule. A `:build` body is rendered INLINE in the Example screen's scaffold body: `jetpacs-m3-example-screen` wraps `jetpacs-m3--example-body` in `(jetpacs-column ... :scroll t :align "center" :spacing 16 :fill t)` and hands it to `jetpacs-chrome-screen` as `:body` (/home/calebc42/pkb/projects/jetpacs/jetpacs/llm-poc-2/emacs/apps/m3-catalog/jetpacs-m3-core.el:417-426, :441-466). AlertDialogWithIconSample's subject is a MODAL AlertDialog raised over the app with its five slots — icon above title, scrim, dialog window (AlertDialogSamples.kt:77-106). A flat column of icon/title/text/two-buttons drawn in the page body is exactly the "something vaguely similar" the README rejects (README:35-52, the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample class). Nothing in the sketch demonstrates a dialog; it demonstrates a column.

(2) THE TWO BUTTONS ARE DEAD — the `badge ""` class of defect, verified in Kotlin. `dialog.submit` / `dialog.dismiss` are rebound to the dialog only when `RenderCtx.dialog != null`: `val d = dialog; if (d != null && descriptor != null && "builtin" in descriptor)` (companion/.../render/Renderer.kt:158-192). On an app surface `d` is null, so both fall through to `bridge.action` -> `CompanionEngine.executeBuiltin`, whose `when` has NO arm for them and whose own comment says: "dialog.submit/dismiss are valid only inside their dialog; the renderer routes those through DialogContext. Reaching here is an invalid context: no-op." (companion/wire/.../CompanionEngine.kt:360-394). They are also absent from `APP_BUILTINS` (render/NodeSupport.kt:65-67), so SPEC 16.2's sender gate forbids emitting them on an app surface at all. `tools/m3-check.el` would not catch it — `jetpacs-check-profile` scans node types only (jetpacs-widgets.el:1762-1785) — so this ships as two visibly enabled buttons that do nothing on tap, which in this sample is the majority of the interactive content.

(3) THE CLAIM'S OWN MECHANISM IS UNREACHABLE FROM AN EXAMPLE. `dialog.show` is an Emacs->Companion REQUEST (SPEC.md:2695 §18.1; `ebp-client-dialog-show`, emacs/ebp.el:1985). A sample builder is a nullary function that must return ONE root node (`jetpacs-m3--guard` enforces `jetpacs--root-node-p`, core.el:390-405); it cannot issue a request. `jetpacs-m3-example` accepts only `:build`/`:slots`/`:top-bar`, and `:slots` is closed over `jetpacs-m3-slot-keys` — `:dialog` signals "unknown slot" (core.el:94-101, :132-139). The triage evidence CONCEDES this ("no :dialog slot in jetpacs-m3-core.el:94-101") and the sketch is even named `--alert-icon-spec`, i.e. a dialog SurfaceSpec with nowhere to attach. A conceded impossibility is not a false blocker.

(4) NO DIALOG NODE TYPE EXISTS. contract.json `node_types` is the 39 and none is a dialog. The only declaratively-raisable modal is the SPEC 14.1 `confirm` descriptor field, "non-empty string" (SPEC.md:1598), which ConfirmHost draws with text-only content and hard-coded "OK"/"Cancel" TextButtons, no icon and no title slot (companion/.../MainActivity.kt:100-115). The module's existing reason is factually correct about that.

What the triage agent got RIGHT, and why it changes nothing: `icon` IS in `DIALOG_NODE_TYPES` (NodeSupport.kt:55-57), and `align_self` IS dead on this build (`RenderRowChildren`/`RenderColumnChildren` read only `weightOf`, Renderer.kt:337-358, contradicting the Attributes.kt:6 comment) — a real latent bug worth filing separately. Neither gives a catalog example any way to put a modal on screen. Its actual argument is a quibble over which mechanism "stands nearest" a dialog, not a demonstration that the example is buildable. At most the existing reason string could be widened to name `dialog.show` alongside `confirm`; that is a wording improvement, not a false blocker.

Minor: the sketch also drops the sample's own "Open dialog" Button (AlertDialogSamples.kt:80), and its centering trick is redundant anyway since the Example body column already sets `:align "center"` (core.el:455-456).

(1) "on the wire that is the SPEC 18.1 dialog.show request Emacs sends with its own SurfaceSpec, not a node type" — dialog.show IS the wire (contract.json:1147; SPEC.md:2695-2715; capability advertised at DeviceBridge.kt:123), and a caller-supplied content tree is exactly what it takes. (2) "nothing in the node vocabulary can put this Surface, its tonal elevation and its trailing Confirm TextButton on screen" — the Companion's DialogHost (MainActivity.kt:127-163) IS that Surface: `Surface(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.large, tonalElevation = 6.dp) { Column(...padding(24.dp)) { RenderDialogRoot(...) } }`, i.e. upstream's `Surface(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.large, tonalElevation = AlertDialogDefaults.TonalElevation)` (= 6.dp) with the Column padding already applied.    ;; :align_self is never read by the renderer, and :arrange "end" would
   ;; drop any :spacing (LayoutNodes.kt:99-108).

;; core verb answers with (ebp-client-dialog-show client "m3-basic-alert"
;; (jetpacs-m3-dialogs--basic-spec)) from inside jetpacs-flow-continue.
findings.refuted_note:
The sketch renders a lookalike, not the subject, and it does so by leaning on a member the dialog target cannot carry.

1) The sample's subject is the caller-supplied Surface, and the dialog profile refuses `surface`. BasicAlertDialog exists to demonstrate the *unstyled* dialog window: unlike `AlertDialog`, the caller must supply the container — `Surface(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.large, tonalElevation = AlertDialogDefaults.TonalElevation)` (AlertDialogSamples.kt:126-130). `shape` and `elevation` exist on exactly ONE node in the contract (`node_schema.surface` = {children | color, shape, elevation}); no other node type and no universal attribute carries tonal elevation. And `surface` is NOT in the dialog profile: NodeSupport.kt puts it in LAYOUT_NODE_TYPES (line 34-36), which is added to APP_NODE_TYPES (43-46) and never to DIALOG_NODE_TYPES (55-57) — the very lines the triage cited as proof the children are supported are the lines that prove the Surface is not. SPEC.md 18.1 (“Every node, builtin, and feature in `spec` MUST be advertised by the `dialog` surface profile”) makes an authored Surface a whole-dialog 1201; Renderer.kt:266-272 degrades an unadvertised type to a bare neutral Column, discarding shape and elevation. The Emacs-side gate agrees (`jetpacs-dialog-node-types` in jetpacs-widgets.el:1626-1637 omits `surface`). So the one thing this sample is *about* is exactly the thing the wire cannot ask for.

2) "The DialogHost IS that Surface" is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample fallacy. MainActivity.kt:136 does draw `Surface(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.large, tonalElevation = 6.dp)` — unconditionally, around EVERY dialog, at padding 24dp (upstream is 16dp). It is fixed Companion chrome the wire can neither request, vary, nor omit. Under the README fidelity rule that is the same defect as "a plain button would render": the pixels appear, but the sample's demonstrated capability is not on the wire. The proof is that the sketch's spec tree — text, spacer, row(weighted spacer, text button) — is indistinguishable from the recreation of *any* dialog content; nothing in it says "BasicAlertDialog" rather than "AlertDialog". Accept it and the two sibling examples become equally "supported", which the module's own reasons already reject as lookalikes.

3) The claimed build is not a build. `jetpacs-m3-example` (jetpacs-m3-core.el:106-140) accepts `:build` (nullary → ONE root node), `:slots` over the six `jetpacs-m3-slot-keys`, or `:top-bar`. The sketch needs a seventh slot key and a core verb calling `ebp-client-dialog-show`; `:slots (list :dialog …)` signals "unknown slot". README rule 5 also forbids a component module registering a new action. The triage concedes this ("The only gap is the catalog harness"), which is itself an admission that nothing today can author it.

(For the record, the sketch's node-level mechanics do check out — `:weight 1` is honored in a row via RenderRowChildren/weightOf (Renderer.kt:335-348), the spacer reads `:height` (Renderer.kt:298-300), and `jetpacs-dialog-submit` passes `jetpacs--check-descriptor`. That is precisely what makes it a convincing lookalike rather than a recreation.)

findings.evidence: Every literal claim in the connected-note holds, but it understates what already composes and misattributes the icon problem. (a) The connected geometry IS on the wire: `corner` takes a per-corner object on ANY node (contract.json:57-78, SPEC.md:2186) and companion/.../render/Attributes.kt:92-109 builds RoundedCornerShape(top_start, top_end, bottom_end, bottom_start) from it, painting `bg`/`border` with that shape (Attributes.kt:153-167) — jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-85 already recreates a fused SplitButton this way, and jetpacs-m3-lists.el:127 does segmentedShapes. flow_row carries the 2dp seam and 2dp run spacing (LayoutNodes.kt:166-181, spacing honored because `arrange` is left default). (b) What genuinely blocks it: no shapeable node holds checked state — only checkbox/switch/enum_list keep state Companion-side (InputNodes.kt:185-369), and enum_list hardcodes FlowRow(FilterChip) at 8dp with no icon and no per-option shape (InputNodes.kt:306-326), while `chip.selected` is authored-only (contract.json:317-327, InputNodes.kt:116-131) and `corner` under a FilterChip paints behind the chip's own pill rather than reshaping it. (c) The Outlined→Filled swap fails for a deeper reason than enum_option's members: IconMap.kt:89-105 resolves Icons.Outlined before Icons.Filled for EVERY name, and all 2075 rows of docs/lookup-tables/M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org are Outlined, so no wire string can select a filled vector.

findings.subject: The multi-select twin: the same connected, wrapping five-option group, but each option toggles independently (mutableStateListOf of five booleans) with the same Outlined→Filled icon swap per checked option.

missing.name: button.checked
missing.detail: Boolean, Companion-held per node id, as above — for multi-select each button simply owns its own state, no group node required.

missing.name: button.on_change
missing.detail: ActionDescriptor with the boolean injected as args.value after state.changed.

missing.name: button.shape_role
missing.detail: `"single"|"leading"|"middle"|"trailing"` → ButtonGroupDefaults connected shape sets, including the checked-shape morph.

missing.name: button.checked_icon
missing.detail: Icon identifier used while checked (or `icon_style: "outlined"|"filled"`), the only route to a filled vector given IconMap's Outlined-first resolution.

findings.evidence: ButtonGroupSamples.kt:212-257 differs from the single-select sample only in holding a boolean per option. Same wire analysis: connected radii compose today (Attributes.kt:92-109; jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66), flow_row carries the 2dp/2dp seams (LayoutNodes.kt:166-181), but no shapeable node holds checked state (contract.json:295-305 button = label/on_tap/icon/variant/enabled; contract.json:317-327 chip.selected is authored-only, InputNodes.kt:116-131) and the only stateful multi-select node, enum_list, draws fixed 8dp FilterChips with no icon slot and no shaping (InputNodes.kt:306-326). Icon swap blocked by IconMap.kt:89-105 (Outlined resolved before Filled for all 2075 names).

findings.subject: Demonstrates a vertical connected group: five ToggleButtons stacked with Arrangement.spacedBy(-6.dp) so their containers interlock, the first and last copying CornerSize(100) onto their outer corners to cap the stack, single-select via checked/onCheckedChange.

missing.name: button.checked
missing.detail: Boolean, Companion-held like checkbox/switch, so the vertical group's selection moves on tap without a round trip.

missing.name: button.on_change
missing.detail: ActionDescriptor dispatched with the new boolean injected as args.value after state.changed.

missing.name: column.spacing signed (or column.overlap)
missing.detail: Either allow `spacing` to be a negative dp number (relaxing SPEC §16.5's non-negative rule for this member, jetpacs-widgets.el:760 and Attributes.kt:40-41 both), or add `overlap: dp` meaning Arrangement.spacedBy(-overlap); without it the (-6).dp interlock that visually connects the five containers cannot be asked for.

missing.name: button.shape_role
missing.detail: `"single"|"leading"|"middle"|"trailing"` with a vertical reading (top cap / middle / bottom cap) so the Companion supplies connectedButtonCheckedShape's morph; the static caps themselves need nothing new — `corner` already carries them.

findings.evidence: The middle clause is flatly FALSE. `corner` is a per-corner object on any node (contract.json:57-78; SPEC.md:2186 "A Corner object MAY contain top_start, top_end, bottom_start, and bottom_end") and Attributes.kt:92-109 turns it into exactly a RoundedCornerShape with four independent radii, painted through bg/border/clip (Attributes.kt:153-167); a large radius on a ~40dp-tall node reads as CornerSize(100), which is precisely how jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66 caps its fused halves (outer 20dp, inner 4dp) and how jetpacs-m3-lists.el:127 builds segmentedShapes. So "no node takes a RoundedCornerShape whose top or bottom corners are copied to CornerSize(100)" is wrong. The other two clauses hold: no node holds ToggleButton checked state (contract.json:295-305), and negative spacing is refused on both sides — jetpacs-widgets.el:760 validates column :spacing with min 0, and Attributes.kt:40-41 safeDp discards anything < 0 before LayoutNodes.kt:117-118 uses it.

findings.subject: The default filled SplitButtonLayout: a fused action half plus a CHECKABLE trailing half whose shape morphs and whose KeyboardArrowDown rotates 180 degrees, driven by onCheckedChange.

missing.name: icon_button.checked
missing.detail: boolean, default false. Companion renders FilledIconToggleButton instead of IconButton, flips device-locally on tap, and gets the M3 expressive checked shape morph free from IconButtonDefaults.toggleableShapes — the SplitButtonDefaults.TrailingButton behaviour.

missing.name: icon_button.on_change
missing.detail: ActionDescriptor. On each flip publish state.changed with the JSON boolean FIRST, then dispatch on_change with the boolean injected as args.value — the same ordering contract RenderCheckbox already implements (InputNodes.kt:185-210).

missing.name: split_button
missing.detail: Alternative, and the only way to also get the 180-degree arrow rotation and the 2dp seam as component semantics rather than authored geometry: {leading: Node-ish {label?, icon?, on_tap}, trailing: {icon, checked, on_change}, variant, size}. Rendered as SplitButtonLayout, it would carry all 11 unsupported samples at once.

findings.evidence: contract.json:295 `button` = {label,on_tap | icon,variant,enabled}; contract.json:306 `icon_button` = {icon,on_tap | content_description,badge,enabled}. Neither carries `checked`; contract-wide only checkbox (contract.json:389) and switch have it, and only chip/month_grid have `selected`. The FUSION half of the reason is already disproven by the module's own jetpacs-m3-split-button--half (jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66) riding Attributes.kt:92-109 (per-corner RoundedCornerShape) + :154-167 (clip/bg with that shape), so `checked` is literally the ONLY thing separating this sample from SplitButtonWithUnCheckableTrailingButtonSample, which the module builds — which is exactly why this one must stay unsupported: built without `checked` the two examples would produce the same tree and merge, against the fidelity rule.

findings.subject: Anchoring a DropdownMenu to the split button's trailing half — tapping the trailing toggle opens a three-item menu (Edit / Settings / Send Feedback).
findings.evidence: The reason's premise is the very thing that makes the sample buildable. InputNodes.kt:150-180 RenderMenu draws its OWN IconButton trigger inside `Box(modifier = m)`, holds `open` in device-local state, and anchors the DropdownMenu to that box — i.e. the `menu` node IS a checkable trailing half that opens a dropdown, which is the whole subject here. `m` is the universal modifier (Renderer.kt:273), so :corner/:bg/:clip fuse it exactly as jetpacs-m3-split-button--half already fuses the icon_button half (jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66). menu.icon is a real member (contract.json:338) and keyboard_arrow_down / edit / settings / email all exist (M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org:1042, 660, 1684, 683). Only the HorizontalDivider and the "F11" trailing shortcut label are unreachable, and both are incidental menu payload, not the sample's subject.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-split-button--dropdown ()
  "Upstream SplitButtonWithDropdownMenuSample."
  (jetpacs-row
   (jetpacs-m3-split-button--half
    (jetpacs-button "My Button" (jetpacs-m3-demo "My Button")
                    :icon "edit" :variant "filled")
    t)
   ;; The menu node IS the trailing half: RenderMenu draws its own icon
   ;; trigger inside Box(modifier = m) and anchors the dropdown to it.
   (jetpacs-m3-split-button--half
    (jetpacs-menu
     (list (jetpacs-menu-item "Edit" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Edit") :icon "edit")
           (jetpacs-menu-item "Settings" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Settings")
                              :icon "settings")
           (jetpacs-menu-item "Send Feedback" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Send Feedback")
                              :icon "email"))
     :icon "keyboard_arrow_down")
    nil)
   :spacing 2 :align "center"))
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED. The claim's own evidence is accurate about the wire (menu.icon exists at contract.json node_schema.menu {required:[items], optional:[icon,enabled]}; `jetpacs-menu` at jetpacs-widgets.el:1038 accepts :icon; Renderer.kt:308 passes the universal `m` into RenderMenu, which puts it on `Box(modifier = m)` at InputNodes.kt:153, so :corner/:bg/:clip do fuse). Nothing in the sketch is schema-invalid. It still fails on the README fidelity rule, on three independent grounds.

1. The sketch is a strict superset of an example this very module already rules unsupported. Upstream SplitButtonWithDropdownMenuSample (SplitButtonSamples.kt:160-234) is FilledSplitButtonSample (same file, :66-115) verbatim — same `var checked by remember`, same `SplitButtonDefaults.TrailingButton(checked=, onCheckedChange=)`, same `animateFloatAsState` 180-degree `rotationZ` on KeyboardArrowDown — with `DropdownMenu(expanded = checked)` added. FilledSplitButtonSample is marked :unsupported on jetpacs-m3-split-button--layout-note ("no wire member holds the checked state of its trailing half: the shape morph and the 180-degree arrow rotation... are what this sample exists to show"). Everything that makes that entry unsupported is present unchanged in this one. Building it would make the module say the identical widget is unrecreatable at entry 1 and recreatable at entry 3.

2. The subject is the shared `checked`, and the menu node cannot carry it. Upstream hoists ONE state that simultaneously (a) makes the trailing half read checked, (b) morphs its shape, (c) rotates the arrow 180 degrees, and (d) sets `expanded`. RenderMenu's `open` is `var open by remember` (InputNodes.kt:151) — device-local, not even rememberSaveable, and the function makes zero ctx.state calls, so Emacs can neither read it nor set it. Its trigger is `IconButton(onClick = { open = true })`, a momentary press, not a toggle: no checked visual, no second tap to collapse, and `Icon(IconMap.get(node.stringOr("icon","more_vert")))` has no graphicsLayer/rotation, so the arrow stays pointing down while the menu is open. The claim's inference "the menu node IS a checkable trailing half" is exactly the thing the Kotlin refutes. `menu` also has no content_description member (SPEC.md:2416), so upstream's authored stateDescription "Expanded"/"Collapsed" + contentDescription "Toggle Button" are unsendable; RenderMenu hardcodes "More".

3. It would duplicate an example already built elsewhere. The sketch's item list is character-for-character `jetpacs-m3-menus--basic` (jetpacs-m3-menus.el:48-56) — Edit/Settings/Send Feedback with edit/settings/email — which is the :build for MenuSample. So the "recreation" is MenuSample wearing corner radii, with a decorative non-functional button glued to its left. And jetpacs-m3-menus.el's own exposed-note already establishes the governing precedent: "the menu node hangs its popup off its own anchor icon, and the wire has no way to anchor one to a text_input, which is the entire subject of this sample" — every ExposedDropdownMenu sample is unsupported for precisely the reason the claim tries to reuse as a virtue here. The anchor being renderer-owned is the blocker, not the enabler.

The existing reason string is substantively correct; only its trailing clause needs care (the divider and "F11" ARE tolerated loss — jetpacs-m3-menus--basic documents exactly that loss — so they should be dropped from the reason or demoted, leaving the checked/anchor argument to carry it). This is a real blocker, not a false one.

findings.subject: The tonal color variant of the split button (TonalLeadingButton + TonalTrailingButton).
findings.evidence: The reason blames the absence of a split_button node for an inability to FUSE the halves, and that is contradicted by the file it sits in: jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66 fuses two halves with the per-corner `:corner` object (Attributes.kt:92-109) plus `row :spacing 2`, and the module's own commentary (lines 28-35) says so. The only genuinely missing piece — the trailing half's `checked` — is not what this sample varies; it varies the color role, and `button :variant "tonal"` is a real member (contract.json:295, enum at contract.json:626, rendered FilledTonalButton at InputNodes.kt:92) with the trailing half tinted by the universal `bg` the --half helper already applies.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-split-button--tonal ()
  "Upstream TonalSplitButtonSample."
  (jetpacs-row
   (jetpacs-with-attrs
    (jetpacs-button "My Button" (jetpacs-m3-demo "My Button")
                    :icon "edit" :variant "tonal")
    :corner (list :top_start 20 :bottom_start 20 :top_end 4 :bottom_end 4)
    :bg "secondary_container" :clip t)
   (jetpacs-with-attrs
    (jetpacs-icon-button "keyboard_arrow_down" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Toggle Button")
                         :content-description "Toggle Button")
    :corner (list :top_end 20 :bottom_end 20 :top_start 4 :bottom_start 4)
    :bg "secondary_container" :clip t)
   :spacing 2 :align "center"))
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on the README fidelity rule (criterion 4). The sketch is mechanically valid — I checked every mechanism and none of them is the defect: `row`/`button`/`icon_button` all exist (contract.json node_schema), `button.variant` includes "tonal" (contract.json enums) and InputNodes.kt:92 really renders FilledTonalButton, per-corner `:corner` really becomes RoundedCornerShape (Attributes.kt:100-104) and the dispatcher applies `.universal(node)` to every node including button/icon_button (Renderer.kt:273,304-305), `row :spacing 2` survives because no `arrange` is set (LayoutNodes.kt:99-108, the discard trap does not fire), `resolveColor("secondary_container")` maps to scheme.secondaryContainer (ColorModel.kt:61) so the painted background and FilledTonalButton's own container are the same color, and jetpacs-widgets.el accepts every argument (`jetpacs-button` :icon/:variant at 988-998, `jetpacs-icon-button` :content-description at 1000-1009, `jetpacs-with-attrs` :corner plist against jetpacs--corner-keys at 189/202-205). It would build and it would render. It still is not the sample.

The triage agent misread both the upstream and the reason string. TonalSplitButtonSample (SplitButtonSamples.kt:236-290) is FilledSplitButtonSample (lines 63-113) with exactly two identifiers changed — `LeadingButton`→`TonalLeadingButton`, `TrailingButton`→`TonalTrailingButton`. Everything else is character-identical, including `var checked by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` (241), `checked = checked, onCheckedChange = { checked = it }` (265-266), `stateDescription = if (checked) "Expanded" else "Collapsed"` (269), and `animateFloatAsState(targetValue = if (checked) 180f else 0f)` driving `rotationZ` on the KeyboardArrowDown icon (273-283). So the assertion "the only genuinely missing piece — the trailing half's `checked` — is not what this sample varies" is false twice over: the checked trailing half is fully present in this sample, and `TonalTrailingButton` differs from a tonal icon button precisely by being *checkable* (it carries SplitButtonDefaults' checked/unchecked trailing shape set). The sketch's trailing half is a stateless IconButton (RenderIconButton, InputNodes.kt:98-114) that fires a snackbar and never enters a checked state — nothing morphs, nothing rotates. No wire member can carry it: icon_button's optional members are content_description/badge/enabled only, and the only checked/selected members anywhere in the contract belong to checkbox, switch, chip and month_grid.

The agent also misquotes the reason. It reads "there is no split_button node to fuse a TonalLeadingButton and a checkable TonalTrailingButton" as blaming fusion alone; the load-bearing word "checkable" is in the sentence, and the module commentary (lines 15-19, 33-35) states the doctrine explicitly: fusion composes, the checked trailing half does not, so the one sample with no checked state anywhere is built and the other eleven are not.

Internal-consistency kill shot: strip `:variant "tonal"` from the sketch and it becomes, literally, `jetpacs-m3-split-button--uncheckable` (lines 68-85) — which means accepting this claim also makes FilledSplitButtonSample supported, and the catalog would then ship FilledSplitButtonSample and SplitButtonWithUnCheckableTrailingButtonSample as two examples with an identical rendered tree, when upstream those two differ in exactly the thing being dropped. That is the README's own ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case: the plain thing renders, but it is not the sample.

One fair sliver in the triage: the reason string leads with the fusion clause, which reads softer than it should given the module fuses two halves thirty lines above. That is a wording fix ("no wire member holds the checked state of a trailing half, so the tonal variant can only be drawn as a static lookalike…"), not a support-status change.

findings.subject: The elevated color/emphasis variant of the split button (ElevatedLeadingButton + ElevatedTrailingButton).

missing.name: button.variant "elevated"
missing.detail: Add to contract.json:626 button.variant. Companion renders ElevatedButton in RenderButton's when-block (InputNodes.kt:89-94) — surfaceContainerLow container plus the M3 shadow. Without it there is no shadowed variant on the wire at all.

missing.name: icon_button.variant
missing.detail: string, one of filled/tonal/outlined/elevated/standard (default standard). icon_button today has no variant at all (contract.json:306), so the elevated TRAILING half has no form even once button gains `elevated`.

findings.evidence: Half true, half false. TRUE: contract.json:626 `button.variant` is exactly [filled, tonal, outlined, text] — no elevated — and there is no shadow-elevation route either: `surface.elevation` maps to tonalElevation only (LayoutNodes.kt:223), which tints without casting a shadow, and `card` (the one ElevatedCard, LayoutNodes.kt:334-345) hard-applies fillMaxWidth() so it can never be a button-sized half. FALSE: the trailing clause 'there is no split_button node to fuse the two halves into one container' is contradicted by the module's own jetpacs-m3-split-button--half at jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66.

findings.subject: The outlined variant of the split button: each half separately stroked, with the outer corners full-radius and the inner corners small across the 2dp seam.
findings.evidence: The reason invents its blocker. Upstream draws NO 'shared outline that runs around both halves and turns inward at the seam' — SplitButtonSamples.kt:357 and :376 use OutlinedLeadingButton and OutlinedTrailingButton, two independently stroked containers separated by the layout's gap. And a per-half outline IS askable: the universal `border` attribute is stroked with the node's OWN cornerShape (Attributes.kt:162-167, `m.border(width, color, shape)` where shape = cornerShape(node) from :154), so `:border (list :width 1 :color "outline")` + the per-corner `:corner` gives exactly the two shapes upstream draws. Use `:variant "text"` for the leading half so the TextButton (InputNodes.kt:90) contributes no competing pill outline of its own.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-split-button--outlined ()
  "Upstream OutlinedSplitButtonSample."
  (let ((stroke (list :width 1 :color "outline")))
    (jetpacs-row
     (jetpacs-with-attrs
      ;; "text" so the button contributes no pill outline of its own; the
      ;; per-corner border below is the OutlinedLeadingButton stroke.
      (jetpacs-button "My Button" (jetpacs-m3-demo "My Button")
                      :icon "edit" :variant "text")
      :corner (list :top_start 20 :bottom_start 20 :top_end 4 :bottom_end 4)
      :border stroke)
     (jetpacs-with-attrs
      (jetpacs-icon-button "keyboard_arrow_down" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Toggle Button")
                           :content-description "Toggle Button")
      :corner (list :top_end 20 :bottom_end 20 :top_start 4 :bottom_start 4)
      :border stroke)
     :spacing 2 :align "center")))
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on the README fidelity rule. The sketch is mechanically valid but does not demonstrate the sample's subject.

UPSTREAM: OutlinedSplitButtonSample (SplitButtonSamples.kt:352) is a CHECKABLE split button. Line 353 `var checked by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }`; :376-378 `SplitButtonDefaults.OutlinedTrailingButton(checked = checked, onCheckedChange = { checked = it }, ...)`; :381 `stateDescription = if (checked) "Expanded" else "Collapsed"`; :386-388 `animateFloatAsState(targetValue = if (checked) 180f else 0f)` driving `graphicsLayer { rotationZ = rotation }`. A grep of the whole file for `checked` shows eleven of the twelve samples carry it; SplitButtonWithUnCheckableTrailingButtonSample (:122) is the ONLY one that does not — and that is exactly the one the module already builds, using this same per-corner fused geometry (`jetpacs-m3-split-button--half`). The module's rule is coherent and consistently applied: the fusion composes, the checked state does not.

WHAT THE SKETCH ACTUALLY SHIPS: an inert `icon_button` whose on_tap pops a demo snackbar. No checked state, no shape morph, no 180-degree arrow rotation, no Expanded/Collapsed state description. That is the already-built uncheckable sample with a stroke instead of a fill — the exact `ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample` failure mode the README names ("unsupported even though a plain button would render... even when something vaguely similar could be drawn"). It would also put two near-identical entries in adjacent catalog slots.

WIRE EVIDENCE: contract.json node_schema `icon_button` = required [icon, on_tap], optional [content_description, badge, enabled] — no `checked`, no `selected`, no `on_change`. `split_button` is not among the 39 node_types. Only `checkbox`/`switch` carry `checked`, and neither is an icon toggle.

MECHANICS (the triage agent's technical claims all hold, and none rescue it): per-corner `:corner` is real — `jetpacs--corner-keys` (jetpacs-widgets.el:189) validated at :202-205, consumed by `cornerShape()` (Attributes.kt:100-104). `:border` is validated at jetpacs-widgets.el:208-212 and IS read: Attributes.kt:154 computes `val shape = cornerShape(node)` and :162-167 does `m.border(width, color, shape)`. `Modifier.universal(node)` runs at the dispatcher for every node (Renderer.kt:273) including button (:304) and icon_button (:305), so this is not a `badge ""` class bug. `jetpacs-button` accepts :icon/:variant (cl-defun at :988) and `jetpacs-icon-button` accepts :content-description (:1000). `jetpacs-row` takes :spacing/:align (:727) and the sketch passes no :arrange, so the horizontalArrange spacing trap is not hit. No scaffold nesting. The build would compile and render — it would simply render the wrong sample.

PARTIAL CONCESSION: the triage agent is right that the CURRENT reason string is loosely worded. Upstream draws no single "shared outline that runs around both halves and turns inward at the seam"; OutlinedLeadingButton and OutlinedTrailingButton are two independently stroked containers. The fix is to reword the reason to `jetpacs-m3-split-button--layout-note` (the checked-state note already used by FilledSplitButtonSample), NOT to convert it to a `:build`.

findings.subject: A split button whose LEADING half is text-only — the leading-content variation is what this sample exists to show (SplitButtonSamples.kt:413, a bare `Text("My Button")` where the sibling samples put Icon+Spacer+Text).
findings.evidence: Every clause of the shared layout-note is factually true (no split_button node; no `checked` on button/icon_button — contract.json:295, :306), but it is the WRONG note for this sample: what this one varies is the leading content, and that survives composition intact. The fused geometry is proven by the module's own jetpacs-m3-split-button--half (jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66, Attributes.kt:92-109), `button` renders label-only when `icon` is absent (InputNodes.kt:82-88 guards the Icon on `iconName.isNotEmpty()`), and the resulting tree is distinct from the already-built uncheckable sample (which carries `:icon "edit"`), so nothing merges. The residual gap is the inert trailing half — and the README's own convention covers it: `jetpacs-m3-demo` is the sanctioned stand-in for an upstream handler that only mutates local state, which `onCheckedChange = { checked = it }` is.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-split-button--with-text ()
  "Upstream SplitButtonWithTextSample: text-only LeadingButton."
  (jetpacs-row
   (jetpacs-m3-split-button--half
    (jetpacs-button "My Button" (jetpacs-m3-demo "My Button") :variant "filled")
    t)
   (jetpacs-m3-split-button--half
    (jetpacs-icon-button "keyboard_arrow_down" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Toggle Button")
                         :content-description "Toggle Button")
    nil)
   :spacing 2 :align "center"))
findings.refuted_note:
The sketch is mechanically valid — every node type and member exists in contract.json, per-corner `:corner` really does reach RoundedCornerShape (Attributes.kt:100-104) ahead of clip/bg in Modifier.universal, RenderButton genuinely renders label-only when `icon` is empty (InputNodes.kt:82-88), the elisp constructors accept every argument, and no scaffold nests. It fails on the README fidelity rule, and the claim's load-bearing evidence is factually wrong about the upstream code.

(1) The claim asserts the residual gap is "the inert trailing half" and that `onCheckedChange = { checked = it }` "only mutates local state," so `jetpacs-m3-demo` is the sanctioned stand-in. SplitButtonSamples.kt:409-446 refutes this: `checked` is not write-only, it is READ in three places inside this sample's own body — `SplitButtonDefaults.TrailingButton(checked = checked, …)` at :424-426 (the shape morph), `animateFloatAsState(targetValue = if (checked) 180f else 0f)` wired to `rotationZ` at :433-443 (the 180-degree arrow), and `stateDescription = if (checked) "Expanded" else "Collapsed"` at :429. README rule 5 licenses replacing a *tap handler* with a snackbar; it does not license deleting rendered state that three visual/semantic properties consume. That is precisely the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case the README names as canonically unsupported: a Companion-side visual the wire cannot ask for.

(2) The wire carries no member for either consumer (see corrected_missing), so the trailing half can only ever be a static pill.

(3) The "distinct tree, so nothing merges" argument is an accident rather than a principle. The module's line is principled: SplitButtonWithUnCheckableTrailingButtonSample is the ONLY upstream sample with no `checked` anywhere (:122-154, `TrailingButton(onClick = …)`), and it alone is built. Apply the claim's reasoning to FilledSplitButtonSample (:66-116) — identical to WithText except the leading icon — and its build would be byte-identical to the already-built `jetpacs-m3-split-button--uncheckable`. WithText escapes duplication only because it happens to drop `:icon "edit"`.

(4) Net effect on device: the screen labeled "SplitButtonWithTextSample" would show SplitButtonWithUnCheckableTrailingButtonSample minus its icon — a different upstream composable — with nothing indicating that this split button's trailing half toggles, which is the half the sample retains verbatim from the baseline. The existing `:unsupported` marking is correct.

findings.subject: A split button whose LEADING half is icon-only (SplitButtonSamples.kt:469-475, a lone Filled.Edit Icon in the LeadingButton with a tooltip for a11y).
findings.evidence: The reason's operative clause is flatly false. It says 'the button node requires a label, so the icon-only LeadingButton ... has no wire form of its own either' — but `icon_button` (contract.json:306, RenderIconButton at InputNodes.kt:99-114) IS an icon-only button with a content_description for exactly the a11y purpose upstream's TooltipBox serves, and the module's own --half helper (jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-66) already wraps one as the trailing half. Only `button.label` being required is true, and it is irrelevant because you never need `button` here.

(defun jetpacs-m3-split-button--with-icon ()
  "Upstream SplitButtonWithIconSample: icon-only LeadingButton."

   ;; icon_button IS the icon-only button; :content-description carries the
   ;; a11y label upstream's TooltipBox supplies.
   (jetpacs-m3-split-button--half
    (jetpacs-icon-button "edit" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Button")
                         :content-description "Button")
    t)
   (jetpacs-m3-split-button--half
    (jetpacs-icon-button "keyboard_arrow_down" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Toggle Button")
                         :content-description "Toggle Button")
    nil)
   :spacing 2 :align "center"))
findings.refuted_note:
The triage agent read the wrong upstream sample boundary. `SplitButtonWithIconSample` (SplitButtonSamples.kt:456-511) opens with `var checked by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` and its trailing half is `SplitButtonDefaults.TrailingButton(checked = checked, onCheckedChange = { checked = it }, modifier = Modifier.semantics { stateDescription = if (checked) "Expanded" else "Collapsed"; contentDescription = description })`, wrapping an Icon whose `graphicsLayer { rotationZ = rotation }` is driven by `animateFloatAsState(targetValue = if (checked) 180f else 0f)`. It is a CHECKABLE split button, not the uncheckable one.

That is precisely the subject the module already ruled out for the other eleven samples, and it is genuinely off-wire: `contract.json` node_types has 39 entries with no `split_button`; `icon_button` is `required [icon, on_tap]`, `optional [content_description, badge, enabled]` (contract.json:306-316) and `button` is `required [label, on_tap]`, `optional [icon, variant, enabled]` — neither has `checked`, `on_checked_change`, nor any rotation/shape-morph member. `RenderIconButton` (InputNodes.kt:99-114) confirms it: a plain M3 `IconButton` that reads only badge / content_description / enabled / on_tap. The proposed build's trailing half is `(jetpacs-icon-button "keyboard_arrow_down" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Toggle Button"))` — a snackbar pop, with no checked state, no "Expanded"/"Collapsed" state description and no arrow rotation. That is the README's ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample failure mode verbatim: something superficially similar renders, but the thing the sample exists to show does not.

Worse, it is an active fidelity regression, not a neutral one. The module ALREADY builds `SplitButtonWithUnCheckableTrailingButtonSample` (jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:68-85) as `--half` + `--half` with the identical `(jetpacs-icon-button "keyboard_arrow_down" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Toggle Button") :content-description "Toggle Button")` trailing half. Upstream ships that sample specifically to contrast an un-checkable trailing button against the checkable default (SplitButtonSamples.kt:122-154 vs :456-511 — the two differ ONLY in checkability). Accepting this sketch makes the two upstream samples render as the same static row, erasing the exact distinction upstream drew. It would also be internally inconsistent: the sibling `SplitButtonWithTextSample` — same shape, leading content varied, checkable trailing half — is correctly unsupported on `--layout-note`.

The agent's evidence attacks only the reason's wording, not its verdict. It is right that `icon_button` exists and is icon-only, so the clause "the button node requires a label, so the icon-only LeadingButton has no wire form of its own" is a bad inference (though `button.required = [label, on_tap]` is itself true). But the same reason string already names "no split_button node" and "the checkable trailing half," both of which are true and decisive. The correct remediation is to reword the reason to `jetpacs-m3-split-button--layout-note` (which the module uses for FilledSplitButtonSample and SplitButtonWithTextSample), not to flip `:unsupported` to `:build`.

Secondary note, not load-bearing: the sketch's leading half is `jetpacs-icon-button` under `--half`'s `:bg "primary"`, but `IconButtonDefaults.iconButtonColors()` leaves contentColor at `LocalContentColor`, so the icon tint is not tied to the authored `:bg` — the filled LeadingButton's on-primary content would not be reproduced. The corner/clip/bg mechanics themselves are fine (Attributes.kt:153-159, corner → clip → bg in SPEC order), so the sketch would serialize and render; it just renders the wrong thing.

findings.subject: SearchBarState itself: a collapsed bar placeholdered "Search..." that, on tap, animates into a FULL-SCREEN results surface over ten "Suggestion N" rows, its leading icon swapping Search -> ArrowBack as it goes (SearchBarSamples.kt:78-129).

missing.name: search_bar
missing.detail: {id, value?, hint?, leading_icon?, trailing_icon?, on_query_change?, on_search?, presentation?, children} where `children` are the result rows shown only while expanded. Companion holds SearchBarValue Collapsed/Expanded device-locally (like collapsible's `expanded`), renders SearchBarDefaults.InputField collapsed and ExpandedFullScreenSearchBar / ExpandedDockedSearchBar when open, and swaps the leading icon to a back affordance while expanded.

missing.name: search_bar expansion + query
missing.detail: Publish state.changed for the query string on the id (the text_input contract, Renderer.kt:414-423) so Emacs can push filtered `children` back as suggestions; the expansion itself stays device-local, no round trip.

findings.evidence: Verified in the renderer: `text_input` really is a plain OutlinedTextField (Renderer.kt:410) and contract.json:347 gives it {id | value,hint,label,on_change,on_submit,single_line,min_lines,max_lines,monospace,syntax,password,keyboard,autofocus,clear_on_submit,enabled} — no leading/trailing icon slot, no expanded state, no results children. The nearest device-local expand-on-tap node, `collapsible` (LayoutNodes.kt:358-391), is not a substitute: it prepends its OWN keyboard_arrow_down chevron at the START of the header where the Search icon belongs, expands INLINE (Column, pushing content down) rather than over the screen, and its header row's clickable would fight a text_input placed inside it. M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:177 confirms SearchBar is Available-not-Wrapped.

findings.evidence: Both clauses hold. The `top_bar` slot genuinely takes any node (Renderer.kt:676-699 renders it in a Row), so the Menu/Account icon buttons — and in fact a `text_input` between them — would travel; what does NOT travel is the expansion the sample is named for, and contract.json:494 `scaffold` = {top_bar,body,bottom_bar,fab,floating_toolbar,drawer,snackbar,snackbar_action,on_refresh} with no scroll-behavior member, confirming the second gap. missing.name: search_bar
