findings.evidence: The wire fact is right but the comparison is wrong. FALSE: "All that separates this sample from the full-screen one is ExpandedDockedSearchBar" — the two InputFields also differ materially: the full-screen sample's field carries a leadingIcon that swaps Search/ArrowBack and a Mic trailing IconButton (SearchBarSamples.kt:157-193), while this one passes ONLY a placeholder (SearchBarSamples.kt:272-286). The same error is in the module commentary (jetpacs-m3-search-bars.el:33-39), whose 'recreated as top bars they would be the same row of icon buttons twice' argument does not hold on these two bodies. TRUE and load-bearing: the docked measurement is a Companion-side layout with no wire member — contract.json:347 text_input has no results slot and contract.json:494 scaffold has no scroll-behavior member — so the verdict survives the bad comparison, because both samples are named for their EXPANDED presentation and neither expansion is on the wire.

findings.subject: The RadioButton control itself: two targets in a selectableGroup, exactly one selected, tapping either moving the selection (RadioButtonSamples.kt:46-65).

missing.name: enum_list.variant
missing.detail: string enum chips|radio (default chips), the minimal addition: enum_list already carries id, {label,value} options, value, multi_select, on_change and enabled (contract.json:411), i.e. every piece of exclusive-choice state this sample needs. Under "radio" the Companion renders M3 RadioButton targets in a Modifier.selectableGroup() instead of FlowRow(FilterChip) at InputNodes.kt:306-326, keeping the identical state/dispatch path. Two options with empty labels give exactly this sample's two bare targets; keeping the flow layout for the radio arm preserves its Row orientation.

missing.name: radio_group
missing.detail: The alternative M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:171-175 already names as future work; strictly more wire surface than enum_list.variant for the same result, and it would duplicate enum_list's selection machinery.

findings.evidence: The renderer claim is verified: RenderEnumList really does draw FlowRow(FilterChip) for both the authored options and the allow_add extras (InputNodes.kt:245-343, FlowRow at :306, FilterChip at :313), so enum_list with multi_select false would answer with the Chips component. contract.json has no radio node and no `selected`/`checked` on any node that could stand in — `checked` is on checkbox (contract.json:389) and switch only. Worth flagging one overstatement: the radio GLYPH is not absent from the wire — radio_button_checked and radio_button_unchecked both resolve (M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org:1535-1536, IconMap reflective lookup at IconMap.kt:89-105), so `(jetpacs-box (jetpacs-icon "radio_button_checked" :color "primary") :on-tap D)` would DRAW two convincing radio targets. That is a lookalike, not the control — by the same logic that the wire carries a `checkbox` node rather than asking authors to draw check_box/check_box_outline_blank icons — so it does not rescue the sample.

findings.subject: The idiomatic radio GROUP: three 56dp full-width rows ("Calls"/"Missed"/"Friends") whose click is hoisted to the row via Modifier.selectable(role = Role.RadioButton) with onClick = null on the button itself, inside a selectableGroup (RadioButtonSamples.kt:70-98).

missing.name: enum_list.variant
missing.detail: string enum chips|radio (default chips). Under "radio" the Companion renders each {label,value} option as a Row(Modifier.selectable(selected, onClick, role = Role.RadioButton)) inside Modifier.selectableGroup(), replacing FlowRow(FilterChip) at InputNodes.kt:306-326 — which is this sample verbatim, including the a11y role, over enum_list's existing id/options/value/on_change state channel (contract.json:411).

missing.name: align_self / semantics role
missing.detail: Optional companion gap: no universal `role` member exists (contract.json:126-146), so even a hand-composed `box :on-tap` row can never declare Role.RadioButton. Folding the role into enum_list.variant "radio" avoids adding a general semantics channel.

findings.evidence: Both named gaps are real: no radio node (contract.json node_schema has no radio entry; `checked` exists only on checkbox/switch, `selected` only on chip/month_grid), and no semantics/role member anywhere — the universal attribute list is contract.json:126-146 {key,id,scroll_here,padding,pad,width,height,min_width,max_width,min_height,max_height,fill_fraction,aspect_ratio,weight,bg,corner,border,alpha,clip,align_self}, and the only a11y members on the wire are icon.content_description and icon_button.content_description. One nuance the phrase 'neither half is on the wire' blurs: the row-level TAP hoisting does compose — `box :on-tap` (RenderBox, LayoutNodes.kt:186-204, m.clickable) with :fill_fraction 1, :height 56 and :pad (:horizontal 16) reproduces the whole 56dp selectable row — so what is actually missing there is the RadioButton target and the Role.RadioButton semantics, not the hoisting.

findings.subject: That the Icon inside an IconButton can be tinted an arbitrary color (tint = Color.Red); everything else is IconButtonSample verbatim.
findings.evidence: ContentNodes.kt:244-262 — RenderIcon resolves the `icon` node's own `color` member into Icon(tint = …) (line 245), and honours `size` (247/255) and `content_description` (251); ColorModel.kt:47 + 15-29 — a #rrggbb literal parses, so Color.Red is expressible as "#FF0000"; LayoutNodes.kt:200 — RenderBox turns `on_tap` into Modifier.clickable (M3 ripple); Attributes.kt:158/139-140 — clip+width/height bound that ripple to a 40dp circle; contract.json:101-111 — icon.color is a real member. The reason's premise (icon_button has no tint member) is true, but its conclusion ("cannot be requested from Emacs") is false: the tinted, tappable icon composes from icon + box.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons--tinted ()
  ;; Color.Red on the Icon; the box is the IconButton's 40dp circular tap target.
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-box
    (jetpacs-icon "lock" :size 24 :color "#FF0000"
                  :content-description "Localized description")
    :alignment "center"
    :on-tap (jetpacs-m3-demo "Localized description"))
   :width 40 :height 40 :corner 20 :clip t))
findings.refuted_note:
The claimant's mechanical evidence is all correct — I verified every citation and even built the sketch: `icon.color` exists in contract.json, `RenderIcon` (ContentNodes.kt:243-261) really does resolve it into `Icon(tint = …)`, `parseHexColor` (ColorModel.kt:15-28) accepts `#FF0000` and `resolveColorIn` returns it at line 47 before any role lookup, `Modifier.universal` applies `clip(cornerShape)` at Attributes.kt:158 BEFORE `RenderBox` appends `m.clickable{}` at LayoutNodes.kt:200 so the ripple is genuinely circular, and the elisp accepts it (canonical JSON: {"alignment":"center","children":[{"color":"#FF0000","content_description":"Localized description","name":"lock","size":24,"t":"icon"}],"clip":true,"corner":20,"height":40,"on_tap":{"action":"m3catalog.demo",…},"t":"box","width":40}). It is refuted on the fidelity rule instead, on three independent grounds.

(1) IT IS NOT AN ICON BUTTON, and the claim's own framing ("everything else is IconButtonSample verbatim") is false — IconButtonSample is `:build #'jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons--standard`, which emits an `icon_button` node; this emits a `box`. `RenderIconButton` delegates to M3 `IconButton`, which supplies `minimumInteractiveComponentSize()` (48dp touch target) and `role = Role.Button`. `RenderBox` uses the ONE-ARGUMENT `clickable` overload — `role = null` — and the Companion contains no `Role.` and no `minimumInteractive` anywhere (grep over companion/render: only `semantics { contentDescription }` on canvas/chart). So the sketch ships a 40dp tap target that TalkBack announces as a generic clickable container, placed on the Icon buttons component page one screen away from a real icon_button. The user comparing the two would conclude the wire can tint icon buttons. That is exactly the false product text this pass exists to prevent.

(2) THE RULE PROVES FAR TOO MUCH. The same box/surface composition mechanically "recreates" 7 of this module's 11 unsupported examples, not one: FilledIconButtonSample and FilledTonalIconButtonSample via `jetpacs-surface :shape "circle" :color "primary"` inside a tapped box; OutlinedIconButtonSample via `:border`; and all three expressive samples (XSmallNarrowSquare / MediumRoundWide / LargeRoundUniformOutlined) via `:width/:height/:corner` — which is verbatim what `jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons--size-note` declares unavailable. Only the four toggle samples survive, and only because `checked` has no analogue at all. A triage rule that dissolves two-thirds of a component's authored gaps is not applying the README fidelity rule ("even when something vaguely similar could be drawn"), it is replacing it.

(3) THE CATALOG'S OWN PRECEDENT CUTS THE OTHER WAY. Composition is licensed where the component is UNWRAPPED — navigation-bar items, ListItem-as-clickable-box (lists.el:181-190) — which is the README's "unless the sample's point survives composition from wrapped nodes" clause, scoped to unwrapped components. Where a wrapped node exists but lacks the member, the catalog refuses the near-substitute: radio-buttons.el:19-23 rejects `enum_list` because it "would substitute the Chips component — which the catalog already lists — for the very control this component is about." `icon_button` IS wrapped, and the tint is a property of that wrapped node. The nearest structural precedent the claimant could cite, jetpacs-m3-badge--item (badge.el:35-58), is not parallel: there the sample's SUBJECT (the bare attention dot) is carried by a real `badge` node and the box only supplies a tap the unwrapped NavigationBarItem never had. Here the subject is a property OF the wrapped IconButton, and the box replaces the IconButton itself.

The existing reason's premise is verifiably true and its verdict is right. Its only defect is the final clause reading as an absolute claim about the wire; it should be sharpened to say the tint cannot be requested ON AN ICON BUTTON — e.g. "The icon_button node draws its own Icon and has no tint or color member: RenderIconButton hands the glyph to M3 IconButton with no tint, so Icon(tint = Color.Red), the one thing this sample adds to IconButtonSample, cannot be asked for on an icon button." That is a wording fix, not a status change.

findings.subject: That an icon button can carry M3's FILLED container — a primary-colored circle behind an onPrimary lock icon.
findings.evidence: Attributes.kt:116-169 applies the §16.5 universals to EVERY node (Renderer.kt:273): width/height (139-140), corner (92-109/155), clip (158), bg (159-161), border (162-167); LayoutNodes.kt:200 gives the box a clickable+ripple; ContentNodes.kt:245 tints the icon. SPEC.md:2178-2188 lists width/height/bg/corner/border as universal. The container is therefore fully askable; the reason's clause "the filled … container this sample exists to show cannot be asked for from Emacs" is false (the first clause, that icon_button has no variant member — InputNodes.kt:99-114 always calls the plain IconButton — is true). Token values transcribed from SmallIconButtonTokens.kt:24 (40dp) and FilledIconButtonTokens.kt:22 (Primary/OnPrimary), exactly as jetpacs-m3-lists--segment-corner already transcribes ListItemDefaults.segmentedShapes.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons--filled ()
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-box
    (jetpacs-icon "lock" :size 24 :color "on_primary"
                  :content-description "Localized description")
    :alignment "center"
    :on-tap (jetpacs-m3-demo "Localized description"))
   :width 40 :height 40 :corner 20 :bg "primary" :clip t))
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on the fidelity clause. Every mechanical claim in the evidence is TRUE — and the sketch still does not demonstrate the sample's subject.

WHAT I CONFIRMED IN FAVOUR OF THE CLAIM (so this is not a machinery dispute): Renderer.kt:273 applies `modifier.universal(node)` to every advertised node; Attributes.kt:116-169 really consumes width/height (139-140), corner (92-109 -> 154), clip (158), bg (159-161), border (162-167) in corner->clip->bg->border order, so a 40x40 `:corner 20 :bg "primary" :clip t` box IS a filled primary circle. LayoutNodes.kt:200 really gives the box `m.clickable{ctx.action(onTap)}`. ContentNodes.kt:244-245 really tints the icon from `color`. contract.json has box{children | alignment,on_tap} and icon{name | size,color,badge,content_description}; universal_node_attributes carries width/height/bg/corner/clip. jetpacs-widgets.el:789 `jetpacs-box` accepts :alignment/:on-tap, :633 `jetpacs-icon` accepts :size/:color/:content-description, :427 `jetpacs-with-attrs` + :192 `jetpacs--check-attr` accept :corner as a number and :clip as t. `(jetpacs-m3-demo …)` is a real descriptor (jetpacs-m3-core.el:208). The sketch compiles and it renders. That is not the question.

WHY IT FAILS ANYWAY — the sketch contains no `icon_button` node at all. It is a `box` and an `icon`. FilledIconButtonSample's single delta from IconButtonSample (which is already :build, jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons.el:55) is `FilledIconButton` in place of `IconButton` — the sample exists to show the filled *variant of the icon button component*. Confirmed absent: SPEC.md:2413 lists icon_button as `icon, on_tap | content_description, badge, enabled`; contract.json agrees; InputNodes.kt:99-114 unconditionally calls the plain `IconButton`. So the example screen for FilledIconButtonSample would show a hand-drawn circle in which the component being catalogued never appears. This is ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample verbatim: "unsupported even though a plain button would render." The README's own supported/unsupported pair states the discriminator explicitly — FilledTonalButtonSample is supported *because* `button` has `:variant "tonal"`; icon_button has no such member, so it is the other side of that exact pair.

THE REASON STRING WAS MISREAD. "The icon_button node has no variant member: it always renders the standard M3 IconButton, so the filled, tonal or outlined container this sample exists to show cannot be asked for" — the subject of "the container" is the icon button's container, governed by the clause before it. The reason never claims no colored circle can be drawn anywhere. The triage agent detached the clause and refuted a sentence the module does not assert. (Note the reason also does NOT invoke the false "no node has a shape member" argument the brief warns about.)

CONSISTENCY — accepting this forces three modules to be rewritten and collapses this one. jetpacs-m3-card.el:38 ("The card node has no variant… the filled Card container this sample exists to contrast with the elevated one cannot be asked for") and jetpacs-m3-text-fields.el:44 ("text_input has no variant member… the filled TextField container") are the same sentence about the same defect, and a box with :bg/:corner/:border "recreates" them just as well. Within icon-buttons itself the same move unblocks TintedIconButtonSample (box + `jetpacs-icon :color`), OutlinedIconButtonSample (:border), and all three expressive size samples (:width/:height/:corner) — a twelve-example module in which the icon_button node appears exactly zero times. That is the outcome the fidelity rule exists to prevent.

THE CITED PRECEDENT IS DIS-ANALOGOUS. `jetpacs-m3-lists--segment-corner` (jetpacs-m3-lists.el:114-128) recreates ListItem, which the README names under "Not node types" and for which it explicitly permits composition from wrapped nodes. The catalog's hand-built-pill idiom appears only there: navigation-bar item (jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:104-115) and navigation-drawer item (jetpacs-m3-navigation-drawer.el:68-84), both unwrapped. IconButton IS wrapped — it is a node — so the composition escape hatch does not apply to it. Separately, the token citations are unverifiable: `find`/`grep` over the whole upstream repo returns no `SmallIconButtonTokens.kt`, no `FilledIconButtonTokens.kt`, no `*Tokens*` file at all, whereas `segmentedShapes` does appear (ListSamples.kt). The 40dp / Primary / OnPrimary numbers are recalled, not transcribed.

SECONDARY (not load-bearing): SPEC 16.4 requires a render to preserve "declared semantic structure … and accessibility meaning." `Box.clickable` carries no button role and no `enabled` member, and IconButton's 48dp minimum interactive target is lost at a 40dp box; the content_description sits on a non-interactive icon.

The blocker is real. Nothing in the sketch is illegal — it is simply a different picture wearing the sample's name.

findings.evidence: Same machinery as FilledIconButtonSample: Attributes.kt:159-161 (bg, filled with the node's corner shape), 92-109 (corner), 158 (clip), 139-140 (width/height); LayoutNodes.kt:200 (box on_tap → clickable); ContentNodes.kt:245 (icon tint); ColorModel.kt:61-62 resolves secondary_container/on_secondary_container. FilledTonalIconButtonTokens.kt:22 fixes the roles. The reason's shared --variant-note conclusion is false for this sample.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons--filled-tonal ()

findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on the fidelity rule, on button semantics, and on the cited upstream tokens (the elisp/schema/renderer path is admittedly fine — the sketch would build and draw).

1) It does not demonstrate the subject; it abandons the node the subject is about. The triage agent's own subject line is "that an ICON BUTTON can carry M3's OUTLINED container." contract.json node_schema gives icon_button {required: icon, on_tap; optional: content_description, badge, enabled} — no variant — and RenderIconButton (InputNodes.kt:96-113) unconditionally calls plain M3 `IconButton(...)`, with no `when (variant)` arm, unlike RenderButton 30 lines above it (InputNodes.kt:88-93) which does branch text/outlined/tonal. The proposition the sample exists to prove is therefore exactly what the wire cannot ask for. The sketch drops icon_button entirely and hand-paints a lookalike out of a generic z-stack. That is the README's named failure mode — "even when something vaguely similar could be drawn" — the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample class.

2) The result is not a button. Upstream OutlinedIconButton (IconButton.kt:960-979) routes through SurfaceIconButton (IconButton.kt:1163-1189), which applies `Modifier.semantics { role = Role.Button }` and a `Surface(onClick=…)` that enforces `minimumInteractiveComponentSize()` (Surface.kt:225/359/494) — a 48x48dp touch target around the 40dp visual, which the KDoc calls out explicitly (IconButton.kt:998-999: "overall minimum touch target size of 48 x 48dp, to meet accessibility guidelines"). RenderBox gives only `m.clickable { ctx.action(onTap) }` (LayoutNodes.kt:200): no Role.Button, no minimum touch target, so the sketch's tap area is the bare 40dp box. This sample is explicitly an a11y demo ("Icon button should have a tooltip associated with it for a11y"), and the module commentary correctly maps that accessible name to icon_button's content_description; the sketch demotes it to a label on a decorative icon nested in an unlabeled clickable box.

3) The cited token evidence is wrong on two of its three values. The sample's default border is `IconButtonDefaults.outlinedIconButtonBorder(enabled)`, whose color is `LocalContentColor.current` (IconButtonDefaults.kt:829-838) — NOT `outline`. `OutlinedIconButtonTokens.OutlineColor` is OutlineVariant (OutlinedIconButtonTokens.kt:28, not `Outline`), and it is used only by `outlinedIconButtonVibrantBorder` (IconButtonDefaults.kt:845-855), which the sample does not call. The default content color is `outlinedIconButtonColors()` → LocalContentColor (IconButtonDefaults.kt:521-533 + defaultOutlinedIconButtonColors 564-578), NOT a fixed onSurfaceVariant. Only the 1dp width (SmallIconButtonTokens.OutlinedOutlineWidth) is right. So the sketch paints a dim `outline` ring around an `on_surface_variant` glyph where M3 paints an onSurface ring around an onSurface glyph, with no state layer and none of the IconButtonColors/disabled-alpha machinery.

4) Reductio, and no house precedent. Nothing in the sketch is specific to "outlined": `:bg "primary"` recreates FilledIconButtonSample just as well, `:bg "secondary_container"` FilledTonalIconButtonSample, and arbitrary :width/:height/:corner "recreate" the whole expressive family (XSmallNarrowSquare…, MediumRoundWide…, LargeRoundUniformOutlined…). Accepting this flips 8 of the module's 11 unsupported entries and makes the shared `--variant-note` and `--size-note` constants false at every other use site while true at one. `:border` is used in zero of the catalog's 41 modules — there is no established pattern of painting a component's container by hand.

5) The existing reason is literally true as written and the claim never contradicts it: "The icon_button node has no variant member: it always renders the standard M3 IconButton, so the filled, tonal or outlined container this sample exists to show cannot be asked for from Emacs." Verified clause by clause against contract.json and InputNodes.kt. Leave the entry `:unsupported`.

findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on the README fidelity rule (criterion 4), not on wire mechanics.

What holds up: I confirmed every mechanical leg of the claim. `box` (contract: required `children`, optional `alignment`/`on_tap`) and `icon` (optional `size`/`color`/`badge`/`content_description`) both exist; `jetpacs-box` (jetpacs-widgets.el:789) accepts `:alignment "center"` and `:on-tap`, `jetpacs-icon` (:633) accepts `:size`/`:color`/`:content-description`; `jetpacs-with-attrs` (:427) accepts `:width :height :corner :bg :clip` and `jetpacs--check-attr` (:202) takes a bare numeric `:corner`. Renderer.kt:273 applies `.universal(node)` to every dispatched type, and Attributes.kt:139-140 (width/height), 154-158 (cornerShape → clip), 159-161 (background(color, shape)) genuinely consume all of them; LayoutNodes.kt:201 wires box `on_tap`; ContentNodes.kt:255 applies icon `size`. The upstream numbers also check out against the real androidx sources (not present in the catalog repo, but at /home/calebc42/pkb/resources/android/androidx/…): XSmallIconButtonTokens.kt ContainerHeight 32dp / IconSize 20dp / Narrow 4+4 → 28dp wide, ContainerShapeSquare = CornerMedium = RoundedCornerShape(12dp) (tokens/ShapeTokens.kt:70), filled colors Primary/OnPrimary (tokens/FilledIconButtonTokens.kt:22). So the sketch would compile, validate and draw. That is exactly the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample trap the README warns about: "even when something vaguely similar could be drawn."

Why it fails anyway:

1. The sketch does not build an icon button. Upstream is `FilledIconButton`, which is `SurfaceIconButton` (IconButton.kt:1173-1189): a `Surface(onClick=…)` carrying `modifier.semantics { role = Role.Button }`, IconButtonColors with a disabled state, and — per its own KDoc at IconButton.kt:530 — "an overall minimum touch target size of 48 x 48dp, to meet accessibility guidelines". `RenderBox` gives it none of that: bare `Modifier.clickable { }` with no `Role.Button`, no colors object, no touch-target floor. On a sample whose upstream comment is literally "Icon button should have a tooltip associated with it for a11y", replacing the button with an unlabelled tappable rectangle inverts the point.

2. The sketch silently drops `Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize()`, which the sample applies explicitly and deliberately — it is there *because* the expressive extra-small container (28x32) is below the 48dp minimum. And a single box cannot restore it: in `Modifier.universal` sizing and painting are the same node (Attributes.kt:139-148 then 158-161), so `:min_width 48 :min_height 48` would enlarge the painted primary container to 48x48 too. The sketch as written ships a 28x32 tap target.

3. It doesn't demonstrate the subject, which is a *token scale on the icon-button component*: `IconButtonDefaults.extraSmallContainerSize(Narrow)` (IconButtonDefaults.kt:1074-1094), `extraSmallSquareShape` (:875), `extraSmallIconSize` (:1055). Hand-inlining 28/32/12/20 onto a layout node shows that the universals can paint a rounded rectangle — already shown elsewhere in the catalog — while the `icon_button` node is unchanged and unused. Nothing in the render proves an icon button has an expressive scale.

4. It proves too much. `bg "primary"` on a box is not narrower than "a filled icon button"; the identical trick would flip FilledIconButtonSample, FilledTonalIconButtonSample, OutlinedIconButtonSample (`:border`), MediumRoundWideIconButtonSample and LargeRoundUniformOutlinedIconButtonSample — 6 of the module's 12 entries — none of which the triage agent challenged. The module's header commentary (jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons.el:11-22) draws that line on purpose. The navigation-bar precedent (jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:104-114, a box with :width 64 :height 32 :corner 16 :bg) is licensed by a different README clause — NavigationBar is an *unwrapped* component, so composition is the only route. `icon_button` IS wrapped; the gap is a missing member on a node that exists, which is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case.

5. The quoted "false" text is a misquote by truncation. The live reason string names its subject: "icon_button has no size or shape member for extraSmallContainerSize(Narrow) with extraSmallSquareShape, and no variant member for the filled container" (jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons.el:124). Every clause is literally true against contract.json (`icon_button`: icon, on_tap, content_description, badge, enabled) and InputNodes.kt:99-114, which always calls the plain M3 `IconButton`. It never claims no node has a size member. There is no false product text in front of the user today. Note also that the sketch answers only the size half and leaves the variant half untouched — it substitutes a different node rather than supplying the member.

findings.refuted_note:
Every mechanical check the claim rests on is TRUE, and none of them establish what it needs. I confirmed: box/icon/on_tap/alignment all exist in contract.json; Attributes.kt:139-140 does read width/height, :154-158 does build cornerShape and clip with it; LayoutNodes.kt RenderBox applies `m.clickable{}` AFTER the universal modifier, so the ripple really is bounded by the clip; jetpacs-box (widgets.el:789) accepts :alignment/:on-tap and jetpacs-icon (:633) accepts :size/:content-description; jetpacs--check-attr (:193-215) accepts :width/:height/:corner/:clip. So a 72x56 stadium-clipped tappable box with a 24dp lock WILL render. It is still not this sample.

(1) FIDELITY — the sketch draws NOTHING the already-supported sibling doesn't. The standard IconButton has a transparent container, so the sketch deliberately omits :bg. What lands on the Example screen is a bare 24dp lock icon — pixel-identical to jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons--standard (IconButtonSample), which is already :build on the previous example screen and whose Icon also defaults to 24dp (RenderIconButton, InputNodes.kt:99-113, passes no size modifier; Compose's Icon default is 24.dp). The entire announced subject — "56dp-tall, Wide (72dp) container with the full-round shape" — is invisible at rest. The claim itself concedes this ("the only state-dependent visual is the pressed ripple"), which means the sample would be carried by a transient press ripple on a node that is not a button. That is the README's ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case verbatim: a press-state visual standing in for a missing member.

(2) It substitutes a box for the component. The sketch contains no icon_button node at all. The house pattern when geometry genuinely composes is the opposite — jetpacs-m3-split-button--half hangs :corner/:bg/:clip ON the real (jetpacs-button …)/(jetpacs-icon-button …) nodes, and jetpacs-m3-lists.el does the same for segmentedShapes. The only places a bare box impersonates a component (nav-bar's 64x32 indicator, nav-drawer's pill) are components M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP says Jetpacs does NOT wrap — the README's explicit escape hatch. IconButton IS wrapped, so the node-member rule governs, and icon_button's schema is required{icon,on_tap} + optional{content_description,badge,enabled}: no size, no shape. Concretely, RenderBox's clickable is the bare 1-arg overload with no Role.Button and no minimumInteractiveComponentSize, so upstream's Button a11y role and touch target are gone too.

(3) Accepting it collapses ~25 examples across 6 modules. The identical trick (hardcode the resolved dp onto a container) recreates every ContainerSize/ContainerHeight sample the catalog deliberately blocks: jetpacs-m3-buttons--size-note (XSmall–XLarge, 5 uses), togglebuttons--size-note (4), split-button--size-note (4), extended-fab--size-note (6), floating-action-buttons--size-note (3), plus the two icon-button siblings. The buttons module header states the standard outright: samples that "exist upstream to demonstrate a SHAPE … or a SIZE … have no wire member to carry the thing they demonstrate." Universal width/height/corner are node geometry, not a component's size/shape API — jetpacs-m3-tooltips.el:126 says so in as many words ("node geometry stops at the universal width and height attributes, which size the node itself"). This one example is not a false blocker; it is the standard applied correctly.

Also worth flagging: the claim's upstream citations are unverifiable here. MediumIconButtonTokens.kt, IconButtonDefaults.kt and ShapeTokens.kt do not exist in /home/calebc42/pkb/resources/android/Compose-Material-3-Expressive-Catalog (it consumes the material3 artifact, not its source), so "IconButtonDefaults.kt:1127-1146" and "ShapeTokens.kt:46" were asserted from memory, not read. The geometry they assert (72x56, CornerFull → 28dp at that height, 24dp icon) is very likely right — but it was never the disputed part.

The existing reason string in jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons.el:51-53 is accurate as written and should stay.

findings.refuted_note:
The sketch emits NO icon_button node at all — it is a `box` z-stack with a stroke drawn around a bare `icon`. The sample's subject is the expressive size/shape scale applied to the OutlinedIconButton COMPONENT (largeContainerSize(), largeRoundShape, largeIconSize). This is exactly the README's ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample class: "something vaguely similar could be drawn."

1. The blocker is renderer-true, not merely schema-true. The triage never checked whether an actual icon_button could carry the geometry. It cannot, and not because of the schema: Renderer.kt:273 puts the universal modifier on the icon_button, InputNodes.kt:99-104 hands it to M3's IconButton — and IconButtonImpl (IconButton.kt:242-256) applies `.minimumInteractiveComponentSize().size(IconButtonDefaults.smallContainerSize()).clip(standardShape).background(...)` AFTER the caller's modifier, so a wire `width`/`height`/`corner` on an icon_button is OVERRIDDEN and the node is hard-pinned to 40x40 in the standard shape. Worse, RenderIconButton builds its `Icon(...)` (InputNodes.kt:105-109) with no size modifier at all, so largeIconSize = 32dp is unreachable on that node under any attribute. There is no wire spelling of "a large round uniform outlined icon button": the only way to get the pixels is to delete the button from the tree, which is what the sketch does.

2. The claimed build's colors are wrong and one citation is fabricated. IconButtonDefaults.kt:829-838 (`outlinedIconButtonBorder`) uses `LocalContentColor.current` as the outline color, and `outlinedIconButtonColors()` (521-533) sets contentColor = LocalContentColor.current — in the real sample the ring and the glyph are the SAME ambient content color. The sketch splits them into an `outline` ring and an `on_surface_variant` glyph; neither token is on this code path (onSurfaceVariant/outlineVariant belong to the *vibrant* defaults, `outlinedIconButtonVibrantBorder`). The cited "ContentNodes.kt:245 (onSurfaceVariant tint)" does not exist — line 245 is `?: LocalContentColor.current`; onSurfaceVariant appears nowhere in RenderIcon. And the wire has no `outline_variant` role at all (contract.json theme_roles / jetpacs-theme-roles), so it cannot name the vibrant token either.

3. It contradicts the catalog's own stated principle. jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:88 refuses the container-size scale in the same terms — "no size member for the SplitButtonDefaults container-height scale (ExtraSmall through ExtraLarge) with the shapes, content padding, icon sizes and text style it selects" — even though that module DOES hand-draw fused geometry with per-corner `:corner`, `:bg` and `:clip`. In every sanctioned composition in the catalog (split-button, navigation-bar, navigation-drawer, lists) the drawing DECORATES a real node or stands in for a component with no node at all; it never SUBSTITUTES for a node that exists. No builder in any of the 42 modules uses `:border`.

4. The argument proves too much. "Both halves are composable" applies verbatim to FilledIconButtonSample (`:bg "primary"`), FilledTonalIconButtonSample (`:bg "secondary_container"`), OutlinedIconButtonSample, XSmallNarrowSquareIconButtonsSample and MediumRoundWideIconButtonSample — five further entries in the same module the triage did not flag. That is a change to the catalog's fidelity policy, not a false-blocker fix.

5. Minor supporting point: RenderBox's `Modifier.clickable` (LayoutNodes.kt:200) carries no `Role.Button` semantics, which SurfaceIconButton attaches explicitly (IconButton.kt:1175).

The existing reason string is accurate as written: icon_button (contract.json node_schema: required [icon, on_tap], optional [content_description, badge, enabled]) has no size, shape or variant member, and RenderIconButton always calls the plain M3 IconButton.

findings.subject: A drawer sheet that stands permanently open BESIDE the content — a 240dp sheet, no DrawerState, no scrim, no hamburger, content laid out next to it.
findings.evidence: Every factual claim in the reason is true — Renderer.kt:765-774 hard-codes ModalNavigationDrawer + ModalDrawerSheet(fillMaxWidth(0.75f)) for scaffold.drawer, SPEC.md:2586 lists `drawer` as a plain Node member with no variant, contract.json node_schema.scaffold has no flavor member — but the conclusion does not follow, because this sample never needed the scaffold slot. M3's PermanentNavigationDrawer IS a Row of (sheet, content) with no drawer state, and every piece is on the wire and consumed: `row` (LayoutNodes.kt:121-143), universal `width` -> Modifier.width (Attributes.kt:139-140) for the 240dp sheet, universal `weight` -> Modifier.weight for the content (Renderer.kt:337-348 RenderRowChildren), and `surface` with an omitted `shape` defaulting to RectangleShape (LayoutNodes.kt:206-219) which is exactly PermanentDrawerSheet's shape. The module already owns the item builder and asserts (its own commentary, jetpacs-m3-navigation-drawer.el:28-31) that NavigationDrawerItem composes from nodes.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-navigation-drawer--permanent ()
  "Upstream PermanentNavigationDrawerSample."
  (let ((selected (cdr (car jetpacs-m3-navigation-drawer--items))))
    (jetpacs-row
     ;; PermanentDrawerSheet(Modifier.width(240.dp)): a rectangular surface,
     ;; the 12dp spacer, then the same 18 items, the first selected.
     (jetpacs-with-attrs
      (jetpacs-surface
       (apply #'jetpacs-column
              (append
               (list (jetpacs-with-attrs (jetpacs-spacer) :height 12))
               (mapcar (lambda (cell)
                         (jetpacs-m3-navigation-drawer--item
                          (car cell) (cdr cell) (equal (cdr cell) selected)))
                       jetpacs-m3-navigation-drawer--items)
               (list :spacing 4)))
       :color "surface")
      :width 240)
     ;; content = Column(fillMaxSize, padding 16, centered) { Text("Application content") }
     (jetpacs-with-attrs
      (jetpacs-column (jetpacs-text "Application content")
                      :align "center" :fill t)
      :weight 1 :padding 16)
     :align "top" :fill t)))

Two traps this sketch deliberately avoids. (1) The sheet column must NOT carry :scroll t: the Example screen already wraps the body in a (jetpacs-column ... :scroll t) (jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457), and a verticalScroll inside a verticalScroll is measured with an infinite max height and throws, blanking the screen — the outer scroll already carries the 18 items. (2) --item hard-codes :key "navigation-drawer-<icon>", which would repeat across the modal and permanent screens; that is legal (a `key` is §16.1 presentation identity scoped to its parent, not a document-unique `id` — jetpacs--collect-node-ids only collects :id), but giving --item a KEY-PREFIX argument keeps the two sheets independently reconcilable. Nodes used: row, column, surface, spacer, box, icon, text — all 39-set, all consumed; :width/:weight/:padding/:bg/:corner/:key all §16.5 and all applied by Attributes.kt/RenderRowChildren.

findings.evidence: The reason's operative clauses are wrong. (a) "inside its container": M3 does not draw supporting text inside the container — TextFieldDefaults.DecorationBox stacks it BELOW the container box with supportingTextPadding (start/end 16, top 4), which is ordinary column layout. (b) "in its own colour and typography, cannot be put on the wire": both can. `text :style "caption"` resolves to MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall (ContentNodes.kt:121-128) — M3's supporting-text type scale exactly — and `:color "on_surface_variant"` resolves to scheme.onSurfaceVariant (ColorModel.kt:69), its exact colour role. `:pad` per-side is consumed (Attributes.kt:119-130). What survives as genuinely absent is only the a11y association between field and helper line, which is not what the sample renders. Contrast TextFieldWithErrorState, which needs the member for real because error COLOURING of the container is unaddressable.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-text-fields--supporting-text ()
  "Upstream TextFieldWithSupportingText."
  (jetpacs-column
   (jetpacs-text-input "text-fields-supporting"
                       :label "Label" :single-line t)
   (jetpacs-with-attrs
    (jetpacs-text "Supporting text that is long and perhaps goes onto another line."
                  :style "caption" :color "on_surface_variant")
    :pad (list :start 16 :end 16 :top 4))
   :fill t))
;; column -> RenderColumn (LayoutNodes.kt:146); text style/colour -> RenderText
;; (ContentNodes.kt:151-183); :pad -> Modifier.universal (Attributes.kt:119-130).
;; Renders as: outlined field, then bodySmall onSurfaceVariant prose indented
;; 16dp, 4dp below it — the same pixels M3's supportingText slot produces.
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED — but the existing reason string is also partly false and must be rewritten.

WHAT THE TRIAGE AGENT GOT RIGHT (verified, so the reason text is defective as product text):
- Every member in the sketch exists, validates and is CONSUMED. `column :fill` -> fillMaxWidth (LayoutNodes.kt:146-162); `text :style "caption"` -> MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall (ContentNodes.kt:124, applied at RenderText 152-179); `:color "on_surface_variant"` -> scheme.onSurfaceVariant (ColorModel.kt:68); `:pad (:start :end :top)` -> Modifier.padding via Modifier.universal, applied to EVERY node at the dispatcher (Attributes.kt:119-130, Renderer.kt:273-275); `text_input :label/:single-line` -> label/singleLine on the OutlinedTextField (Renderer.kt:363-437). `jetpacs-with-attrs`/`jetpacs--pad-keys` accept :start/:top/:end (jetpacs-widgets.el:190, 206). No `badge ""`-class trap. And M3 really does draw supporting text OUTSIDE the container box — TextFieldImpl.kt:363-366 says the container is passed as a composable "so that elements like supporting text can be placed outside of it". So the reason's clauses "inside its container" and "in its own colour and typography, cannot be put on the wire" are FALSE and must be fixed.

WHY THE BUILD STILL FAILS THE FIDELITY RULE (the claim of "the same pixels" is refutable from the androidx source):
1. M3 binds the helper line's WRAP WIDTH to the field's own measured width. The supporting Box is measured with `.copy(minHeight = 0, maxWidth = width)` where `width` is the field's measured width — TextFieldImpl.kt:781 (filled) and :1449 (outlined) — and placed at the field's start edge (placeRelative(0, height)). The field's width is NOT the parent's width: OutlinedTextField applies `.defaultMinSize(minWidth = OutlinedTextFieldDefaults.MinWidth …)` (OutlinedTextField.kt:199-202) with MinWidth = 280.dp (TextFieldDefaults.kt:88/1010), and calculateWidth returns `constraints.constrainWidth(wrappedWidth)` (TextFieldImpl.kt:1034-1054), i.e. content-driven from a 280dp floor, not fillMaxWidth. In the sketch the caption is a SIBLING in a `column :fill t`, so it wraps at the column's width. On a 411dp phone the Example screen body is 379dp wide (jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457 wraps every sample in `(jetpacs-column BODY :scroll t :align "center" :spacing 16 :fill t)` with `:padding 16`): the field renders ~280dp, the caption ~347dp — the helper line overhangs the field's right edge by ~67dp and breaks at different words. Upstream's string is literally "Supporting text that is long and perhaps goes onto another line" — the wrap INSIDE the field's width is the thing the sample was written to show. No wire member can bind one node's wrap width to another node's measured width; `:max_width 280` would be hard-coding a Companion-side constant that the field itself stops obeying as its content grows.
2. Alignment: upstream's Example screen is `Box(fillMaxSize, contentAlignment = Center)` (Example.kt:57-62) so the 280dp field is centred with its helper line inside it; the sketch's `:fill t` pins the field to the start edge with a near-full-width paragraph under it.
3. The slot also carries state: supporting text is decorated with `colors.supportingTextColor(enabled, isError, isFocused)` (TextFieldImpl.kt:230-234). The sketch hard-codes one static role, which is also why the module's TextFieldWithErrorState reason (which the triage agent concedes) rests on the SAME missing member — building this one and not that one would split one member across two verdicts.
4. Upstream is the FILLED `TextField` (TextFieldSamples.kt:248-257). M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:111,194-198 records that Jetpacs exposes OutlinedTextField only, which is the exact ground on which this module already marks SimpleTextFieldSample unsupported — and TextFieldWithSupportingText is SimpleTextFieldSample plus the slot.

The lists precedent does not license this: ListItem has NO node and the lookup ratifies manual composition; `text_input` IS the wrapped node whose upstream slot this sample exists to show. Per the README rule this is the "something vaguely similar could be drawn" case — the pixels are close but the demonstrated binding (helper line owned, sized and coloured by the field) is not on the wire.

ACTION: keep :unsupported, but replace the reason. Suggested: "The text_input node has no supporting_text member: M3 measures the helper line to the FIELD's own width and recolours it with the field's enabled/error state, so a text node stacked under the field wraps to the screen instead of to the field and never follows it."

The universal attribute is outer: Attributes.kt:129-133 applies `Modifier.padding(...)` to the modifier the widget is composed WITH, insetting the whole field rather than its interior. And the height half IS already askable — `min_height` reaches Modifier.heightIn(min=…) at Attributes.kt:145-148 — but alone it cannot shrink anything, because OutlinedTextField's own interior padding still measures ~56dp and heightIn only lowers the constraint floor. contract.json:347 has no content_padding. findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on two grounds: one of the four cited "consumed members" is provably dead, and the sample's actual subject (the size step) is not demonstrated — the app's own screens contradict it.

1) `:elevation 6` IS the `badge ""` trap. `RenderSurfaceNode` (LayoutNodes.kt:207-225) passes the wire's elevation as `tonalElevation` ONLY (line 223); it never passes `shadowElevation`. M3's `Surface` runs that through `surfaceColorAtElevation` → `ColorScheme.applyTonalElevation` (/home/calebc42/pkb/resources/android/androidx/compose/material3/material3/src/commonMain/kotlin/androidx/compose/material3/ColorScheme.kt:1560-1567), which returns `backgroundColor` UNCHANGED unless it `== surface`. With `:color "primary_container"` the 6 is discarded outright — no tint, no shadow, not one pixel changes. The only two `shadowElevation` uses in the entire Companion are hardcoded (Renderer.kt:712 floating_toolbar, EditorToolbar.kt:102); no node type carries a shadow member at all (contract.json node_schema: `surface` has only color/shape/elevation). So the evidence line "surface colour/elevation (LayoutNodes.kt:219-223)" is false as stated.

2) Upstream, the small FAB's elevation is not a static tint but `elevation.shadowElevation(interactionSource)` (FloatingActionButton.kt:176-177), `FabPrimaryContainerTokens.ContainerElevation = ElevationTokens.Level3` = 6dp of animated SHADOW (Level4 on hover). The sketch renders a flat colored rectangle. "Floating" is the component's premise.

3) The subject is not just undemonstrated, it is inverted. FabSmallTokens = 40x40, CornerMedium 12dp, IconSize 24 — the claim's numbers are right. But the whole point of this sample (and the module's own commentary) is that Small is a step DOWN from `FloatingActionButtonSample` (FabBaselineTokens = 56x56, CornerLarge). The catalog already renders FloatingActionButtonSample as a bare `icon_button`, and the Companion's `IconButton` is pinned to `IconButtonDefaults.smallContainerSize()` (InputNodes.kt:99-113 → IconButtonDefaults.kt:1101-1119 → SmallIconButtonTokens: IconSize 24 + 2×DefaultLeadingSpace 8 = 40 wide, ContainerHeight 40). So the proposed "small" FAB renders at exactly the same 40×40 as the app's "default" FAB — and, being filled/rounded/coloured against a transparent icon button, reads as the LARGER, more prominent of the two. The scale the sample exists to show is contradicted on screen.

4) Fidelity rule: this is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case. The subject is the `SmallFloatingActionButton` composable; the wire has no FAB node and no size on the fab slot's container, so the sketch abandons the module's own slot doctrine ("RenderScaffold hands the fab node straight to RenderNode, so the M3 FAB elevation and corner size are the Companion's business") and hand-draws a lookalike box in the slot. That is "something vaguely similar could be drawn".

What the claim gets right (so the refutation does NOT rest on syntax): every node/member exists in contract.json; `jetpacs-with-attrs` accepts numeric `:corner` (jetpacs-widgets.el:202-205) and `:width`/`:height`; `jetpacs-surface`/`jetpacs-box`/`jetpacs-icon` accept every argument used; numeric `:corner` really does beat the shape enum (LayoutNodes.kt:217-218); `box :on-tap` gives a ripple clipped by Surface's `.clip(shape)`; the icon inherits `LocalContentColor` = onPrimaryContainer (ContentNodes.kt:244-246) and defaults to 24dp; and no scaffold is nested. It fails on the dead member and on fidelity, not on validation.

findings.subject: The default FILLED M3 Card container — a flat, 12dp-rounded, filled 180x100 box reading "Card content" — as the contrast partner to ElevatedCardSample.
findings.evidence: The reason's closing clause ("the filled Card container ... cannot be asked for from Emacs", jetpacs-m3-card.el:37-39) is false. M3's filled Card IS a Surface with a container color and a 12dp shape, and the wire has that node: RenderSurfaceNode (LayoutNodes.kt:206-226) honors `color`, and takes its shape from the universal `corner` (LayoutNodes.kt:217-218 -> cornerShape, Attributes.kt:92-109), with tonalElevation defaulting to 0 — i.e. flat. Unlike ElevatedCard, the filled card needs NO shadow, so the one thing the wire genuinely cannot express (a shadow elevation; LayoutNodes.kt:223 passes elevation as tonalElevation only) is not needed here. The claims about the `card` node itself are true (contract.json:240-250; RenderCard is always ElevatedCard at LayoutNodes.kt:334) — but they do not make the SAMPLE unbuildable. Caveat to state honestly in any rewrite: M3's exact token is surfaceContainerHighest, which ColorModel.kt:54-83 does not resolve; `surface_variant` (ColorModel.kt:67) is the listed role that lands in the same place in the M3 baseline palette.
findings.build_sketch:
(jetpacs-with-attrs
 (jetpacs-surface
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-box (jetpacs-text "Card content") :alignment "center")
   :fill_fraction 1.0 :height 100)
  :color "surface_variant")
 :width 180 :height 100 :corner 12)

;; surface -> RenderSurfaceNode: color = surfaceVariant, shape = RoundedCornerShape(12.dp)
;; from the universal :corner, tonalElevation 0 => flat filled 12dp container, which is
;; precisely CardDefaults.cardColors()/CardDefaults.shape. Sizing is the universal
;; width/height (Attributes.kt:139-140); the inner box centers the label. Note the surface
;; node adds no 16dp content padding of its own (RenderCard does, LayoutNodes.kt:342), so
;; the inner box takes the full 100dp height rather than 100-2*16.
findings.refuted_note:
The sketch is mechanically legal but fails the README fidelity rule, so `:unsupported` stands.

MECHANICS (the claim's citations check out — I am not refuting on these): `surface` exists with `color` optional (contract.json node_schema.surface: required children; optional color/shape/elevation); `corner`/`width`/`height`/`fill_fraction` are universal (contract.json universal_node_attributes); RenderSurfaceNode does read `color` and does take its shape from the universal `corner` (LayoutNodes.kt:207-226 -> cornerShape, Attributes.kt:92-109); `jetpacs-with-attrs` accepts `:fill_fraction 1.0` (jetpacs-widgets.el:197, check-number 0..1). I built the sketch in `emacs -Q --batch` and it serializes clean:
{"children":[{"alignment":"center","children":[{"t":"text","text":"Card content"}],"fill_fraction":1.0,"height":100,"t":"box"}],"color":"surface_variant","corner":12,"height":100,"t":"surface","width":180}
No scaffold nesting, no dead member, no rejected argument.

WHY IT STILL FAILS — the sample's subject is the *container style*, and the color is a hand-picked lookalike, materially worse than the claim's own caveat admits:

1. No wire role reaches the filled Card's container token. `CardDefaults.cardColors().containerColor` is `surfaceContainerHighest`; contract.json `theme_roles` has no such role and ColorModel.kt:54-83 has no arm for it (it would fall through to the `scheme.onSurface` legible fallback — the inverse color). So the sample's defining attribute is genuinely unnameable.

2. `surface_variant` is NOT "the same place in the M3 baseline palette" — it is the user's Emacs theme color. jetpacs-theme.el:282 maps `:surface_variant` to Modus `bg-dim`, and ThemeModel.kt:59-100 overlays it verbatim (line 94) while re-deriving only surfaceContainerLow/Container/High from the pushed pair (lines 97-99) — `surfaceContainerHighest` is never re-derived and stays at the untouched Material baseline. So under any pushed palette (the normal Jetpacs case) the stand-in is the Emacs dim background, unrelated to the card token. Even with no theme pushed the equivalence fails in dark mode (baseline surfaceVariant #49454F vs surfaceContainerHighest #36343B).

3. It breaks the very contrast the task says the sample exists for. ElevatedCardSample is built with `jetpacs-card` -> ElevatedCard, whose container is `surfaceContainerLow` = lerp(surface, surface_variant, 0.25) (ThemeModel.kt:97). The proposed filled stand-in sits at 100% surface_variant — four tonal steps away — where upstream Card vs ElevatedCard differ by roughly one step in the same neutral ramp. Side by side on the Card screen the pair would misrepresent the filled/elevated relationship, and the sketch's card would contain no `card` node at all.

4. This is exactly the move the module and the house standard already refuse. jetpacs-m3-card.el:22-26 names it ("a `surface' node with a hand-picked color ... would put a lookalike where the sample's whole subject is the container style"), and the same reasoning is applied in 14 other modules (dialogs, chips, carousel, search-bars, split-button, button-groups, fab-menu, tooltips, adaptive, material-shapes, loading-indicators, navigation-suite-scaffold). Accepting it proves too much: OutlinedCardSample would then be "supported" by the same surface + universal `:border`, and every container-variant sample in the catalog collapses into "draw a rounded box."

The existing reason string is true as written — "the filled Card container ... cannot be asked for from Emacs" means asked for, not hand-drawn. The one thing worth tightening is that the reason should say the *container color token* has no role either, not only that the card node lacks the member.

findings.subject: The onClick overload of the FILLED Card: the same flat filled 180x100 container, tappable, reading "Clickable".
findings.evidence: "Only half of this one is on the wire" (jetpacs-m3-card.el:100-101) is false: the other half — the filled container — is a `surface` with a color and a universal `corner` (LayoutNodes.kt:206-226, Attributes.kt:92-109), and the tap is a `box.on_tap`, which RenderBox turns into `m.clickable { ctx.action(onTap) }` (LayoutNodes.kt:200) with the ripple bounded by the universal `clip` applied just before it (Attributes.kt:158). CardSamples.kt:45-52 shows the sample is Card(onClick) + Modifier.size(180,100) + a centered Text and nothing else.
findings.build_sketch:
(jetpacs-with-attrs
 (jetpacs-box
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-surface
    (jetpacs-with-attrs
     (jetpacs-box (jetpacs-text "Clickable") :alignment "center")
     :fill_fraction 1.0 :height 100)
    :color "surface_variant")
   :width 180 :height 100 :corner 12)
  :on-tap (jetpacs-m3-demo "Clickable"))
 :corner 12 :clip t)

;; The outer box carries :on-tap (RenderBox, LayoutNodes.kt:200) plus :corner/:clip so the
;; ripple is rounded to the container (Attributes.kt:158 clips before RenderBox appends
;; .clickable). Everything inside is the CardSample sketch.
findings.refuted_note:
The sketch is technically constructible — I built it under `emacs -Q --batch` and it produced `(:t "box" :children [(:t "surface" … :color "surface_variant" :width 180 :height 100 :corner 12)] :on_tap … :corner 12 :clip t)`. Every claim about the plumbing checks out: `box.on_tap` is in contract.json and RenderBox reads it (`m.clickable { ctx.action(onTap) }`, LayoutNodes.kt:200); `surface.color` is schema'd and consumed (LayoutNodes.kt:208); `clip` really does precede the clickable (Attributes.kt:158, applied at the dispatcher, Renderer.kt:273). So the claim does not fail on any wire-mechanics ground.

It fails on the fidelity rule, which is the ground that matters. The sketch contains no `card` node at all — it is a foundation `Box` wrapping a `Surface`. CardSamples.kt:45-52 is `Card(onClick = …)`: the subject is the M3 **Card** composable's clickable overload, and within this module's matrix (three container styles × plain/onClick, spelled out in jetpacs-m3-card.el:11-26) the thing that separates `ClickableCardSample` from the already-supported `ClickableElevatedCardSample` is precisely the filled container. Substituting a rounded `surfaceVariant` rectangle with a `Modifier.clickable` is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case verbatim — "something vaguely similar could be drawn," so the example stays unsupported. It also drops what `Card(onClick)` actually is on device: shadow + pressed elevation, `CardDefaults` container/content pairing, M3 card interaction semantics. `box.on_tap` is a raw foundation clickable.

Two further disqualifiers:

1. The color is not an approximation the author was free to pick — it is unaskable. The filled Card's container is `surfaceContainerHighest`; the wire cannot name that role (see corrected_missing). `surface_variant` is a *different M3 slot*, chosen only because it is the closest nameable one. The one contrast this sample exists to draw would be rendered in a color that is neither filled nor elevated.

2. Accepting the claim makes the catalog self-contradictory. `CardSample` (jetpacs-m3-card.el:91-95) differs from `ClickableCardSample` by nothing but `onClick =` (CardSamples.kt:36-40 vs 45-52), and it stays `:unsupported` with `--filled-note`, which states the filled container "cannot be asked for from Emacs." The same box+surface sketch minus `:on-tap` would recreate it, and the same reasoning plus a universal `:border` would recreate both OutlinedCard samples — all three of which the module commentary explicitly rejects at lines 21-26 ("Drawing them anyway (a `surface' node with a hand-picked color, or a universal `border' stroked over an always-elevated card) would put a lookalike where the sample's whole subject is the container style"). The triage claim changes one of four entries while its argument applies to all four, leaving the user reading that the identical 180x100 filled container is on the wire in one example and unavailable in the one directly above it.

The cited evidence — "'Only half of this one is on the wire' is false" — is itself false: the current reason is accurate as written. `card` does carry `on_tap` and does not carry the filled container style, and no other node supplies it.

findings.subject: The OUTLINED M3 Card container — a flat, unfilled, 12dp-rounded 180x100 box with a 1dp outline stroke, reading "Card content".
findings.evidence: Two independent falsehoods in jetpacs-m3-card.el:41-43. (1) "The card node has no ... border member": `border` is a §16.5 UNIVERSAL attribute legal on any node (contract.json:57-78; SPEC.md:2187) and the renderer consumes it — Attributes.kt:162-167 does `m = m.border(width, color, shape)` with shape = cornerShape(node), and Renderer.kt:273 applies `universal` to every node including `card`. This is the same class of error as the already-caught "no shape member" (surface HAS :shape) and "no per-corner shape" (:corner IS per-corner, Attributes.kt:100-104). (2) "the wire can neither drop the card's elevation nor ask for that outline": it can do both at once by using `surface` instead of `card` — RenderSurfaceNode (LayoutNodes.kt:206-226) is flat by default, and M3's OutlinedCard is literally Card -> Surface with color=surface and a 1dp border, which is exactly this node plus the universal border. `outline_variant` resolves at ColorModel.kt:76 (and plain `outline` at :75 is the contract-listed role).
findings.build_sketch:
(jetpacs-with-attrs
 (jetpacs-surface
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-box (jetpacs-text "Card content") :alignment "center")
   :fill_fraction 1.0 :height 100)
  :color "surface")
 :width 180 :height 100 :corner 12
 :border (list :width 1 :color "outline_variant"))

;; Attributes.kt:162-167 strokes the border with the SAME RoundedCornerShape(12.dp) the
;; surface uses (LayoutNodes.kt:217), so stroke and container agree; tonalElevation stays
;; 0 => flat. Use :color "outline" if only contract-listed theme_roles are wanted.
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on fidelity, with one wording fix owed to the reason string.

What the claim gets right (verified, do not re-litigate): `border` IS a §16.5 universal attribute (contract.json universal_node_attributes; SPEC.md:2187) and IS consumed — Attributes.kt:162-167 does m.border(width, color, cornerShape(node)), and Renderer.kt:273 applies `universal` before dispatch for every type including `card` (RenderCard, LayoutNodes.kt:330-345, receives `m` and passes it to ElevatedCard). RenderSurfaceNode (LayoutNodes.kt:206-226) does prefer `corner` over `shape` and leaves tonalElevation 0. I built and serialized the sketch in batch Emacs and it passes every constructor and validator: {"border":{"color":"outline_variant","width":1},"children":[{"alignment":"center","children":[{"t":"text","text":"Card content"}],"fill_fraction":1.0,"height":100,"t":"box"}],"color":"surface","corner":12,"height":100,"t":"surface","width":180}. So this is not a crash, not a rejected argument, and not a badge-"" style dead member.

Why it is still not a FALSE BLOCKER:

1. The catalog's own applied precedent decides this case, 1:1. jetpacs-m3-bottom-app-bar.el:68-77 composes an M3 FILLED icon-button container from precisely this move — (jetpacs-surface (icon-button …) :color "primary" :shape "circle") — and states the licence in its docstring: "The `icon_button' node has no filled variant, but THE CONTAINER IS NOT WHAT THESE SAMPLES DEMONSTRATE and it composes from wrapped nodes." The same catalog then marks FilledIconButtonSample :unsupported (jetpacs-m3-icon-buttons.el:39-40, used at :89) with "The icon_button node has no variant member: … the filled, tonal or outlined container THIS SAMPLE EXISTS TO SHOW cannot be asked for from Emacs." Identical structure: hand-mixing the container is legitimate when the container is incidental, and is a lookalike when the container is the subject. OutlinedCardSample's entire subject is the container style (upstream CardSamples.kt is a 3x2 matrix: Card / ElevatedCard / OutlinedCard x plain / onClick — the bodies are byte-identical apart from the composable name). This is the README's ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample rule, not a "vaguely similar" quibble.

2. Not an oversight by the module author. jetpacs-m3-card.el:20-27 names and rejects this exact construction: "Drawing them anyway (a `surface' node with a hand-picked color, or a universal `border' stroked over an always-elevated card) would put a lookalike where the sample's whole subject is the container style." The triage agent re-derived a build the author had already considered.

3. The claimed build's defining feature is off-contract. `outline_variant` is NOT in contract.json theme_roles (I checked programmatically: False; the list ends …"outline" "success" "warning", mirrored in jetpacs-theme-roles). It resolves only because THIS Companion carries a bonus arm at ColorModel.kt:76; per SPEC §16.6 an unregistered role is contractually a legible fallback (onSurface), i.e. a heavy 1dp onSurface stroke. validate.py only enforces theme_roles on theme.set (validate.py:325), so nothing catches it. The claim's own contract-legal fallback, `outline`, is not the token OutlinedCard uses (the claim itself reaches for outline_variant, conceding the point). So the single thing OutlinedCard exists to show — its outline — is either off-contract or the wrong colour.

4. `:corner 12` is an Emacs-side guess at a Companion token the wire cannot learn. theme.set carries only dark|colors|syntax (contract methods), ThemeModel.kt has no shape or typography model, and the surface shape vocabulary is rounded(8)/rounded_small(4)/circle — none of which is the card shape. In an EXPRESSIVE catalog whose premise is the new shape scale, a real card follows the Companion's tokens and this hand-drawn surface cannot.

5. Secondary tell: the sketch's geometry would not even match its own sibling in the same module. RenderCard adds Box(Modifier.padding(16.dp)) (LayoutNodes.kt:342), which jetpacs-m3-card--sized compensates for; a surface has none. The matrix that is supposed to contrast three containers would be contrasting two different container implementations.

ONE LEGITIMATE CORRECTION the parent should apply anyway: jetpacs-m3-card.el:42 (and :122) says "the wire can neither drop the card's elevation nor ask for that outline". The second clause is inaccurate — a `card` CAN carry a universal border. Reword to something like "…and a border stroked over it would still be an elevated card", keeping :unsupported. That is a product-text fix, not a verdict change.

findings.subject: The onClick overload of the OutlinedCard: the same flat outlined 180x100 container, tappable, reading "Clickable".
findings.evidence: jetpacs-m3-card.el:121-122 repeats the border error: the card node (and any node) DOES take a `border` — contract.json:57-78 lists it among universal_node_attributes, SPEC.md:2187 defines it as {width, color}, and Attributes.kt:162-167 applies it via Renderer.kt:273. And the sample as a whole is buildable: flat outlined container = `surface` + universal `corner` + universal `border` (LayoutNodes.kt:206-226), tap = `box.on_tap` -> Modifier.clickable (LayoutNodes.kt:200). CardSamples.kt:87-94 confirms the sample adds nothing but onClick to OutlinedCardSample.
findings.build_sketch:
(jetpacs-with-attrs
 (jetpacs-box
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-surface
    (jetpacs-with-attrs
     (jetpacs-box (jetpacs-text "Clickable") :alignment "center")
     :fill_fraction 1.0 :height 100)
    :color "surface")
   :width 180 :height 100 :corner 12
   :border (list :width 1 :color "outline_variant"))
  :on-tap (jetpacs-m3-demo "Clickable"))
 :corner 12 :clip t)
findings.refuted_note: The sketch is constructible and renders, but it never uses the `card` node — it hand-draws a lookalike out of box+surface+border, which is exactly what the README fidelity rule forbids and what the module's own commentary (jetpacs-m3-card.el:22-26) pre-rejects. Evidence: (1) contract.json node_schema.card = {required:[children], optional:[on_tap,on_long_tap,swipe_start,swipe_end]} and SPEC.md:2342 agrees — no variant, colors, or elevation; RenderCard (LayoutNodes.kt:334) emits ElevatedCard unconditionally; M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:75 and WIDGET-REFERENCE.org:70 both record card -> ElevatedCard. Nothing on the wire selects OutlinedCard. (2) The sample's subject is OutlinedCard's onClick overload; "a clickable card" is ALREADY demonstrated by ClickableElevatedCardSample, which is :build. The only delta is the outlined container — precisely the missing part. This is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case verbatim. (3) The argument proves too much: drop :on-tap and the same sketch "supports" OutlinedCardSample; swap :border for :bg and it "supports" CardSample and ClickableCardSample. All four card gaps would flip and the catalog would assert the wire can ask for OutlinedCard, which it cannot. No builder anywhere in emacs/apps/m3-catalog/ uses :border — the technique is unprecedented in the catalog. (4) Secondary contract violation: :color "outline_variant" is NOT one of contract.json's 25 theme_roles. ColorModel.kt happens to map the string, but buildColorScheme (ThemeModel.kt:72-100) never overlays outlineVariant from the §18.4 palette, so that stroke is frozen at the Material default and is the one color in the catalog that would not follow the running Emacs theme. The triage agent's technical points about `border` being universal and consumed (Attributes.kt:162-167, Renderer.kt:272) and box.on_tap -> Modifier.clickable (LayoutNodes.kt:200) are correct, and the elisp validators do accept every argument in the sketch (jetpacs-widgets.el:208-212 :border, :789 box :on-tap, :804 surface :color) — but they establish only that a rectangle can be drawn, not that the Card component's outlined variant is on the wire.

findings.subject: A FAB that toggles open into a stack of labelled icon+text action pills (Reply, Reply all, Forward, Snooze, Archive, Label) and closes again — plus, secondarily, hiding itself while a 100-item list is scrolled away from the top.
findings.evidence: Three checkable claims in the reason are wrong or misleading. (1) "the scaffold fab slot takes ONE node with no expanded or checked member" — the slot takes ONE node of ARBITRARY type and depth: Renderer.kt:702-704 is `node.objOrNull("fab")?.let { RenderNode(it, ctx.child(it, 2)) }`, and SPEC.md:2586 declares bottom_bar/fab/floating_toolbar/drawer "as Nodes". (2) An expanded/collapsed member DOES exist on a node that is legal there: `collapsible` carries `collapsed` (contract.json:251-263) and is in APP_NODE_TYPES via LAYOUT_NODE_TYPES (NodeSupport.kt), and RenderCollapsible toggles DEVICE-LOCALLY on a header tap (LayoutNodes.kt:373,:375) seeded once by `collapsed` (LayoutNodes.kt:359-362) — no round trip and no new action needed, which is precisely the sample's rememberSaveable. (3) The pills are already a wrapped node: RenderButton draws icon + label as an M3 pill (InputNodes.kt:75-95). The reason's `menu` objection is fair (InputNodes.kt:150-180 really is a DropdownMenu popup), but it never considers `collapsible`. The one claim that IS true is the last: the LazyColumn scroll position genuinely never reaches Emacs — state.changed carries only input ids (contract.json:1130-1146) and lazy_column has no scroll callback (LayoutNodes.kt:231-260); that residual, and the Add->Close morph, belong in a narrowed reason, not a blanket unsupported.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-fab-menu--sample ()
  "Upstream FloatingActionButtonMenuSample, claiming this screen's :fab slot."
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-collapsible
    "fab-menu-expanded"
    ;; header MUST be a plain icon/text, never an icon_button: IconButton owns
    ;; its own click (InputNodes.kt:99-114) and would swallow the toggle that
    ;; LayoutNodes.kt:375 hangs on the header Row.
    (jetpacs-icon "add" :size 24 :content-description "Toggle menu")
    (jetpacs-button "Reply"     (jetpacs-m3-demo "Reply")     :icon "message"  :variant "tonal")
    (jetpacs-button "Reply all" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Reply all") :icon "people"   :variant "tonal")
    (jetpacs-button "Forward"   (jetpacs-m3-demo "Forward")   :icon "contacts" :variant "tonal")
    (jetpacs-button "Snooze"    (jetpacs-m3-demo "Snooze")    :icon "snooze"   :variant "tonal")
    (jetpacs-button "Archive"   (jetpacs-m3-demo "Archive")   :icon "archive"  :variant "tonal")
    (jetpacs-button "Label"     (jetpacs-m3-demo "Label")     :icon "label"    :variant "tonal")
    :collapsed t)
   ;; RenderCollapsible does m.fillMaxWidth() (LayoutNodes.kt:367), which would
   ;; span the screen in the fab slot.  :max_width is applied FIRST by
   ;; Attributes.kt:141-144, capping the constraints the inner fillMaxWidth then
   ;; fills -- so the node stays FAB-sized.
   :max_width 220 :bg "primary_container" :corner 24 :clip t :padding 8))

;; registered on the example, exactly like the other chrome samples:
;;   :slots (list :fab #'jetpacs-m3-fab-menu--sample)

;; Honest residuals to name in a NARROWED reason instead of dropping the
;; sample: the pills unfold BELOW the toggle (header-then-children,
;; LayoutNodes.kt:367-390) where upstream unfolds above; the open/close
;; affordance is the rotating chevron (LayoutNodes.kt:365-366,376-380), not an
;; Add->Close morph across checkedProgress; and animateFloatingActionButton's
;; hide-on-scroll is the only part that would need a wire addition.
findings.refuted_note:
The sketch is mechanically legal — I built it and it passes the gate's own checks (`BUILD OK` / `PROFILE OK`, canonical JSON emitted; every member exists: contract.json collapsible = required id/header/children, optional collapsed/on_long_tap/swipe_start/swipe_end; button = label/on_tap + icon/variant/enabled; icon = name + size/color/badge/content_description; all seven icon names are in M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org; `collapsible` is in APP_NODE_TYPES via LAYOUT_NODE_TYPES; `max_width` really does cap the inner fillMaxWidth, Attributes.kt:141-144 then LayoutNodes.kt:367). The triage agent's factual corrections (1) and (2) are also CORRECT: Renderer.kt:703 hands the fab slot an arbitrary node, and RenderCollapsible does toggle device-locally (LayoutNodes.kt:359-362, 373-375). So the reason's wording overreaches and should be tightened.

But the verdict is right, and it fails the README fidelity rule ("what does this sample exist to demonstrate?"), which is one of the listed disqualifiers:

1. THE TOGGLE AFFORDANCE IS UNCONDITIONALLY THE WRONG ONE. LayoutNodes.kt:376-380 hard-codes `Icon(IconMap.get("keyboard_arrow_down"), contentDescription = if (expanded) "Collapse" else "Expand", …graphicsLayer { rotationZ = chevron })` as the first child of the header Row. No `collapsible` member suppresses, replaces, or moves it — the schema has exactly id/header/children/collapsed/on_long_tap/swipe_*. So what renders in the fab slot is a 220dp-wide left-aligned bar carrying a rotating disclosure chevron next to a static plus glyph. Upstream is a circular checkable ToggleFloatingActionButton whose glyph morphs Add→Close via `animateIcon({ checkedProgress })` (FloatingActionButtonMenuSamples.kt:116-141). The chevron is not a residual; it is the wire drawing a different affordance in place of the one the sample is named after.

2. THE UNFOLD DIRECTION IS THE COMPONENT'S DEFINING LAYOUT AND IS INVERTED. LayoutNodes.kt:367-389 is `Column { header; if (expanded) children }` — items below the toggle, with no spacing member and no arrange/align member to right-align them. Upstream is `FloatingActionButtonMenu(Modifier.align(Alignment.BottomEnd))` with items unfolding ABOVE the button. Nothing on the wire reverses it.

3. THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAMPLE ISN'T DRAWN AT ALL. With `:slots` and no `:build`, jetpacs-m3-core.el:407-426 makes the body the literal caption "This sample renders in the screen chrome: fab." The 100-item LazyColumn that drives `animateFloatingActionButton` is absent from the screen entirely — not merely un-hooked.

4. THE MENU'S OWN CLOSE SEMANTICS ARE GONE. Upstream `onClick = { fabMenuExpanded = false }` closes the menu on item tap and `BackHandler(fabMenuExpanded)` closes it on back; `jetpacs-m3-demo` pops a snackbar and leaves the collapsible open, and RenderCollapsible has no back handling.

5. IN-REPO PRECEDENT REJECTS EXACTLY THIS SUBSTITUTION. jetpacs-m3-togglebuttons.el's commentary: "`switch` and `checkbox` do hold state Companion-side, but they draw a switch and a checkbox, each the subject of its own catalog component." `collapsible` holds expansion state Companion-side but draws a chevron disclosure section — the same class of lookalike. This is also the README's ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample rule verbatim: the wire cannot ask for the morph, so a thing that merely renders is not a recreation.

Note also that M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org (the authority per the README) has no FloatingActionButtonMenu or ToggleFloatingActionButton row — only `FloatingActionButton → scaffold.fab`. Two unwrapped composables, and the sample's point does not survive composition from wrapped nodes.

The reason text SHOULD be narrowed: drop "the scaffold fab slot takes ONE node with no expanded or checked member" (the slot takes any node, and `collapsible` does carry `collapsed`), and instead say that no fab-slot node draws a checkable FAB or unfolds items above it — RenderCollapsible's chevron-below-header is the only device-local expander the wire has.

findings.subject: jetpacs-m3-core.el has ZERO `jetpacs-m3-example :unsupported` entries — it is the model/screens/verbs file. Its four gap declarations are `jetpacs-m3--unsupported-row` calls in the theme screen (jetpacs-m3-core.el:478-508), mirroring upstream ThemePicker.kt. This one is upstream's ColorMode enum (Themes.kt:78-98): baseline scheme, a pre-selected custom palette, or the Android system's dynamic (wallpaper) colours.

missing.name: theme.set.dynamic
missing.detail: optional boolean param on the existing theme.set notification (contract.json methods.theme.set.params.optional, alongside dark/colors/syntax). When true the Companion builds its ColorScheme from dynamicLightColorScheme()/dynamicDarkColorScheme() (Android 12+) instead of the baseline light/darkColorScheme() at ThemeModel.kt:134, falling back to baseline where unavailable — exactly upstream's documented fallback (Themes.kt:93-98). Emacs cannot supply this as `colors` because the palette is derived from the device wallpaper, which never reaches Emacs.

findings.evidence: "the Companion owns the color scheme" is false, and §18.4 exists to say so. contract.json:1229-1245 declares `theme.set` (sender emacs, capability `theme`) with optional `colors`; ThemeModel.kt:59-101 buildColorScheme overlays EVERY pushed §18.4 role onto the polarity base and re-derives the surface_container tones, and EbpTheme (ThemeModel.kt:124-146) applies it. Emacs already drives it: jetpacs-theme.el:67-87 `jetpacs-theme-mode` is exactly {system,light,dark,mirror,off}, and `mirror` pushes the running Emacs palette. So Baseline == system/light/dark and Custom == mirror with any authored role plist — 2 of the 3 options are already on the wire today. Only Dynamic is not.

findings.example: ThemePicker "Theme" (System / Light / Dark) — the row core labels "Light/Dark/System"
findings.subject: Upstream ThemeColorMode (Themes.kt:115-119): whether the chosen colour scheme renders light, dark, or follows the device.
findings.evidence: "Set by the Companion; Emacs mirrors it with jetpacs-theme-mode" inverts the direction of control. contract.json:1229-1245 — theme.set's optional `dark` is sent BY EMACS; ThemeModel.kt:129-132 — a real JSON boolean `dark` FORCES the polarity and only its ABSENCE falls through to isSystemInDarkTheme() (amendment #36, SPEC-CHANGES.md:3, which exists precisely to express light/dark/follow-system). jetpacs-theme.el:67-87 already spells the three-way choice as `system`/`light`/`dark`, and setopt applies immediately on a live connection (jetpacs-theme.el:448 `jetpacs-theme--push-mode`, :464 `jetpacs-theme-send`). The catalog does not even need new wire vocabulary — core already owns the toggle-and-repush verb (`m3catalog.pref`, jetpacs-m3-core.el:577-595).
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3--polarity-row ()
  "Upstream ThemePicker's Theme section, as a real three-way control."
  (let ((mode (symbol-name jetpacs-theme-mode)))
    (jetpacs-enum-list
     "m3-pref-polarity"
     (list (jetpacs-enum-option "System" "system")
           (jetpacs-enum-option "Light"  "light")
           (jetpacs-enum-option "Dark"   "dark"))
     ;; :value must name an authored option (jetpacs-widgets.el:1144-1147), and
     ;; `mirror'/`off' are not offered here -- so guard rather than pass blind.
     :value (and (member mode '("system" "light" "dark")) mode)
     :on-change (jetpacs-action "m3catalog.pref"
                               :args (list :key "polarity")))))

;; one new pcase arm in `jetpacs-m3--on-pref' (jetpacs-m3-core.el:581-586):
;;   ("polarity" (setopt jetpacs-theme-mode (intern (plist-get args :value))))
;; the picked value arrives injected as args.value (contract.json:829-833);
;; RenderEnumList publishes the EXACT authored scalar (InputNodes.kt:287-304),
;; and setopt pushes theme.set on the live connection with no further work.
