findings.subject: A horizontal floating toolbar whose five trailing actions (Download, Favorite, Add, Person, ArrowUpward) spill into a more_vert overflow menu when they do not fit.
findings.evidence: companion/.../render/InputNodes.kt:149-180 — RenderMenu IS an overflow control: IconButton whose icon defaults to "more_vert" (line 157) opening a DropdownMenu of items with label+icon+enabled; contract.json:338-346 (menu: items required, icon/enabled optional); Renderer.kt:706-716 — the floating_toolbar slot renders WHATEVER node it is given, full width. The reason's two factual claims (no AppBarRow node, no measure-driven re-flow) are true, but the sample's visible artifact — a toolbar band ending in a more_vert overflow menu carrying the actions that do not fit — is fully authorable; only the width-measurement that CHOOSES the split point is Companion-side, and upstream's own split point at phone width is fixed in practice.
findings.build_sketch:
Same shape as the recreated --expandable-horizontal (top-bar path + :slots (list :floating-toolbar #'...--overflowing-horizontal)):

(defun jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar--overflowing-horizontal ()

Upstream's clickableItem labels are reused verbatim as the menu-item labels — which is exactly what AppBarRow shows once an item overflows. Do NOT pass :spacing alongside :arrange "center": horizontalArrange (LayoutNodes.kt:99-108) discards spacing in every non-else arm (the existing --expandable-horizontal already trips this).
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED — the `:unsupported` marking is correct; this is not a false blocker.

The claim's *mechanical* checks all pass, and I confirmed them rather than assuming:
- `menu` is one of the 39 wire types; contract.json `node_schema.menu` = {required:["items"], optional:["icon","enabled"]}.
- `RenderMenu` (InputNodes.kt:150-180) genuinely consumes `icon` (`node.stringOr("icon","more_vert")`), and each item's `label`/`icon`/`enabled`/`on_tap`. Not a `badge ""` case.
- `jetpacs-menu` / `jetpacs-menu-item` (jetpacs-widgets.el:1030-1042) accept `:icon` via `jetpacs--check-identifier`; all eight icons (check, edit, add, download, favorite, person, arrow_upward, more_vert) are in M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org.
- `:arrange "center"` without `:spacing` is correct w.r.t. the horizontalArrange trap (LayoutNodes.kt:99-108).
- No scaffold-in-scaffold; the `:top-bar` + `:slots` shape is the same one `--expandable-horizontal` already uses.

It fails on the README fidelity rule — the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample test — and it fails on the renderer geometry, which the claim never checked:

1. **The subject is the measurement, not the more_vert glyph.** Upstream's `AppBarRow` (FloatingToolbarSamples.kt:142-193) takes five undifferentiated `clickableItem`s and computes the split at layout time. Every catalog entry that exists *only* because of `AppBarRow` is marked unsupported for exactly this — `BottomAppBarWithOverflow` (jetpacs-m3-bottom-app-bar.el:175), `SimpleTopAppBarWithAdaptiveActions` (jetpacs-m3-top-app-bar.el:166), `OverflowingVerticalFloatingToolbarSample` (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar.el:168). Flipping this one alone leaves three near-identical samples with contradictory verdicts in the shipped product text. The claim's own evidence concedes "no AppBarRow node, no measure-driven re-flow" are TRUE facts; that concession *is* the missing member.

2. **The sketch merges two examples.** Strip the hand-placed menu and `--overflowing-horizontal` is byte-for-byte `--expandable-horizontal` (same Check/Edit/[Add]/Download/Favorite row). `AppBarRow` is the entire reason upstream ships these as two entries. Recreating it as "the other one plus a static ⋮" is the merge the README forbids ("Never drop, rename, reorder or merge an example").

3. **The renderer makes the artifact affirmatively wrong, not merely approximate.** Renderer.kt:706-716 draws the `floating_toolbar` slot as a `Surface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth())` full-width band, and the sketch's row adds `:fill t` + `:arrange "center"`. So the device shows six controls clustered in the middle of a full-width band with empty space on *both* sides — and an overflow indicator next to that empty space. Upstream's overflow only ever appears because `HorizontalFloatingToolbar` is a wrap-content pill that ran out of room. The recreation renders an overflow menu in a container under zero width pressure, which reads as a plain "more" menu (the Menus component), i.e. it does not merely fail to demonstrate overflow — it depicts the opposite of the condition that causes it.

4. **"Upstream's split point at phone width is fixed in practice" is unsupported and false.** `AppBarRow` re-measures per constraint; on a tablet, a foldable, or landscape all five actions sit inline and no more_vert is drawn at all. Hard-coding Download+Favorite visible / Add+Person+ArrowUpward hidden asserts one device's measurement as the sample's content. The Companion runs on Android at arbitrary widths.

This is the `ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample` pattern precisely: something renders, it just is not the thing the sample exists to demonstrate.

findings.subject: FloatingToolbarDefaults.exitAlwaysScrollBehavior(Bottom): the toolbar slides off the bottom edge while the body scrolls down and returns on scroll up.

missing.name: scaffold.floating_toolbar_scroll
missing.detail: Optional enum string, "none" (default) | "exit_always", with an optional companion member scaffold.floating_toolbar_exit_direction ("bottom" default | "top" | "start" | "end"). findings.evidence: contract.json:494-507 — scaffold's optional list is exactly top_bar/body/bottom_bar/fab/floating_toolbar/drawer/snackbar/snackbar_action/on_refresh, with no scroll member; Renderer.kt:705-736 draws the floating_toolbar Surface unconditionally inside the bottomBar Column with no nestedScroll connection; the only scroll-shaped members on the wire are row/column.scroll and the scroll_here anchor (SPEC.md:2168-2197), all Emacs→Companion, and no method in contract.json:871-1583 reports scroll position back. A plain :build (body), not a slot:

    (apply #'jetpacs-column

                           (number-sequence 0 75))
                   (list :spacing 8 :scroll t)))
    :height 480 :fill_fraction 1.0)

    (jetpacs-surface
     (jetpacs-column
      (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar--action "check" "Check")
      (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar--action "edit" "Edit")
      (jetpacs-with-attrs
       (jetpacs-surface (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar--action "add" "Add")

The explicit :height 480 on the inner scrolling column is required: the Example screen already wraps the body in (jetpacs-column ... :scroll t) (jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457), and a nested verticalScroll with an unbounded height constraint throws in Compose. RenderColumn applies the universal height BEFORE .verticalScroll (LayoutNodes.kt:146-151), so the bound holds. The rail is the front child, pinned at center-end while the list scrolls under it — upstream's zIndex(1f) overlay.
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED. The sketch is syntactically legal (I built it in batch Emacs: `BUILD OK`, `:alignment "center_end"` survives; `box.alignment` does enumerate `center_end` in contract.json and `RenderBox` reads it at LayoutNodes.kt:186-204). It still fails, on three independent grounds.

(1) RENDERER TRAP — `surface.elevation` is silently discarded here, which is the `badge ""` class of bug. `RenderSurfaceNode` (LayoutNodes.kt:207-226) passes the wire `elevation` to `tonalElevation` ONLY and never to `shadowElevation`, using `androidx.compose.material3.Surface` directly (material3 1.5.0-alpha16, libs.versions.toml:14). M3's `applyTonalElevation` returns the background color unchanged unless it equals `colorScheme.surface`; the sketch's surface is `:color "primary_container"`. So `:elevation 6` renders LITERALLY NOTHING — no shadow, no tonal shift. A body-composed `surface` cannot cast a shadow at all, on any node, for any color. The only shadow-casting toolbar on the wire is the `floating_toolbar` slot itself, which the renderer draws as `Surface(tonalElevation = 3.dp, shadowElevation = 4.dp, modifier = fillMaxWidth())` (Renderer.kt:706-716). The claim's own citation of "surface :shape circle + :elevation is consumed at LayoutNodes.kt:206-226" is exactly wrong: the shape is consumed, the elevation is not. What the sketch actually draws is a FLAT primary_container pill sitting flush inside the article. Nothing floats. That is the one word in `VerticalFloatingToolbar` the recreation must carry.

(2) FIDELITY — the subject is not carried. Upstream (FloatingToolbarSamples.kt:275-322) is `expanded by rememberSaveable` driven by `Modifier.floatingToolbarVerticalNestedScroll(expanded, onExpand, onCollapse)` on the LazyColumn: scrolling collapses the rail to just the 64dp Add button and hides LeadingContent (Check/Edit, :801-808) and TrailingContent (Download/Favorite, :810-818); scrolling back re-expands it. That is what "Expandable" names, and the wire has no `expanded` member and no scroll signal at all. The claimed precedent does not transfer: the horizontal twin (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar.el:73-88) is hosted in the wire's OWN dedicated floating-toolbar affordance — the `floating_toolbar` scaffold slot, which really is a shadowed floating band — so reading it as `expanded = true` is honest. The vertical proposal abandons that affordance and hand-assembles a lookalike from generic `box`/`surface`/`column`, which is the README's `ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample` case: something similar renders, the subject does not. The catalog already refuses this exact move one module over — jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail.el marks `NavigationRailSample` unsupported because "a full-height column of destinations at the leading edge is not one of the scaffold slots," even though box + a column of icon buttons would draw something similar.

(3) THE PLACEMENT IS NOT REPRODUCED, AND THE SKETCH AS WRITTEN IS BROKEN. The `:height 480` the claim concedes is required (and it is — `RenderColumn` does apply `m` from `modifier.universal(node)` at Renderer.kt:273 before `.verticalScroll`, LayoutNodes.kt:146-151) is itself the tell: upstream's list is the SCREEN's list filling the scaffold content, and the rail is at the screen's CenterEnd with `offset(x = -ScreenOffset).zIndex(1f)`. The sketch gives you a 480dp sub-scroller with a rail at the right edge of that box, inset by the Example screen's own `:padding 16` (jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457), and the whole assembly scrolls away with the page — plus two nested vertical scrollers competing for the same drag. Separately, the `:padding 8` is applied to the surface node itself, i.e. OUTSIDE the container: M3 `Surface` clips to its shape, so with `:shape "circle"` (radius = minDimension/2 on a narrow tall rail) the top Check and bottom Favorite icon buttons are cut by the pill's semicircular ends. There is no inner content padding anywhere in the sketch.

The existing reason's operative claim is not false. Verified: `scaffold` has exactly one bare `floating_toolbar` Node slot with no orientation, alignment or offset member (contract.json scaffold schema; SPEC.md 17.6 line 2586), and the Companion draws it as a full-width band above the bottom bar (Renderer.kt:706-716). Keep the example `:unsupported`.

Overflow: the menu node is precisely a more_vert-defaulted IconButton opening a DropdownMenu (InputNodes.kt:149-180, contract.json:338-346), and a column of icon_buttons ending in one is what AppBarColumn renders once items overflow. findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED — on the README fidelity rule, not on node/member existence.

WHAT THE CLAIM GETS RIGHT (conceded, verified): every node and member in the sketch exists and is consumed. `box.alignment "center_end"` -> Alignment.CenterEnd at /home/calebc42/pkb/projects/jetpacs/jetpacs/llm-poc-2/companion/app/src/main/kotlin/com/calebc42/ebp/companion/render/LayoutNodes.kt:194 (contract.json node_schema box = {children; alignment, on_tap}); `menu` renders an IconButton defaulted to more_vert opening a DropdownMenu at render/InputNodes.kt:149-180; `jetpacs-menu`/`jetpacs-menu-item`/`jetpacs-box`/`jetpacs-surface`/`jetpacs-column` all accept exactly these arguments (jetpacs-widgets.el:1030-1042, 789-817, 749-768); `fill_fraction` -> fillMaxWidth (Attributes.kt:149-150); all eight icons are in M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org. I built the sketch verbatim inside the real example-screen wrapper: it builds, passes the app profile, canonicalizes. No schema/renderer/constructor failure. It fails on the fourth condition.

1. THE OVERFLOW HALF IS THE SUBJECT, AND IT IS NOT DEMONSTRATED. In /home/calebc42/pkb/resources/android/Compose-Material-3-Expressive-Catalog/app/src/main/java/com/emertozd/compose/catalog/samples/FloatingToolbarSamples.kt, OverflowingVerticalFloatingToolbarSample (l.297-419) differs from ExpandableVerticalFloatingToolbarSample (l.248-296) in exactly one thing: `trailingContent = { AppBarColumn { 5x clickableItem } }` instead of `TrailingContent()`, with `expanded` pinned true. The sample exists to show AppBarColumn measuring the available cross-axis extent and MOVING the items that do not fit into the overflow menu. The sketch hard-codes all five into a static `menu`: nothing measures, nothing moves, the split point is authored in Elisp and never changes with window size. It is not even a static snapshot of the upstream rendering — AppBarColumn shows as many items INLINE as fit (on a tall rail, several of Download/Favorite/Add/Person/ArrowUpward are visible icon buttons) and only the remainder goes under more_vert; the sketch shows zero inline and everything hidden. The claim's own concession, "only the width/height measurement that chooses the split point is Companion-side", names the subject and then discards it. This is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case in README l.41-43: something similar renders, the demonstrated behavior does not exist on the wire.

2. IT CONTRADICTS AN UNCHALLENGED SIBLING. The same module already marks OverflowingHorizontalFloatingToolbarSample :unsupported with "There is no AppBarRow node: a row cannot measure its children and move the ones that do not fit into a more_vert overflow menu" (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar.el:142-148). AppBarRow and AppBarColumn are the same mechanism on two axes. Accepting the vertical twin as a :build while the horizontal twin stays unsupported would put mutually contradictory product text in front of the same user, two screens apart.

3. THE FLOATING/VERTICAL HALF ABANDONS THE SLOT AND PAINTS A LOOK-ALIKE IN THE BODY. The wire's floating toolbar IS `scaffold.floating_toolbar`, which Renderer.kt:705-716 draws as a `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` Surface inside the bottomBar Column — no orientation, no alignment, no offset. The sketch does not use it; it draws a decorative rail as ordinary body content and has to fabricate a 480dp stand-in "screen content" (a 76-`text` column) to have something to float over. The real screen content sits elsewhere: jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457 already wraps every :build in `(jetpacs-column BODY :scroll t :align "center" :spacing 16 :fill t)` with :padding 16, so the rail is centered inside a synthetic band inside the screen's own scroll column — not pinned at the content area's CenterEnd with ScreenOffset above the screen's scrolling list. The catalog's own precedent rejects exactly this move: jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail.el marks all 8 samples unsupported because no slot holds a full-height edge rail, explicitly declining to draw the rail in the body instead.

4. SUPPORTING (dependency floor, verified against the material3 AAR on disk): the Companion's material3 1.4.0 contains only `tokens/FloatingToolbarTokens.class` — no FloatingToolbar composable at all — so no wire member could render a real VerticalFloatingToolbar today. `AppBarColumnKt`/`AppBarRowKt` ARE present in 1.4.0, so the overflow container is implementable the moment the wire has a node for it.

The existing reason string is accurate as written ("the floating_toolbar slot has no orientation member for a vertical rail, and there is no AppBarColumn node that moves the actions which do not fit into an overflow menu"). Leave it :unsupported.

findings.refuted_note:
The sketch type-checks but does not demonstrate the sample's subject, and its central mechanism does not work at all on device.

(1) DECISIVE — the FAB does not toggle. The collapsible header in the sketch contains `jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar--action "add" "Add"`, i.e. an `icon_button`. RenderIconButton (InputNodes.kt:99-113) is a Material3 `IconButton` with `onClick = { onButton(node.objOrNull("on_tap"), ctx) }`. The collapsible's toggle is `Modifier.clickable { expanded = !expanded }` on the header Row (LayoutNodes.kt:371-375). The inner IconButton consumes the pointer input inside its touch target, so tapping the visible FAB fires `m3catalog.demo` — a wire round-trip that pops a snackbar — and `expanded` never changes. Only a tap on the chevron or the row's dead space folds it. The claim's load-bearing sentence ("The FAB (the collapsible header) toggles the cluster with zero wire traffic — the sample's actual subject") is exactly inverted by the renderer: wire traffic, no toggle.

(2) Wrong axis + an uninvited chevron. RenderCollapsible is `Column(m.fillMaxWidth())` that unconditionally prepends a rotating `keyboard_arrow_down` Icon (LayoutNodes.kt:376-380) and renders children BELOW via RenderColumnChildren (:389). Upstream is a single horizontal pill — four IconButtons with the vibrant FAB attached at the TRAILING end — collapsing horizontally into the FAB. The sketch draws [chevron][FAB] on top with the four icons stacked in a second row beneath. The FAB migrates from trailing-end to leading-top and a disclosure chevron upstream does not have becomes the real affordance. The triage agent concedes this as a "caveat to state in the docstring"; under README rule "what does this sample exist to demonstrate?" it is the disqualifier, not a footnote.

(3) Nothing collapses toward the FAB. `fillMaxWidth()` on the collapsible Column is unconditional, so the `:max_width 280` surface stays a ~264dp pill in both states and merely loses height. Upstream's collapsed state is a lone FAB. The `expanded` flag's entire visual point is absent.

(4) It duplicates an existing supported example: `jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar--as-scaffold-fab` already renders that same person/edit/favorite/more_vert + Add cluster in a primary_container circle surface. The sketch is that node plus a chevron and a vertical fold.

Nothing in the sketch is schema-invalid — box.alignment "bottom_end" (contract.json box.optional, LayoutNodes.kt:189-199), surface.shape/color/elevation, collapsible {id, header, children}, :max_width via widthIn (Attributes.kt), and jetpacs-collapsible/jetpacs-box/jetpacs-surface all accept these arguments; no scaffold nests. It fails on fidelity and on the renderer refusing the toggle — the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample class exactly.

Note on the existing reason: clause (a) as worded ("no alignment ... member floats a toolbar over the body at BottomEnd") is loose, since box.alignment plus padding can position a node bottom-end; it is only true of the floating_toolbar SLOT, which the renderer draws as a full-width band. Clause (b) is sound and carries the verdict. The reason string deserves re-wording, not the verdict flipping.

findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED — the sketch draws a chevron accordion, not a FAB-toggled floating rail.

1. THE FAB TOGGLES NOTHING (fatal, README fidelity rule). `RenderCollapsible` (LayoutNodes.kt:358-390) puts the toggle on the header ROW: `Modifier.clickable { expanded = !expanded }`. The sketch's header is `(jetpacs-surface (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar--action "add" "Add") ...)`, and `--action` is `jetpacs-icon-button` (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar.el:59), which `RenderIconButton` (InputNodes.kt:99-114) emits as a real `IconButton(onClick = { onButton(node.on_tap) })`. A child `clickable` consumes the down event (`clickable` -> `detectTapAndPress` -> `awaitFirstDown(requireUnconsumed = true)`), so the parent Row's clickable never fires. Tapping the "FAB" pops the `jetpacs-m3-demo "Add"` snackbar and leaves the rail exactly as it was. The single line this sample exists to demonstrate — `VibrantFloatingActionButton(onClick = { expanded = !expanded })`, FloatingToolbarSamples.kt:611-615 — is not wired and cannot be: no node's `on_tap` can address another node's Companion-local expansion. This is precisely the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case the README names.

2. THE AFFORDANCE THAT DOES TOGGLE IS A CHEVRON THE SAMPLE DOESN'T HAVE. LayoutNodes.kt:376-380 unconditionally prepends a rotating `keyboard_arrow_down` Icon to the header row. The user sees a disclosure caret beside a circle; the caret is the collapse control. M3's whole point in this sample is that the FAB *is* the control and there is no caret.

3. ORDER INVERSION IS STRUCTURAL. `Column { headerRow(); if (expanded) children }` — header always above. Upstream anchors BottomEnd (line 618) with the FAB at the bottom of the rail; the sketch parks it at the top, farthest from the thumb, at the corner the toolbar is anchored to. The claimed build's own docstring concedes this.

4. HALF THE SAMPLE HAS NO WIRE AT ALL. Lines 651-663 apply `floatingToolbarVerticalNestedScroll(expanded, onExpand, onCollapse)` to the content Column — scrolling the body drives the same `expanded`. The wire carries no scroll signal; the sketch's `:scroll t` cannot reach the collapsible. The module's own ScrollableHorizontal reason already establishes this.

5. GEOMETRY DOESN'T FIT (evidence it was never rendered). `:max_width 96 :padding 8` leaves 80dp of content; the header row is chevron (24dp Icon + 4dp padding per side = 32dp) + the `:width 56` FAB surface = 88dp. Surface clips to its shape, so the FAB is clipped at the right edge.

6. IT DOESN'T COMPILE. `jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar--lorem` is not defined in the module (the catalog's only lorem is `jetpacs-m3-text-fields--lorem`, jetpacs-m3-text-fields.el:51). `tools/m3-check.sh` byte-compiles warnings-as-errors -> free variable.

7. The component is absent from the Companion's material3 1.4.0 entirely (M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:20 — FloatingToolbar arrives in 1.5+), and the one route the wire has, `scaffold.floating_toolbar`, is drawn by Renderer.kt:706-716 as a full-width `Surface(fillMaxWidth)` inside the scaffold's `bottomBar` slot: no orientation, no alignment, no offset, no expanded.

WHAT THE TRIAGE AGENT GOT RIGHT (and the maintainer should act on): `box.alignment "bottom_end"` genuinely is consumed (LayoutNodes.kt:197), and the shared `--vertical-note` (jetpacs-m3-floating-toolbar.el:48-51) IS sloppy for this example — it says "the center end of the screen" while this sample aligns BottomEnd (lines 617-620), and it argues only the orientation axis when this sample's headline axis is the FAB-toggled `expanded`. The reason string deserves a rewrite; the `:unsupported` verdict does not.

The plain `snackbar` string stays the message and the accessibility text. Rejected as content-invalid if it contains a scaffold. findings.evidence: contract.json:494-507 + field_types "snackbar": "string" (contract.json:518) — the snackbar is a bare message, not a Node; SPEC.md:2593-2595 says outright "`snackbar` carries no §16.1 presentation identity: it is not a node"; Renderer.kt:674 hardwires snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(hostState) } with no content lambda seam. Nothing in the 39 node types reaches inside the host, and drawing a bordered card at the bottom of the body would be the "vaguely similar" the README forbids (no host animation, no timing, not the snackbar surface).

findings.subject: Raising a snackbar through a business-logic layer (a CONFLATED Channel) rather than from the click handler, showing "Snackbar # N" with actionLabel "Action on N", then branching on SnackbarResult.
findings.evidence: The first clause is true — nothing reports SnackbarResult.Dismissed (Renderer.kt:668-669 dispatches only on ActionPerformed) — but upstream's two branches are both EMPTY (ScaffoldSamples.kt:265-273: "/* action has been performed */", "/* dismissed, no action needed */"), so nothing observable rides on it. The second clause is FALSE: scaffold.snackbar_action {label, on_tap} exists (contract.json:503-505, field_types "snackbar_action": "label-on-tap-object" at contract.json:596), the Companion feeds its label to showSnackbar as actionLabel and dispatches its on_tap on a user tap (Renderer.kt:664-669), and jetpacs-scaffold already accepts :snackbar-action with a validator (jetpacs-widgets.el:1501-1541). Emacs authors the whole tree, so the very push that carries a new `snackbar` string can carry the matching action — the two are members of one snapshot, not separately-timed events. The business-logic-layer half is if anything a better match than upstream's: jetpacs-shell--snackbars is a per-surface latest-wins slot (jetpacs-shell.el:56-57), i.e. Channel.CONFLATED.
findings.build_sketch:
Route the Example screen through the :top-bar path so it is a jetpacs-scaffold — jetpacs-chrome-screen has no :snackbar keyword (jetpacs-chrome.el:79-80), so a :snackbar slot only reaches the wire that way:

(defun jetpacs-m3-snackbars--coroutines-top-bar (back)
  (apply #'jetpacs-row
         (append (when back (list (jetpacs-m3-back-button back)))
                 (list (jetpacs-with-attrs
                        (jetpacs-text "ScaffoldWithCoroutinesSnackbar" :style "title" :max-lines 2)
                        :weight 1))
                 (list :align "center" :spacing 4))))

(jetpacs-m3-example "ScaffoldWithCoroutinesSnackbar" "Snackbars examples"
  :source jetpacs-m3-snackbars--source
  :build #'jetpacs-m3-snackbars--coroutines-body        ; (jetpacs-text "Snackbar demo")
  :top-bar #'jetpacs-m3-snackbars--coroutines-top-bar
  :slots (list :fab #'jetpacs-m3-snackbars--simple-fab
               :snackbar "Snackbar # 1"
               :snackbar-action (jetpacs-snackbar-action
                                 "Action on 1" (jetpacs-m3-demo "Action on 1"))))

Wire-side this is complete today. Two catalog-plumbing (NOT wire) edits it needs, both one-liners in core: add :snackbar-action to jetpacs-m3-slot-keys (jetpacs-m3-core.el:94-95) and give it the same non-function pass-through :snackbar already has in jetpacs-m3--example-slots (jetpacs-m3-core.el:435). Worth knowing while authoring: on this app jetpacs-shell-notify does NOT become a scaffold snackbar — the catalog surface is a multi_view stack, so the H10 note applies and notify degrades to a toast (jetpacs-chrome.el:28-32; jetpacs-shell.el:862-865 injects only when the ROOT spec is a scaffold). The authored :snackbar member above is the reliable route, and it presents on screen entry because RenderScaffold's LaunchedEffect(snackbar) fires when that view composes (Renderer.kt:662).
findings.refuted_note: Wire members check out (contract.json:503-504,519,596; Renderer.kt:656-669; jetpacs-widgets.el:1501-1541), but the sketch fails the README fidelity rule. Upstream (ScaffoldSamples.kt:239-278) the subject is CAUSATION routed through an intermediary: FAB click -> channel.trySend(++clickCount) -> a collector calls showSnackbar("Snackbar # N", actionLabel="Action on N"). The sketch has no causation at all: :snackbar "Snackbar # 1" is a static member of the registry plist and RenderScaffold's LaunchedEffect(snackbar) (Renderer.kt:662) fires it the moment the view composes, so the snackbar appears unprompted on screen entry. The one control upstream wires to the channel — the FAB — is jetpacs-m3-snackbars--simple-fab, whose tap goes m3catalog.demo -> jetpacs-m3--on-demo (jetpacs-m3-core.el:609-615) -> jetpacs-shell-notify, and the claim itself concedes that on this multi_view surface (jetpacs-chrome.el:275) the injection gate (jetpacs-shell.el:864) fails and it degrades to jetpacs-toast (jetpacs-shell.el:920-921). On device: an uninvited snackbar on arrival and a "Show snackbar" button that pops a toast. That is exactly the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample failure mode. Second, the counter — the only observable evidence of Channel.CONFLATED — is dead: a constant string can never change and the Companion re-shows only on change (Renderer.kt:662; jetpacs-shell.el:955), so there is exactly one snackbar for the life of the view and the conflation the sample is named for is unobservable. Third, the existing reason's second clause is NOT false: for the only tap-driven route in this app, jetpacs-shell-notify stores a bare string and the shell injects (list :snackbar snack) and nothing else (jetpacs-shell.el:864-865) — no channel for an accompanying action, and on a multi-view surface it never reaches a scaffold. The claim rebuts it by describing a different build (a tap-driven repush carrying a new snackbar plus matching action) that the sketch does not perform, that needs per-tap state a static jetpacs-m3-example plist cannot hold, and that would require registering a new action from a component module — forbidden by README rule 5. Minor but real: :snackbar-action is absent from jetpacs-m3-slot-keys (jetpacs-m3-core.el:94-95) so jetpacs-m3-example signals today; with only the first "one-liner" applied, jetpacs-m3--example-slots (jetpacs-m3-core.el:435) funcalls the plist, the guard substitutes an empty_state node, and jetpacs--check-snackbar-action then signals OUTSIDE any guard, taking the screen build and the gate down. The :top-bar route also drops the guidelines/docs/source actions every other Example screen carries. Separate finding for the parent: by the same H10 reasoning the already-supported ScaffoldWithSimpleSnackbar is subtly wrong — its module Commentary and simple-fab docstring claim the tap returns as scaffold.snackbar, but on this multi_view surface it returns as a toast.

findings.subject: A very long message in a snackbar, clamped by a custom SnackbarHost to the two lines the Material spec recommends, with TextOverflow.Ellipsis.

The long message ITSELF is already carriable (:snackbar with the 40-"very" string), so what is missing is exactly the clamp that distinguishes this sample from ScaffoldWithSimpleSnackbar — text.max_lines exists (contract.json:80-91) but no node carries the snackbar message, so it cannot be reached.

findings.subject: Checkbox(checkmarkStroke = Stroke(w, cap = StrokeCap.Round, join = StrokeJoin.Round), outlineStroke = Stroke(w)) — the expressive rounded-stroke checkbox drawing.

missing.name: checkbox.stroke
missing.detail: Optional object {width?: non-negative dp (default CheckboxDefaults.StrokeWidth), cap?: "butt" (default) | "round" | "square", join?: "miter" (default) | "round" | "bevel"}, applied by the Companion as checkmarkStroke = Stroke(width, cap = cap, join = join) and outlineStroke = Stroke(width). Unknown cap/join fall back to the default per SPEC 12 rule 6. Same member SHOULD be accepted on switch for symmetry. A leaner alternative: a single enum checkbox.stroke_cap: "butt" | "round".

findings.evidence: contract.json:389-399 — checkbox takes id + checked/label/on_change/enabled and nothing else; InputNodes.kt:200-209 calls M3 Checkbox(checked, enabled, onCheckedChange) with no stroke arguments. The canvas escape hatch does not exist either: VisualizationNodes.kt:232-261 strokes every op with Stroke(strokeW) at default Butt cap / Miter join, and canvas ops carry only color/fill/stroke_width/closed (SPEC.md:2548-2556), so a hand-drawn rounded checkmark is not expressible and would be inert anyway (SPEC.md:2561: "Canvas has no implicit interaction").

findings.subject: TriStateCheckbox as a parent whose ToggleableState is derived from two dependent checkboxes — On when both are checked, Off when neither, Indeterminate in between — and whose click drives both children.

missing.name: checkbox.state
missing.detail: Optional enum string "off" | "on" | "indeterminate", mutually exclusive with `checked` (a node carrying both is content-invalid). When present the Companion renders TriStateCheckbox with the matching ToggleableState; a click cycles Indeterminate/Off → On → Off exactly as ToggleableState does, publishes the new enum string as the state.changed value, and then dispatches on_change with that string in args.value. §13.6 draft compatibility keys on the value schema, so a retained boolean draft is incompatible with a state-typed node and is erased. This is the wire's third-state channel: it changes what state.changed carries for that id from boolean to the enum string, which is why it must be a distinct member rather than a widened `checked`.

findings.evidence: contract.json:389-399 (no tri-state node, no third-state member) and field_types "checked": "boolean" (contract.json:562); SPEC.md:2496-2498 — "Checkbox and switch `checked` values are booleans" and "Every flip MUST produce state.changed" with a boolean; InputNodes.kt:184-210 instantiates M3 Checkbox, never TriStateCheckbox. The visual alone IS drawable (icons check_box / check_box_outline_blank / indeterminate_check_box all exist — M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org:414, 415, 1006 — inside a box with on_tap), but the derivation is not: the children's flips are Companion-local drafts, and the only way Emacs learns of one is state.changed, which would need a module-registered subscription (jetpacs-surfaces.el:1092 jetpacs-on-state-change), a new verb to re-push, and reset_input_ids to force the children — a server round trip per flip, forbidden by README rule 5 and not the local tri-state toggle the sample demonstrates.

findings.subject: The TriStateCheckbox parent/child cascade drawn with rounded checkmark and outline strokes — the two previous samples' axes at once.

missing.name: checkbox.state
missing.detail: Optional enum "off" | "on" | "indeterminate" (mutually exclusive with `checked`) rendering TriStateCheckbox and publishing the enum string through state.changed / on_change — as specified on TriStateCheckboxSample.

missing.name: checkbox.stroke
missing.detail: Optional {width?, cap?: "butt"|"round"|"square", join?: "miter"|"round"|"bevel"} mapped to checkmarkStroke/outlineStroke — as specified on CheckboxRoundedStrokesSample. It must apply to the tri-state rendering too, since TriStateCheckbox takes the same two Stroke parameters.

findings.evidence: Both clauses check out against the same ground truth: contract.json:389-399 lists no state and no stroke member on checkbox, field_types "checked": "boolean" (contract.json:562), and InputNodes.kt:184-210 renders M3 Checkbox with only checked/enabled/onCheckedChange — no TriStateCheckbox, no checkmarkStroke/outlineStroke. Nothing in the 39 node types renders a three-state toggle, and canvas cannot fake the rounded caps (VisualizationNodes.kt:232-261, default Butt/Miter).

findings.subject: It exists to demonstrate WideNavigationRailState: a header icon button that expands/collapses the wide rail in place (menu <-> menu_open), with the rail's currentValue and isAnimating printed beside it.

missing.name: navigation_rail
missing.detail: {items: [{icon, label, selected?, badge?, on_tap}], expanded?: bool, header?: Node, arrangement?: "top"|"center"|"bottom", modal?: bool, hide_on_collapse?: bool, on_expand_change?: ActionDescriptor}. findings.subject: It exists to demonstrate ModalWideNavigationRail with hideOnCollapse=false: the rail stays on screen as a narrow icon rail when collapsed and expands into a scrimmed modal panel, with expandedHeaderTopPadding aligning its header to the screen.

missing.detail: boolean, default false. Emacs-authored open state for the drawer panel; the Companion syncs its DrawerState to the pushed value (open on true, close on false) while still allowing scrim dismissal. This is what lets a body button expand the panel and an item tap collapse it via the ordinary action round-trip.

With it the sample recreates as: drawer = the composed expanded rail, body = the "$page Page / Open modal rail" button.

findings.subject: It exists to demonstrate WideNavigationRail with railExpanded=false items: a ~96dp vertical bar of three destinations drawn icon-above-label, the selected one carrying the active-indicator pill and the filled glyph.
findings.evidence: jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:98-131 builds exactly this item (box+column+icon+text with `:bg "secondary_container" :corner 16` as the active indicator) for NavigationBarItem, and the same module's commentary settles the sizing argument: "The one member a bar node would add is the container HEIGHT — and that is the universal `height` attribute" (:width here). Attributes.kt:154-161 consumes bg with cornerShape; LayoutNodes.kt:186-204 makes the box tappable. The shared `--wide-note` reason claims "no node carries a WideNavigationRailItem's selected state or the active indicator" — false twice over: the indicator is bg+corner, and `chip.selected` renders a FilterChip selection (InputNodes.kt:119-131) if a pill item were preferred. Icon names home/favorite/favorite_border/star/star_border all exist in M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item (label sel unsel selected)
  (jetpacs-box
   (jetpacs-column
    (jetpacs-with-attrs
     (jetpacs-box (jetpacs-icon (if selected sel unsel)
                                :color (if selected "on_secondary_container" "on_surface_variant"))
                  :alignment "center")
     :width 56 :height 32 :corner 16 :bg (and selected "secondary_container"))
    (jetpacs-text label :style "label"
                  :color (if selected "on_surface" "on_surface_variant"))
    :spacing 4 :align "center")
   :alignment "center" :on-tap (jetpacs-m3-demo label)))

(defun jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--collapsed ()
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-column
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Home"     "home"     "home"            t)
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Search"   "favorite" "favorite_border" nil)
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Settings" "star"     "star_border"     nil)
    :spacing 12 :align "center")
   :width 96 :min_height 320 :bg "surface"))
;; upstream's own label/icon mismatch (Search->Favorite, Settings->Star) is kept.
findings.refuted_note:
The sketch is mechanically valid — I evaluated it against the real constructors and it builds and canonicalizes; min_height is consumed (Attributes.kt:145), box on_tap is consumed (LayoutNodes.kt:201), and cornerShape turns a scalar :corner into a RoundedCornerShape (Attributes.kt:92-109). The triage agent is also correct that the shared --wide-note is partly false: the active indicator IS bg+corner (Attributes.kt m.background(it, shape)), navigation-bar already ships that item, and chip.selected does exist and renders a FilterChip (contract chip.optional; InputNodes.kt:118-131). The reason string needs repair. But the verdict stands, on the fidelity prong.

1) The outer node in the sketch IS the rail container — the "~96dp vertical bar" the subject names — and the wire cannot color it. M3's rail container is surfaceContainer. contract.json theme_roles lists 25 roles with no surface_container, and resolveColorIn (ColorModel.kt:54-83) has no case for it, falling through to `else -> scheme.onSurface`, i.e. naming it paints the rail in the foreground text color. The sketch's fallback :bg "surface" resolves to scheme.surface — and jetpacs-theme.el:277-279 pushes (:background . bg) and (:surface . bg) as the SAME hex, ThemeModel.kt:89 is `background = c.role("background") ?: c.role("surface")`, and RenderScaffold uses M3 Scaffold's default containerColor = colorScheme.background. So scheme.surface == scheme.background for every theme Jetpacs pushes and the bar is painted exactly the page color. On device the sketch renders three floating icon/label stacks with a pill on the first — no bar, which is the sample's whole subject.

2) Screen model. jetpacs-m3-example-screen (jetpacs-m3-core.el:451-454) puts the body in (jetpacs-column BODY :scroll t :align "center" :spacing 16 :fill t) under :padding 16. The "rail" renders horizontally CENTRED in the content area, 16dp inside the padding, scrolling with the content, at an invented :min_height 320 — where WideNavigationRail is fillMaxHeight, leading-edge anchored, non-scrolling, with its own windowInsetsPadding. RenderScaffold applies statusBarsPadding/navigationBarsPadding only at the top_bar and bottom_bar slots (Renderer.kt:680, 723); body content gets none. This is exactly the README's "superficially similar but does not demonstrate the subject" case.

3) The navigation-bar parity the evidence leans on cuts the other way. That recreation is legitimate because the SLOT supplies what the wire cannot: Renderer.kt:707-730 wraps the bottom_bar node in Surface(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceContainer, Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) inside Box(Modifier.navigationBarsPadding()…). The wire authors only the items; the Companion draws the container, the band, the edge anchoring and the system inset. contract scaffold.optional is [top_bar, body, bottom_bar, fab, floating_toolbar, drawer, snackbar, snackbar_action, on_refresh] and jetpacs-m3-slot-keys matches — there is no leading-edge slot, so a rail must be drawn from body nodes, which per (1) and (2) cannot produce a rail. The quoted "the one member a bar node would add is the container HEIGHT" is true only because the bar had a slot to live in.

4) Secondary: the sketch is indistinguishable from what one would author for NavigationRailSample (80dp vs 96dp) and near-indistinguishable from a hand-drawn WideNavigationRailExpandedSample, collapsing three separate upstream entries into one picture.

findings.subject: It exists to demonstrate WideNavigationRail opened Expanded: the same three destinations drawn as icon-BESIDE-label rows, with the active indicator wrapping icon and label together in a wide (~220dp) rail.

The shared `--wide-note` ("no node ... carries the active indicator its railExpanded form draws around the icon and label") is contradicted by the sibling module's own working code.

(defun jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--expanded ()
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-column
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--wide-item "Home"     "home"     "home"            t)
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--wide-item "Search"   "favorite" "favorite_border" nil)

findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED — on fidelity and placement, not on schema. First, what the triage got right: every member in the sketch exists and is live. box{alignment,on_tap}, row{spacing,align}, column{spacing}, icon{color}, text{style,color} are all in ebp/contract.json node_schema; width/min_height/bg/corner/pad are in universal_node_attributes and are all read in Attributes.kt (pad 119-130, width 139, min_height 145-148, corner 92-109/154, bg 159-161); RenderBox maps "center_start" -> Alignment.CenterStart (LayoutNodes.kt:192) and applies on_tap; jetpacs-with-attrs drops nil-valued members (jetpacs-widgets.el:437) so `:bg (and selected ...)` is legal. The shared --wide-note's SECOND clause ("no node carries ... the active indicator") is genuinely overstated — jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:117-131 does draw a static selected pill with :pad/:corner/:bg. The triage wins that narrow point and loses the example.

(1) THE CITED EVIDENCE CUTS THE OTHER WAY. navigation-bar's horizontal-item is supported because a navigation BAR is screen chrome: those samples claim the Example screen's real `bottom_bar` slot (jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:197/204/209; jetpacs-m3-core.el:428-439). jetpacs-m3-slot-keys is '(:fab :bottom-bar :drawer :floating-toolbar :on-refresh :snackbar) (jetpacs-m3-core.el:94-95) — there is no leading-edge slot, which is exactly why the rail module's commentary says a rail is the not-a-bottom-bar case. The sketch therefore puts the "rail" in the BODY, and the body is `(jetpacs-column BODY :scroll t :align "center" :spacing 16 :fill t)` under :padding 16 (jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457). Every body sample is horizontally CENTERED. The claimed build renders three pills floating dead-center in a scrolling column. A navigation rail centered in the content area is not a navigation rail.

(2) THE ONE MEMBER THAT COULD FIX (1) IS A DEAD MEMBER — the `badge ""` trap exactly. `align_self` is in contract.json universal_node_attributes and is validated by jetpacs--check-attr (jetpacs-widgets.el:213-215), and Attributes.kt:6 even claims "`weight` and `align_self` ... are applied by the container cases". Grep of the entire companion source finds align_self in that comment and NOWHERE else: RowScope.RenderRowChildren and ColumnScope.RenderColumnChildren (Renderer.kt) apply `weightOf(child)` only. So nothing on the wire can pull a body child back to the leading edge.

(3) FULL HEIGHT IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE. WideNavigationRail fills its parent's height; that is the defining geometry of any rail. On the wire `fill` and `fill_fraction` are fillMaxWidth ONLY (Attributes.kt:149-150 fill_fraction -> fillMaxWidth; LayoutNodes.kt RenderRow/RenderColumn: `fill -> m.fillMaxWidth()`), and there is no fill-height attribute at all. The sketch substitutes `:min_height 320`, an invented dp with no upstream counterpart, on a node inside a vertically scrolling column.

(4) FIDELITY RULE (the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample test). Read the upstream sample (NavigationRailSamples.kt:339-366): it is `WideNavigationRail(state = rememberWideNavigationRailState(initialValue = WideNavigationRailValue.Expanded))` wrapping three `WideNavigationRailItem(railExpanded = true)`. Its subject is the WideNavigationRail component at the Expanded value of WideNavigationRailValue — it exists as the paired opposite of WideNavigationRailCollapsedSample (lines 312-337), which is the identical item list at railExpanded = false. Strip the rail node and the state and the pair collapses into "rows vs stacks". What the sketch actually draws is the sibling module's ShortNavigationBarItem-at-IconPosition.Start row (spacing/pad/corner nudged 8/8/20 -> 12/12/28) minus the bar — i.e. the catalog would show WideNavigationRailExpandedSample and ShortNavigationBarWithHorizontalItemsSample as the same picture, which is the example-merging the fidelity rule forbids.

(5) IT DOES NOT EVEN DRAW WHAT THE CLAIM SAYS. The claim's own subject line is "the active indicator wrapping icon and label together in a wide (~220dp) rail". The indicator here is the wrap-content row, so each pill hugs its own label — "Home" and "Settings" get visibly different indicator widths inside a 220dp box, where the expanded rail's items span the rail. Nothing has :fill or :fill_fraction, and because the tap `box` is content-sized, its `:alignment "center_start"` is inert.

Net: the sketch compiles and renders, but it renders a centered, fixed-height list of three pills. It demonstrates neither the rail nor its Expanded state. Keep :unsupported.

findings.subject: It exists to demonstrate swapping the rail's vertical Arrangement between Center and Bottom and seeing the destinations move.
findings.evidence: LayoutNodes.kt:110-119 `verticalArrange` maps column.arrange "center" -> Arrangement.Center and "end" -> Arrangement.Bottom, consumed by RenderColumn (LayoutNodes.kt:146-162) — so the reason's "a column's arrange member positions body content, not rail destinations" is circular and false: if the rail IS a column, arrange positions its destinations, which is the entire subject. `tabs` (LayoutNodes.kt:396-465) supplies the device-local swap with no new action, which respects the module rule against registering actions. TRAP: with `arrange` set, verticalArrange DISCARDS `spacing`, so space the items with per-item :pad instead.

findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on fidelity and on a self-contradicting dependency. The claim's wire facts are correct as far as they go — I verified them and they are not the reason it fails:

VERIFIED TRUE (so these are NOT my grounds): `column.arrange` is in contract.json (`column: {required:[children], optional:[spacing,align,arrange,scroll,fill]}`); `jetpacs-column` accepts `:arrange` against `jetpacs--arranges` ("start center end space_between space_around space_evenly", jetpacs-widgets.el:719-720,762); `verticalArrange` maps "center"→Arrangement.Center and "end"→Arrangement.Bottom (LayoutNodes.kt:110-119) and RenderColumn consumes it (LayoutNodes.kt:154); `:width/:height/:bg` are applied in Modifier.universal (Attributes.kt:139-140,159); `:pad (list :vertical 6)` passes `jetpacs--pad-keys` (widgets.el:190) and Attributes.kt:121-129 reads pad.vertical for top/bottom; the arrange-discards-spacing trap is real and correctly worked around; `jetpacs-tabs` accepts equal-length lists plus `:id` (widgets.el:922-943); no scaffold nesting. So the "member is ignored" / "constructor rejects" / "screen model" grounds all fail.

IT FAILS ON THE README FIDELITY RULE — this is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case:

1. The subject is a WideNavigationRail PARAMETER, not a column's. Upstream (NavigationRailSamples.kt:371-473) `arrangement` positions the rail's items **below a pinned header** — the menu IconButton at line 401 stays anchored at the top while only the destinations move to Center or Bottom. A column's `arrange` moves ALL of its children; you cannot express "header pinned top, destinations at bottom" with one column's arrange at all. The sketch's answer is to delete the header outright, which deletes the very frame that makes the arrangement legible. What is left — three icon/label stacks sitting high or low in a 96x360 box — is a generic column alignment, not a rail arrangement.

2. The build depends on a helper the module holds to be impossible. It says "items are `jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item` from the Collapsed sketch". No such function exists in jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail.el, and WideNavigationRailCollapsedSample is `:unsupported` under `--wide-note` precisely because "no node carries a WideNavigationRailItem's selected state or the active indicator". I confirmed against contract.json that `selected` exists on exactly two node types — `chip` and `month_grid` — neither usable as a rail destination. Upstream's Arrangements items (lines 432-446) are byte-for-byte the Collapsed items: `selected = selectedItem == index` plus the Filled/Outlined icon swap. The claim therefore imports its rail from a sketch that cannot be built, and the triage pass did not flag Collapsed as a false blocker, so its own reasoning is inconsistent.

3. Accepting it breaks the module. NavigationRailBottomAlignSample is `:unsupported` with "bottom-aligning items inside a rail that cannot be drawn demonstrates nothing" — and its subject is literally `arrange "end"` on a column, the exact member invoked here. The claim's logic would flip that example too, yet the triage pass left it alone. The existing reason's clause "a column's arrange member positions body content, not rail destinations" is not circular: it is the same judgment already applied consistently to BottomAlign, and it makes no false wire claim (unlike the "no node has a shape member" class of error the brief warns about).

4. The tabs substitution adds a component the sample does not contain and removes the one it does. RenderTabs (LayoutNodes.kt:436-455) draws a full-width M3 TabRow with a selection indicator on the Navigation-rail example page, and HorizontalPager renders two independently authored static columns. The user never watches an arrangement change; they slide between two pre-baked layouts. Upstream's affordance is a Button whose label is the arrangement to switch TO ("Bottom"/"Center", line 450), mutating one live rail. Also worth noting: `tabs` appears nowhere else in the 41-module catalog outside jetpacs-m3-tabs.el, and no module uses a stateful node as a substitute affordance.

Secondary: `:bg "surface"` resolves to scheme.surface (ColorModel.kt:65), which is the Scaffold's own default container color (Renderer.kt:673 passes no containerColor) — in M3's baseline scheme the rail box would have no visible bounds, so even the geometric read of "inside the rail" is not there.

The blocker stands. What is missing is a node type, not a member: a `navigation_rail` node with a pinned header slot, an arrangement member over its destinations, and per-destination selected state. M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP already lists NavigationRail as available-but-unwrapped, and this sample's point does not survive composition from wrapped nodes.

findings.subject: It exists to demonstrate NavigationRail: a vertical bar of three NavigationRailItems at the leading edge, the first selected (filled glyph inside the active-indicator pill), the others outlined.
findings.evidence: The load-bearing clause "icon_button has no selected member for a NavigationRailItem's active indicator" is true about icon_button and irrelevant: jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:98-131 draws the identical M3 active indicator with a 64x32 `:corner 16 :bg "secondary_container"` box (Attributes.kt:154-161) around an icon, taps via `box.on_tap` (LayoutNodes.kt:200), and the whole navigation-bar module ships that way despite NavigationBar being listed as unwrapped in M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:158-163 exactly like NavigationRail (line 166-169). The scaffold-slot clause is also a non-blocker: a rail is not chrome here, it is the example BODY. Only full-bleed height is unreachable (no fill-height universal attribute, contract.json universal_node_attributes) — cosmetic, not the subject; `:min_height` approximates it.
findings.build_sketch:

    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Home"     "home"     "home"            t)
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Search"   "favorite" "favorite_border" nil)
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Settings" "star"     "star_border"     nil)
    :spacing 12 :align "center")
   :width 80 :min_height 320 :bg "surface")) ; item defn as in the Collapsed sketch,

findings.refuted_note:
The claim's central analogy is factually wrong about WHY the navigation-bar module ships, and the sketch fails the README fidelity rule on the one thing that makes a rail a rail.

1. NAVIGATION-BAR IS NOT A PRECEDENT — THE COMPANION DRAWS THAT BAR'S CONTAINER, NOT THE WIRE. Renderer.kt:717-733 wraps whatever node lands in the `bottom_bar` slot in `Surface(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceContainer, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth())` inside `Box(Modifier.navigationBarsPadding().padding(horizontal = 8.dp, vertical = 6.dp))`, with the comment "A DOCKED bar... the M3 navigation-bar container color makes it read as a band flush with the screen edge, and it owns the system navigation inset". That is why NavigationBarSample is a real recreation: the renderer supplies the M3 NavigationBar container (edge-flush, full-width, surfaceContainer, inset-aware) and jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el only supplies items plus the 64/80dp height. A rail gets none of that. contract.json `node_schema.scaffold.optional` is exactly ["top_bar","body","bottom_bar","fab","floating_toolbar","drawer","snackbar","snackbar_action","on_refresh"] — no side/rail slot — and the `body` slot is rendered by a bare `Box(bodyModifier)` (Renderer.kt:761). The evidence's "the whole navigation-bar module ships that way ... exactly like NavigationRail" is the disanalogy, not the analogy.

2. THE RAIL'S CONTAINER IS UNREACHABLE ON TWO AXES, AND IT IS THE COMPONENT. Compose's NavigationRail is `Surface(color = surfaceContainer) { Column(Modifier.fillMaxHeight().widthIn(min = 80.dp).padding(vertical=...), verticalArrangement = spacedBy(4.dp, Alignment.Top)) }`. (a) Height: NOTHING on the wire fills height. `fill` on row/column is `fillMaxWidth()` only (LayoutNodes.kt:125-129 and 149-151) and `fill_fraction` is `fillMaxWidth(fraction)` only despite the neutral name (Attributes.kt:149-151); no wire-driven fillMaxHeight exists anywhere in render/. Worse, the example body is `:scroll t` (jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457 → verticalScroll, LayoutNodes.kt:149-151), so height constraints there are unbounded and even a hypothetical fill-height member would be a no-op in this screen. `:min_height 320` is a magic number that is short on the tablet/desktop widths the component exists for. (b) Tint: `surface_container` is not a theme role (contract.json theme_roles; jetpacs-widgets.el:67-74), and `:bg "surface"` is the color the screen already is, so the Surface that IS the rail renders invisible. The claim calls the height "cosmetic"; the very next example, NavigationRailBottomAlignSample, exists solely to push items against that full height with a weighted Spacer — it is the component, not a cosmetic.

3. THE SKETCH DOES NOT EVEN PUT IT AT THE LEADING EDGE — THE SUBJECT THE TRIAGE AGENT ITSELF STATED. Every `:build` node is wrapped by core in `(jetpacs-column BODY :scroll t :align "center" :spacing 16 :fill t)` (jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457), i.e. `horizontalAlignment = CenterHorizontally` (LayoutNodes.kt:155-158). A bare 80dp column therefore renders as a centered floating strip. And the one member that could override it is DEAD IN THE RENDERER: `align_self` is in contract.json universal_node_attributes and validated by jetpacs-widgets.el:61,213-215, but a grep of the whole companion module finds it only in a comment (Attributes.kt:6) — `RenderRowChildren`/`RenderColumnChildren` (Renderer.kt:341-357) apply `weight` and nothing else. That is the exact `badge ""` class of bug, and it means the sketch as written cannot be salvaged by adding `:align_self "start"`.

4. THE README RULE AND THE MODULE NORM BOTH SAY NO. NavigationRail is named in the unwrapped list (README:58) and again in "Not node types (do not reach for them)" (README:185). NavigationBar appears in that same forbidden list but is explicitly carved out by the chrome section — ":slots ... Covers ... Navigation bar (as a bottom bar of icon buttons)" (README:207). No such carve-out exists for the rail. Every other unwrapped-component module in the catalog is 100% `:unsupported` — segmented-button (2/2), radio-buttons (2/2), search-bars (3/3), carousel (6/6), navigation-suite-scaffold (2/2) — and radio-buttons is the governing precedent: M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP says RadioButton is "currently achievable via enum_list with multi_select: false", and the module still refuses because the substitute "would substitute the Chips component -- which the catalog already lists -- for the very control this component is about". A vertical column of nav-bar items in the body is the identical substitution: it draws NavigationBarItems in a Column, which is the Navigation bar page the catalog already ships, with the destinations relabelled Home/Search/Settings. That is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case verbatim.

WHAT THE CLAIM GETS RIGHT (and it does not change the verdict): the active indicator IS drawable — jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar.el:103-115 builds it with a box at `:width 64 :height 32 :corner 16 :bg "secondary_container"`, all consumed by Attributes.kt:139-161, and `box.on_tap` is a real clickable (LayoutNodes.kt:200-201). So the current reason string's second clause ("icon_button has no selected member for a NavigationRailItem's active indicator") is a weak clause a reader can refute, and it should be rewritten. But the first clause — "There is no navigation_rail node type on the wire: a full-height column of destinations at the leading edge is not one of the scaffold slots" — is verified correct against contract.json and Renderer.kt and is by itself sufficient. Suggested repair, keeping the example unsupported: "There is no navigation_rail node and no scaffold slot for one: the rail is a full-height surfaceContainer container at the leading edge, and the wire has no height-filling member at all (fill and fill_fraction are fillMaxWidth only) and no surface_container role, so a body column can only fake it with a hard-coded min_height."

findings.subject: It exists to demonstrate one line — `Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))` as the first child of a NavigationRail — pushing the destinations to the bottom of the rail.
findings.evidence: Renderer.kt:337-358: `weightOf` is applied to every column child through ColumnScope.RenderColumnChildren, so a `(jetpacs-with-attrs (jetpacs-spacer) :weight 1)` first child does exactly upstream's job — provided the column has a bounded height (`:height`), since the example body column is `:scroll t` and would otherwise leave the main axis unbounded. The reason ("no navigation_rail node type for the Spacer to push against") collapses once the rail composes; the module even concedes "the weighted spacer is the only half of this sample on the wire" — with the other half now buildable, both halves are.
findings.build_sketch:
(defun jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--bottom-align ()
  (jetpacs-with-attrs
   (jetpacs-column
    ;; "A Spacer that pushes the NavigationRail items to the bottom."
    (jetpacs-with-attrs (jetpacs-spacer) :weight 1)
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Home"     "home"     "home"            t)
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Search"   "favorite" "favorite_border" nil)
    (jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item "Settings" "star"     "star_border"     nil)
    :spacing 12 :align "center")
   :width 80 :height 360 :bg "surface"))  ; bounded height is what gives weight room
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on the README fidelity rule (and on a false premise in the claim's own reasoning).

1. The claim is circular and never establishes its premise. Its argument is "the reason collapses ONCE THE RAIL COMPOSES." The rail does not compose. `navigation_rail` is not among the 39 node types (verified: ebp/contract.json `node_types` has zero entries matching "rail" or "nav"), and the scaffold's optional members are exactly `top_bar body bottom_bar fab floating_toolbar drawer snackbar snackbar_action on_refresh` — no leading/side slot for a full-height rail. The adjacent, uncontested `NavigationRailSample` (same file, same three items, identical minus one Spacer) is `:unsupported` for exactly that reason. Accepting this claim would put two neighbouring examples in the catalog where the plain rail is declared undrawable and its one-line variant is declared drawable from the same nodes.

2. The cited evidence disproves something nobody claimed. Renderer.kt:337-358 (`weightOf` -> `ColumnScope.RenderColumnChildren`, LayoutNodes.kt:160) does apply `Modifier.weight` to column children, and `"spacer" -> Spacer(m.width(0.dp).height(0.dp))` at Renderer.kt:298-300 does not defeat it (weight's fill=true hands the child fixed constraints, and `.height(0.dp)` is enforce-incoming, so it constrains back to the allocated slot). The elisp accepts it too (`jetpacs-widgets.el:60` lists `:weight` universal, `:198` validates it as a positive finite number; `jetpacs-spacer` at :832 takes no args and is sized by universal attrs). So the weighted spacer works — which is precisely what the existing reason already concedes ("the weighted spacer is the only half of this sample on the wire"). The claim refutes the half of the reason that was never in dispute.

3. The sketch does not demonstrate the subject; it demonstrates `column` + `weight`. Upstream (NavigationRailSamples.kt:503-527) `NavigationRail` is fillMaxHeight leading-edge chrome, so "pushes the destinations to the bottom of the rail" means the bottom edge of the screen. The sketch replaces the rail with `:width 80 :height 360` — an invented box, rendered by jetpacs-m3-core.el:454-457 inside `(jetpacs-column … :scroll t :align "center" :fill t)`, i.e. floating in the middle of a scrolling body. "The bottom" becomes a number the author picked, not the rail's extent. What renders is a grey 80x360 rectangle with three icon/label pairs at its lower edge — indistinguishable in kind from `(jetpacs-column … :arrange "end" :height 360)`, and carrying no rail. That is the `ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample` case named in README:35-52: something vaguely similar draws, but the thing the sample exists to show does not.

4. The sketch as written does not even build: `jetpacs-m3-navigation-rail--item` does not exist anywhere in emacs/ (grep is empty; only `jetpacs-m3-navigation-bar--item` exists). The builder would signal void-function and land in jetpacs-m3--guard's "Sample failed to build" card. Porting navigation-bar's helper is possible visually (it fakes the active indicator with a `box :bg "secondary_container"`), but navigation-bar's samples are supported because they claim the scaffold's real `bottom_bar` SLOT — chrome rendered where upstream chrome lives. There is no analogous slot for a rail, which is the whole distinction the module documents at lines 11-32.

Every clause of the existing reason checks out against the Kotlin and the contract; it is accurate and, if anything, generous to the wire.

The sample's subject is code-level extensibility (supplying suspend animation behavior), which no describable JSON member carries; the nearest reasonable extension would be a canned spring parameter object, which is not what the sample demonstrates. findings.subject: It exists to demonstrate hoisting isRefreshing out of the composable into a ViewModel: the indicator, the list contents, and the Refresh button's enabled flag all read one owned state.

missing.name: scaffold.is_refreshing
missing.detail: boolean, default false. With it, on_refresh fires -> Emacs pushes is_refreshing t plus a disabled refresh button and an empty list -> Emacs pushes is_refreshing :json-false with the new items, which is this sample verbatim.

findings.evidence: Two of the three consumers of isRefreshing DO reach the wire: `icon_button.enabled` exists (contract.json chip/icon_button schema; InputNodes.kt:99-114 consumes it) and the list contents are just the next snapshot, so "the ViewModel-held isRefreshing ... never reaches the wire" overstates it — Emacs is precisely the ViewModel here and re-pushes the gated surface. What is genuinely missing is only the third consumer: Renderer.kt:746-750 keeps `refreshing` in Companion-local state that self-clears after a hardcoded 1200ms delay, so the spinner cannot reflect Emacs's state. (Note also the module commentary attributes "there is no completion signal" to SPEC 17.6; that sentence is in Renderer.kt:643-651, not SPEC.md.)

findings.evidence: "cannot be requested from Emacs" is false: SPEC.md:2698-2705 and contract.json:704-708 already define `dialog.show` with `style` = dialog | sheet | sheet_full, and ebp.el:1985-2003 (`ebp-client-dialog-show ... :style`) already sends it — the sheet is a declared wire form. missing.detail: string enum "start" (default) | "end"; RenderMenu hoists a rememberScrollState(), passes it as DropdownMenu(scrollState = …) and runs LaunchedEffect(open) { if (open && initial_scroll == "end") state.scrollTo(state.maxValue) } — the literal upstream LaunchedEffect. The universal `scroll_here` (SPEC.md:2177) cannot stand in twice over: MenuItems are records, not Nodes (SPEC.md:2426), so no universal attribute attaches to them, and the renderer honours scroll_here only for direct lazy_column children (LayoutNodes.kt:233-244). The 30 items themselves DO scroll natively — only the opening position is unreachable.

Renderer.kt:363-437 RenderTextInput is a bare OutlinedTextField with no menuAnchor and no read_only member (contract.json:347-368 lists text_input's members; `enabled: false` greys the field out, which is not readOnly). The nearest composition — row(text_input, menu) — fails on three counts: the popup anchors to the icon rather than spanning the field, tapping the field raises the keyboard instead of opening the menu, and the field cannot be made read-only. docs/lookup-tables/M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:83 and :142-146 list ExposedDropdownMenu as available-but-unwrapped and already propose a `dropdown` wire type.

The real gaps are exactly two: the field-anchored popup and the rich option label.
