findings.subject: A single-choice segmented button: three options (Day/Month/Week) fused into one connected track by SegmentedButtonDefaults.itemShape(index,count), with exactly one selected and the selected item carrying the check glyph.
findings.evidence: companion/app/src/main/kotlin/com/calebc42/ebp/companion/render/Attributes.kt:92-109 (cornerShape reads the per-corner object top_start/top_end/bottom_end/bottom_start -> RoundedCornerShape), Attributes.kt:158-167 (clip, bg and border ALL stroke/fill with that same per-corner shape), LayoutNodes.kt:186-204 (box consumes alignment + on_tap), Renderer.kt:341-348 (row children consume weight), SPEC.md:2189-2192 (Corner object is universal), ebp/contract.json:57 (corner/border/bg/clip/weight/height are universal attributes). Precedent in-tree: emacs/apps/m3-catalog/jetpacs-m3-lists.el:114-128 builds ListItemDefaults.segmentedShapes this exact way, and jetpacs-m3-split-button.el:55-85 builds the fused SplitButton halves this exact way. The reason's claim that "the connected Day/Month/Week track ... cannot be asked for from Emacs" and the module commentary's "the only shape member on the wire is surface's rounded/rounded_small/circle enum, which has no start, middle or end form" (jetpacs-m3-segmented-button.el:32-33) are both false: start/middle/end shape math IS the per-corner `corner` attribute. The one true clause is that no node holds a live selected-segment state, but the catalog already accepts authored selection as a recreation (jetpacs-m3-chips.el:28-33, 111-135 ships FilterChip samples with :selected authored).
findings.build_sketch:
One segment = a `box` (alignment center, on_tap -> jetpacs-m3-demo) wrapped in jetpacs-with-attrs :weight 1 :height 40 :clip t :border (:width 1 :color "outline"), plus :corner (:top_start 20 :bottom_start 20) on the first, no corner on the middles, :corner (:top_end 20 :bottom_end 20) on the last (20 = SegmentedButtonDefaults 50% of a 40dp track); the selected one adds :bg "secondary_container". Segment content is a `row` (:spacing 8 :align "center") of an optional `icon` "check" :size 18 and a `text` label, colored on_secondary_container when selected else on_surface. Three of those in one `jetpacs-row ... :fill t :align "center"` (NO :arrange -- LayoutNodes.kt:99-108 discards spacing on any non-start arrange; here spacing must stay 0 so the segments abut). Concretely:

(defun jetpacs-m3-segmented-button--item (label index count selected &optional icon)
  (let* ((r 20)
         (corner (cond ((= index 0) (list :top_start r :bottom_start r))
                       ((= index (1- count)) (list :top_end r :bottom_end r))))
         (fg (if selected "on_secondary_container" "on_surface"))
         (glyph (if selected "check" icon)))
    (apply #'jetpacs-with-attrs
           (jetpacs-box
            (apply #'jetpacs-row
                   (append (when glyph (list (jetpacs-icon glyph :size 18 :color fg)))
                           (list (jetpacs-text label :style "label" :color fg))
                           (list :spacing 8 :align "center")))
            :alignment "center" :on-tap (jetpacs-m3-demo label))
           (append (list :weight 1 :height 40 :clip t
                         :border (list :width 1 :color "outline"))
                   (when corner (list :corner corner))
                   (when selected (list :bg "secondary_container"))))))

(defun jetpacs-m3-segmented-button--single ()
  "Upstream SegmentedButtonSingleSelectSample."
  (let* ((options '("Day" "Month" "Week")) (n (length options)))
    (apply #'jetpacs-row
           (append (cl-loop for l in options for i from 0
                            collect (jetpacs-m3-segmented-button--item l i n (= i 0)))
                   (list :fill t :align "center")))))

I byte-evaluated this against emacs/jetpacs-widgets.el: it passes every constructor/attribute validator and serializes canonically (row > 3 boxes with corner objects, border, bg, weight, height, clip, on_tap). What is lost is only the live toggle -- selectedIndex is authored, taps pop the demo snackbar -- which is exactly how the Chips page recreates FilterChip ("a filter chip recreates as ONE state of the upstream toggle", jetpacs-m3-chips.el:28-33). enum_list is indeed the wrong answer (it renders FlowRow(FilterChip), InputNodes.kt:306-343), but it is not the only answer.
findings.refuted_note:
The sketch is mechanically clean — I byte-built it (emacs -Q --batch against emacs/jetpacs-widgets.el) and it serializes to row > 3 boxes with corner/border/bg/clip/weight/height/on_tap, every member present in ebp/contract.json and every one consumed by the Kotlin (Attributes.kt:92-109 per-corner cornerShape, :154-167 clip/bg/border all stroke with that shape, LayoutNodes.kt:186-204 box alignment + on_tap, Renderer.kt:341-348 row-child weight, ContentNodes.kt:244-262 icon size/color, :152-184 text style/color; "check" is pre-seeded in IconMap.kt). The triage agent is also right that two clauses of the shipped reason are FALSE: per-corner :corner does express itemShape's start/middle/end radii, and jetpacs-m3-segmented-button.el:32-33's "the only shape member on the wire is surface's rounded/rounded_small/circle enum" is flatly contradicted by jetpacs--corner-keys (jetpacs-widgets.el:189) and by split-button.el:29-34 saying so in as many words. But the example is still not a false blocker — it fails the README fidelity rule, on three counts.

(1) THE REPO HAS ALREADY DECIDED THIS EXACT CASE, IN THE FILE THE CLAIM CITES AS ITS PRECEDENT. jetpacs-m3-lists.el:59 defines jetpacs-m3-lists--single-selection-note — "There is no radio_button node type and no container node carries a selected member: this sample exists to make a whole list row one exclusive choice that recolors when it wins" — and applies it to BOTH single-selection samples, including SingleSelectionSegmentedListItemSample (lists.el:357-362), i.e. a segmented, single-choice sample marked unsupported by the same module that owns jetpacs-m3-lists--segment-corner (lists.el:113-121), the per-corner helper the claim invokes as proof. MultiSelectionListItemSample is :build only because checkbox is a real stateful node (lists.el:24-28). SegmentedButtonSingleSelectSample is that sample: N options, exactly one wins, the winner recolors — M3 even gives each segment `.semantics { role = Role.RadioButton }` inside `.selectableGroup()` (SegmentedButton.kt:239, :336). Accepting the sketch requires overturning two shipped lists verdicts. split-button.el says the same thing from the other side: the fused geometry composes, and eleven of twelve samples are STILL unsupported "on the checked state each of them needs"; the one recreated is the one with no checked state anywhere.

(2) THE CHIPS PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER. chips' :selected is a real member of a real wrapped node — InputNodes.kt:119-131 renders FilterChip(selected = node.boolOr("selected")), so Emacs sends a snapshot of M3's own selected state and the Companion draws M3's own selected visual. That is what jetpacs-m3-chips.el:28-33 means by "authored presentation state ... ONE state of the upstream toggle". The sketch sends no selected member at all: the wire carries bg:"secondary_container" and one extra icon child that the author hand-painted onto a box. That is a picture of a selected segment, not a state of a toggle. By the sketch's own logic SingleSelectionListItemSample is equally recreatable (paint one row's bg, draw a circle for the radio) — which the catalog explicitly refuses.

(3) THE "CONNECTED TRACK" IS THE PART THAT DOESN'T RENDER. SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow fuses with `horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(-space)`, space = SegmentedButtonDefaults.BorderWidth, plus interactionZIndex — the KDoc at SegmentedButton.kt:350-352 says "It handles overlapping items so that strokes of the item are correctly on top of each other". The overlap is what makes one shared 1dp seam. Negative spacing is unaskable: jetpacs-widgets.el:739 validates row :spacing with min 0, and safeDp (Attributes.kt:40-41) rejects negatives anyway. So the sketch draws three independently-stroked boxes whose interior seams double to 2dp — three outlined boxes abutting, not one connected track, which is precisely the headline the claim says it delivers.

Verdict stands as :unsupported. The reason STRING should be rewritten, though — it currently asserts something false about shape and would be false product text either way. Something like: "No node carries a selected-segment state and there is no segmented_button node type: this sample exists to make Day/Month/Week one exclusive choice inside a single connected track, and while the per-corner corner attribute can round the first and last segment, nothing on the wire moves the selection or overlaps the adjacent 1dp strokes that SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow fuses with Arrangement.spacedBy(-BorderWidth)." That is also consistent with jetpacs-m3-lists--single-selection-note.

findings.subject: A multi-choice segmented button: three options in one connected track where each option's icon slot shows that option's own icon while unchecked and a checkmark while checked (SegmentedButtonDefaults.Icon(active = index in checkedList)).
findings.evidence: Same wire facts as the single-select sample: Attributes.kt:92-109 + :158-167 (per-corner corner honored by clip/bg/border), LayoutNodes.kt:186-204 (box alignment/on_tap), Renderer.kt:341-348 (weight). The reason's second clause -- "no node carries a per-option icon slot" -- is true only of `enum_list` (contract.json node_schema enum_list options are {label,value} only, and InputNodes.kt:310-325 renders label text alone); it is false of a hand-composed segment, whose content is arbitrary child nodes, so an `icon` child IS the per-option icon slot. Icon names star_border, trending_up, bookmark_border and check all resolve (docs/lookup-tables/M3-ICON-REFERENCE.org). Only the crossfade ANIMATION between the two glyphs is Companion-side, and §16.4 (SPEC.md:2149-2156) explicitly does not require animation parity.
findings.build_sketch:
Identical helper to the single-select sketch, called with the upstream strings and icons and a checkedList that is authored non-empty so BOTH branches of SegmentedButtonDefaults.Icon are visible side by side in one snapshot:

(defun jetpacs-m3-segmented-button--multi ()
  "Upstream SegmentedButtonMultiSelectSample."
  (let* ((options '(("Favorites" . "star_border")
                    ("Trending"  . "trending_up")
                    ("Saved"     . "bookmark_border")))
         (n (length options))
         (checked '(0)))                ; authored checkedList
    (apply #'jetpacs-row
           (append (cl-loop for (label . icon) in options for i from 0
                            collect (jetpacs-m3-segmented-button--item
                                     label i n (memq i checked) icon))
                   (list :fill t :align "center")))))

Checked segment: :bg "secondary_container" + icon "check"; unchecked segments keep their own icon (star_border / trending_up / bookmark_border) over the bare outlined track -- which is precisely what SegmentedButtonDefaults.Icon(active=) draws in each state. Taps are (jetpacs-m3-demo LABEL). If strict fidelity to the sample's initial state is preferred, author checked = '() and all three show their own icons; the mixed authoring demonstrates more of the sample's subject in one frame.
findings.refuted_note:
REFUTED on four independent grounds; any one is sufficient.

(1) THE SKETCH DOES NOT EXIST AND CANNOT BE CHECKED. `jetpacs-m3-segmented-button--item` is referenced but defined nowhere: `grep -rn "segmented-button--item"` over llm-poc-2 returns zero hits (the only `segmented_button` hits are the two reason strings and M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:192). The claim's load-bearing member set (`:corner`, `:border`, `:bg`, `:weight`, box `:on-tap`) lives entirely inside that unwritten helper, so the "claimed build" is not a build.

(2) THE CONNECTED TRACK IS NOT REACHABLE — and this is the part the claim waves through as solved by per-corner `:corner`. Per-corner corner is real (Attributes.kt:92-109, honored by clip/bg/border at :154-167), but it only rounds each box's own outline. Compose's `SingleChoice/MultiChoiceSegmentedButtonRow` fuses the track with `Arrangement.spacedBy(-space)` — NEGATIVE spacing equal to `SegmentedButtonDefaults.BorderWidth` — so adjacent 1dp outlines overlap into one hairline. The wire cannot ask for that twice over: `jetpacs-row` validates `(jetpacs--check-number spacing ":spacing" 0 nil)` (jetpacs-widgets.el:735-ish, min 0), and even a nonconforming negative dies at the renderer, since `horizontalArrange` (LayoutNodes.kt:99-107) computes `safeDp(node.doubleOr("spacing", 0.0)) ?: 0f` and `safeDp` (Attributes.kt:40-41) rejects anything `< 0f`. Nor can a side be dropped: `:border` is validated to exactly `{:width :color}` (jetpacs--check-attr, `:border` arm) and `Modifier.border(width, color, shape)` strokes the whole perimeter. Best case is three abutting fully-outlined boxes with a DOUBLED 2dp rule at every interior seam — three adjoined buttons, not one track. The module's own commentary is correct that "that fusing IS the control".

(3) FIDELITY — this is the ButtonWithAnimatedShapeSample case exactly. Upstream's subject is `checked = index in checkedList` + `onCheckedChange` toggling it, with `SegmentedButtonDefaults.Icon(active = index in checkedList)` DERIVED from that state. The claim's own words give it away: `checkedList` starts EMPTY upstream, so the sketch must fabricate `checked '(0)` — a state the sample never shows — to "demonstrate more of the sample's subject in one frame". A frame is not the subject. Every catalog tap is `(jetpacs-m3-demo LABEL)`, which is `(jetpacs-action "m3catalog.demo" :args (list :message …))` — a snackbar, nothing else (jetpacs-m3-core.el:208-212), and README rule 5 forbids a component module registering any other action. `box.on_tap` (LayoutNodes.kt:186-204) dispatches an action and holds no state; `box`/`row`/`icon`/`text` have no checked member anywhere in contract.json node_schema. So on device the checkmark can never appear or disappear: tapping "Trending" pops a toast and the icons stay frozen. That ships a still photograph of a multi-choice control as a working one. The §16.4 cite is misapplied — 16.4 excuses ANIMATION/pixel parity while explicitly requiring "declared semantic structure … enabled state, interaction hooks" be preserved; what is missing here is the state that drives `active`, not the crossfade.

(4) HOUSE PRECEDENT MAKES IT SELF-CONTRADICTORY. jetpacs-m3-togglebuttons.el marks all ten samples unsupported for precisely this, and states the rule the claim breaks: `chip` "has a `selected` member but no id, so its state is authored from Emacs and a tap can never flip it." Its ToggleButtonWithIconSample reason is the identical construct — "the Filled/Outlined Edit swap this sample drives from checked cannot be expressed." `SegmentedButtonDefaults.Icon(active =)` IS a checked-driven icon swap. Calling it supported here while it is unsupported there would put contradictory product text in front of the same user.

One concession to the claim: the reason string's second clause is sloppily worded. Per-option icons DO exist on the wire (tab_item `:icon`, `chip :icon`), and `enum_list` really is label-only (InputNodes.kt:310-325, `label = { Text(opt.stringOr("label")) }`, options `{label,value}` per node_schema). The clause is true of enum_list but overstated as written and should be re-pointed at the checked state. That is a copy fix, not a verdict change — the example stays `:unsupported`.

findings.subject: The multi-browse carousel strategy: a preferred 186dp item measured large, then medium, then small toward each edge, every item re-measured and re-masked on every scroll frame.

missing.name: carousel
missing.detail: children: Node[] (the items); `strategy`: "multi_browse" | "uncontained" | "centered_hero" | "multi_aspect"; `preferred_item_width` (dp, multi_browse), `item_width` (dp, uncontained), `item_spacing` (dp), `content_padding` (dp); optional `id` so the scroll/snap position is Companion-local presentation state under §16.1, and optional `on_item_tap` (index injected as args.value, §14.3). The Companion runs the keyline math -- large/medium/small measurement and the per-frame mask -- exactly as `tabs` owns its pager and `collapsible` its expansion; Emacs authors the item nodes once and never learns the width.

findings.evidence: ebp/contract.json:16 lists all 39 node types -- no carousel, no lazy_row; the only horizontally scrolling container is `row` with `scroll` (contract.json:166 row schema = spacing/align/arrange/scroll/fill; LayoutNodes.kt:122-143 renders it as Row + horizontalScroll with no snap, no keyline, no per-frame item measurement, and with weights explicitly dropped in the scroll arm at LayoutNodes.kt:140). Nothing in Attributes.kt makes a child's size a function of scroll offset. The reason string is factually correct on every clause.

findings.subject: The uncontained strategy: items pinned at exactly 186dp that keep their size and scroll off the container edge, with the fling settling on an item.

missing.name: row.snap
missing.detail: string enum "none" | "start" | "center", default "none", meaningful only with `scroll: true`. The Companion attaches a snapping fling behavior that settles the scroll with a child's leading edge (start) or center (center) at the viewport's corresponding edge -- i.e. rememberSnapFlingBehavior over the row's scroll state. No new state channel: the position stays Companion-local presentation state like tabs' page.

missing.name: row.content_padding
missing.detail: non-negative dp, default 0, meaningful only with `scroll: true`: padding applied INSIDE the scroll viewport so it scrolls with the content (PaddingValues), unlike the universal `padding`, which RenderRow applies outside the scroll modifier. This is what upstream's contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 16.dp) means; without it the first/last item sit flush at the viewport edge while scrolling. Cosmetic relative to `snap`.

findings.evidence: The reason asserts "a scrolling row has no item width and no snap position". The first half is FALSE: `width`/`height` are universal (contract.json:57; Attributes.kt:139-140 applies them) and RenderImage explicitly takes the width+height pair as Modifier.size (ContentNodes.kt:82-94), so `image :width 186 :height 205` is exactly the uncontained item size; the extraLarge maskClip of a non-resizing item is a static rounded clip, which is `:corner 28 :clip t` (Attributes.kt:92-109 + :158). What is genuinely absent is snap: LayoutNodes.kt:122-143 renders `row :scroll` as a plain horizontalScroll with no snapFlingBehavior, and `row`'s schema (contract.json:166) has no snap or content_padding member (universal `padding` sits OUTSIDE the scroll viewport because RenderRow appends horizontalScroll after modifier.universal). So this is the one carousel sample that is a single named member away, not a node away.

findings.subject: The centered-hero strategy: one large item held in the center of the container with a small item peeking at each edge, re-masked as the user scrolls.

missing.name: carousel
missing.detail: As for the multi-browse sample, with `strategy: "centered_hero"`: the Companion holds one item at the container center at full size and lays a small anchor item at each edge, re-measuring per scroll frame. Members: children (items), strategy, item_spacing, content_padding, optional id (Companion-local snap position) and on_item_tap.

findings.evidence: ebp/contract.json:16 (no carousel node) and contract.json:166 + LayoutNodes.kt:99-143: `row` offers only spacing/align/arrange/scroll/fill; `arrange: "center"` centers the whole child sequence and, per LayoutNodes.kt:99-108, silently discards spacing while doing so -- it cannot hold ONE child centered while the rest scroll past it, and nothing re-sizes the edge items into peeking anchors. The reason string is correct.

findings.subject: Custom item content drawn against the carousel item's own live mask: two independently maskClip'd/maskBorder'd images stacked in items 1 and 4, and elsewhere a chip whose alpha and translationX are lerped every scroll frame from carouselItemDrawInfo.size / maxSize / maskRect.left.

missing.name: carousel
missing.detail: The base node (children/strategy/preferred_item_width/item_spacing/content_padding/id), whose Companion-side implementation owns the per-frame item mask.

missing.name: carousel.item_mask
missing.detail: Object {corner: number|Corner, border?: {width,color}} applied by the Companion to each item's LIVE mask rectangle rather than to its layout bounds -- the wire form of maskClip(shape)/maskBorder(stroke, shape). A per-child override (the same member on a carousel child) covers items 1 and 4, which mask two stacked images independently.

missing.name: carousel.item_overlay
missing.detail: A Node drawn over an item and pinned by the Companion to the item's mask rect, fading in as the mask coverage approaches the item's full width -- declarative intent for exactly the graphicsLayer { alpha = lerp(...); translationX = maskRect.left + 8.dp } this sample is named for. Emacs can only declare it; it can never compute it, because no wire message reports per-frame geometry.

findings.evidence: contract.json:16 (no carousel node); contract.json:112 image schema = url + content_description + content_scale only, and RenderImage (ContentNodes.kt:68-117) consumes nothing mask-shaped. Nuance worth recording: the STATIC analogues of maskClip/maskBorder do exist as universal attributes -- `corner` + `clip` + `border` all stroke and fill with the same shape (Attributes.kt:92-109, :158-167) -- so the reason's "the image node also has no mask member" is true only of the DYNAMIC, scroll-driven mask, which is the one this sample needs. The chip fade is unreachable in principle from Emacs: the lerp inputs exist only per frame on device, and no wire message carries geometry back (SPEC.md:3335 device report has no layout metrics).

findings.subject: Pairing a multi-browse carousel with a "Show all" text button that overflows the same five items into a two-column grid page, with back returning to the carousel.

missing.name: carousel
missing.detail: The multi-browse carousel this sample overflows FROM (children/strategy/preferred_item_width/item_spacing/content_padding). No other addition is required: the button, the grid page and the back navigation are already expressible.

findings.evidence: Everything in this sample EXCEPT the carousel already composes: the "Show all" TextButton is `button :variant "text"` (InputNodes.kt:89-94), the two-column LazyVerticalGrid is a lazy_column of rows of two weighted children (the pattern jetpacs-m3-core.el:304-317 already uses for the Home grid), the placeholder Boxes are `box :bg "surface_variant" :corner 16`, and the page navigation is an ordinary screen push with the chrome back arrow. So the reason's "with no carousel node there is nothing for the button to overflow from" is exactly right -- the missing piece is only the carousel itself. contract.json:16 confirms no carousel node.

findings.subject: MultiAspectCarouselScope over a lazy row of items 305, 205, 275, 350 and 100dp wide, each keeping its own aspect and masked through its own MultiAspectCarouselItemDrawInfo as it crosses the container edges.

missing.name: carousel
missing.detail: With `strategy: "multi_aspect"`, each child keeping its own universal `width` as its main-axis size, plus `item_spacing`/`content_padding` and an optional `id` for the Companion-local snap position; the Companion derives each item's MultiAspectCarouselItemDrawInfo and clips the child to it per frame.

missing.name: carousel.item_mask
missing.detail: Object {corner: number|Corner, border?: {width,color}} applied to the item's live mask rect (the wire form of maskClip(shape, drawInfo)); without it the multi-aspect items are drawn with a static rounded clip that never reacts to the scroll.

findings.evidence: The per-item widths are NOT the gap -- `width` is universal (contract.json:57, Attributes.kt:139) and RenderImage sizes on width+height (ContentNodes.kt:88-90), so a `row :scroll t` of five images at 305/205/275/350/100dp with `:corner 28 :clip t` reproduces the resting frame exactly. The gap is the per-item live mask and the snapping lazy row: contract.json:16 has no carousel and no lazy_row, and LayoutNodes.kt:122-143 gives `row :scroll` no snap and no scroll-driven clipping. The reason string states this correctly.

findings.subject: A list-detail pane scaffold that shows list and detail side by side on an expanded window and collapses to one pane with a navigator on a phone -- the automatic adaptation IS the sample.

missing.name: pane_scaffold
missing.detail: Named pane children -- `list` + `detail` (+ optional `extra`) for the list-detail form and `main` + `supporting` (+ `extra`) for the supporting form -- each a Node; optional `id` so the pane navigator/adapted value is Companion-local presentation state under §16.1, and optional `on_pane_change` (the newly active pane role injected as args.value, §14.3) so Emacs can re-author pane content. The Companion computes the M3 scaffold directive from its own window (calculatePaneScaffoldDirective) and decides how many panes are expanded; Emacs sends every pane in one snapshot. No window-size-class wire message is needed for this sample.

findings.evidence: contract.json:16 (39 node types, none of them a pane scaffold) and contract.json:494 (scaffold's optional members are top_bar, body, bottom_bar, fab, floating_toolbar, drawer, snackbar, snackbar_action, on_refresh -- named chrome slots, no pane roles), rendered as written at Renderer.kt:654-775. Every clause of the reason is factually true. One qualification and one nit: (a) the reason's second half ("no wire message reports the window size class to Emacs") is true -- SPEC.md:3335-3350 device report carries caps/permissions/trigger and state types and NO layout metric, contract.json state_types has no size type, and docs/lookup-tables/ADAPTIVE-REFERENCE.org:11,38 confirms device_state_update and jetpacs-responsive are PROPOSALS -- but it is not actually a REQUIREMENT for this sample: a `pane_scaffold` node would adapt Companion-side from its own window measurement, exactly as `tabs` owns its selected page and `collapsible` its expansion (SPEC.md:2330-2402, §16.4 at SPEC.md:2149-2156 blesses native adaptation), with Emacs authoring all panes once and never learning the width. Only the node is load-bearing. (b) the slot enumeration omits snackbar_action.

findings.subject: Three panes (list, detail, extra) plus a user-draggable pane split: PaneExpansionAnchors of proportion 0, offset 240dp from start, proportion 0.5, offset 240dp from end, proportion 1, with a VerticalDragHandle the user drags between them.

missing.name: pane_scaffold
missing.detail: As above, with the third `extra` pane role populated.

missing.name: pane_scaffold.pane_expansion
missing.detail: Object {anchors: [{proportion: 0..1} | {offset_start: dp} | {offset_end: dp}, ...], initial_index: integer, drag_handle: boolean}. The Companion draws a VerticalDragHandle on the seam, drags the split between the authored anchors and keeps the settled anchor as Companion-local presentation state keyed on §16.1 identity (the same rule as collapsible.collapsed at SPEC.md:2367-2373). No dispatch is required for the sample to work.

findings.evidence: contract.json:16 / :494 as above -- no pane scaffold, no pane roles, and no drag-handle or expansion member anywhere in node_schema; the only drag mechanic the renderer implements is reorderable_list's vertical item drag (LayoutNodes.kt:622-747) and the swipe sides (LayoutNodes.kt:267-326), neither of which re-splits a layout. The reason names both halves correctly.

findings.subject: AdaptStrategy.Levitate applied to the extra pane only when the window is single-pane: the extra pane floats centered over the scaffold behind a LevitatedPaneScrim whose tap navigates the pane back.

missing.name: pane_scaffold
missing.detail: As above, with the extra pane role.

missing.name: pane_scaffold.adapt_strategy
missing.detail: Object mapping a pane role to "hide" | "reflow" | "levitate" (default hide), where levitate takes {alignment: the 9-value box alignment vocabulary, scrim: boolean, only_if_single_pane: boolean}. The Companion floats that pane over the scaffold at the given alignment behind a dismissing scrim, and a scrim tap pops the pane's own history (Companion-local) rather than dispatching -- i.e. AdaptStrategy.Levitate(...).onlyIfSinglePane(directive) expressed as one member.

findings.evidence: contract.json:16 has no pane scaffold and no dialog node; a dialog reaches the screen only through the `dialog.show` METHOD (contract.json methods; SPEC.md:1226 routes it through the surfaces.dialog capability; the elisp seam is ebp-client-dialog-show at emacs/ebp.el:1985), never as a node a tree can place -- so the reason is factually true. Worth recording alongside it: the wire DOES own a modal presentation channel with a style enum dialog|sheet|sheet_full (contract.json:605 enums "dialog.style"), so a scrimmed modal per se is not off the wire -- what is off the wire is a modal that is a PANE of a scaffold, chosen by the scaffold's own adapt strategy and dismissed into its pane history. (docs/AUDIT-w7-conformance.md:354 also records dialog.show `style` as neither validated nor honored today.)

findings.subject: A supporting-pane scaffold: main content with a 200dp supporting pane beside it on an expanded window, collapsing to one pane on a phone, plus an extra pane reachable from the main pane.

missing.name: pane_scaffold
missing.detail: The supporting-pane role set: `main` + `supporting` (+ `extra`), each a Node, with the Companion deciding from its own window how many are expanded and the pane navigator kept as Companion-local presentation state under an optional `id`.

findings.evidence: Identical wire facts to ListDetailPaneScaffoldSample (this example shares the same jetpacs-m3-adaptive--pane-note constant, jetpacs-m3-adaptive.el:51-53): contract.json:16 has no pane scaffold, contract.json:494 / Renderer.kt:654-775 gives the scaffold only chrome slots. Same qualification: the window-size-class half of the reason is a true fact (SPEC.md:3335 device report has no layout metric) but not a requirement -- the adaptation would be Companion-side inside the node. Same nit: the slot enumeration omits snackbar_action.

findings.subject: AdaptStrategy.Levitate with Alignment.BottomCenter and a rememberDragToResizeState(dockedEdge = Bottom): in a single-pane layout the extra pane docks to the bottom edge as a drag-resizable sheet with a BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle.

missing.name: pane_scaffold
missing.detail: The supporting-pane role set (main/supporting/extra) as above.

missing.name: pane_scaffold.adapt_strategy
missing.detail: The same levitate object as the dialog sample, extended with {docked_edge: "bottom" | "top" | "start" | "end", drag_to_resize: boolean}: the Companion docks the levitated pane to that edge, draws the M3 drag handle, and lets the user resize it, keeping the size as Companion-local presentation state. Alternative (coarser) route, already sketched by M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:122-129: a `bottom_sheet` node or a `scaffold.bottom_sheet` slot with a peek height -- but that carries the sheet, not the pane-adaptation this sample is about.

findings.evidence: contract.json:16 has neither a pane scaffold nor a bottom_sheet node, and docs/lookup-tables/M3-COMPONENT-LOOKUP.org:73,122-129 does list BottomSheetScaffold/ModalBottomSheet as Available-not-Wrapped, so the reason's facts hold. The one over-reach is "has nothing on the wire to carry it": contract.json:605 enums "dialog.style" includes sheet and sheet_full, so a bottom-sheet PRESENTATION exists as a §18.1 dialog verb (docs/AUDIT-w7-conformance.md:354 notes the style is currently ignored by the Companion). It is still not a pane, not drag-resizable, and not selected by an adapt strategy -- so the verdict stands.

findings.subject: Comparing the four BackNavigationBehaviors (PopUntilScaffoldValueChange, PopUntilCurrentDestinationChange, PopUntilContentChange, PopLatest) over a NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold's OWN pane history, chosen on a welcome screen first.

missing.name: pane_scaffold
missing.detail: The list/detail/extra node with an `id` under which the Companion keeps the pane back stack as presentation state.

missing.name: pane_scaffold.back_behavior
missing.detail: String enum "pop_until_scaffold_value_change" | "pop_until_current_destination_change" | "pop_until_content_change" | "pop_latest", default the first. The Companion consumes a back gesture INSIDE the node while its pane history is non-empty, rewinding by the named rule, and only lets back fall through to the surface's view/screen stack when the node can no longer navigate back -- which is the behavioral difference the four options exist to demonstrate.

findings.evidence: contract.json:16 (no pane scaffold, hence no pane history to rewind) and the EBP back model: back is the `view.switch` builtin bound to the chrome back arrow (emacs/jetpacs-chrome.el:14, :79-97, :243), Emacs owns the screen stack, and the Companion implements no system-back handler at all (no BackHandler anywhere under companion/app/src/main/kotlin). So "EBP back pops whole screens off the chrome stack, so the four behaviors this sample exists to compare have nothing to act on" is accurate. Note the welcome screen itself is fully buildable (the four RadioButtonRows are an `enum_list` with multi_select absent, InputNodes.kt:245-343, plus a `button`), so the missing piece is only the scaffold and its back rule.

findings.subject: A Navigation 3 back stack whose entries carry list/detail/extra pane metadata, with ListDetailSceneStrategy composing them into the panes of ONE window (including a detail placeholder when only the list entry is on the stack).

missing.name: pane_scaffold
missing.detail: list/detail/extra Node slots + optional `id`; the Companion measures the window and expands the panes that fit, so Emacs's chrome layer can map its own screen stack onto pane roles the way ListDetailSceneStrategy maps NavKeys.

missing.name: pane_scaffold.on_pane_change
missing.detail: ActionDescriptor dispatched when the active pane role changes (role injected as args.value, §14.3), so Emacs can keep its screen stack and the Companion's pane navigator in step -- the wire equivalent of the back stack driving the scene. Alternative, heavier route: extend the app surface spec so `views` may carry a pane role and be presented side by side, which would be a genuine NEEDS_PROTOCOL change; the node route avoids it.

findings.evidence: contract.json:16 (no pane scaffold) and the EBP navigation model: a surface's app variant carries `views` + `initial_view` with one view presented at a time and `view.switch` moving between them (contract.json surface_spec_variants; emacs/jetpacs-chrome.el:14-25, :225-250), so today the wire offers only a linear stack of whole screens -- the reason is accurate. Adversarially, though, the SCENE-STRATEGY half needs no new protocol: once a pane_scaffold node exists, Emacs already owns its own screen stack in elisp and can author the top entries straight into the list/detail/extra slots (with a placeholder node for an unfilled detail), letting the Companion decide which panes fit. Only the node is load-bearing.
